chapters.title: Chapter 801: The Man Who Knows Too Much
paragraphs: Broken had already marked the location where he suspected the dragonkin were hiding.
At least now, he wouldn't have to aimlessly search the forest anymore.
With this, he could focus on gathering intel, uncovering the truth about the dragonkin, and figuring out what they were hiding.
But getting there would still take time.
So, as usual, he would proceed slowly, adjusting their exploration schedule to match their real-world responsibilities.
"Let's go, continue?" he said to SexyGrill, who had been fighting non-stop for hours now.
The girl nodded, about to climb back onto Polly when—
They both felt something.
A presence.
It came from behind them.
Then, a sharp yet controlled voice rang out.
"So you're the ones responsible!"
Broken immediately turned toward the source.
Above the man's head, a player name: Vallrick.
A figure cloaked in black stood before them, revealing only his face, illuminated faintly in the night. His brown hair was slightly unkempt, and despite the darkness, it was clear—he was a player.
Had he been part of the earlier group? Had he been left behind?
[SexyGrill]: "Kill him?"
[Broken]: "That's not even a real question."
Without hesitation, Broken drew his spear and began walking toward the man.
Vallrick didn't flinch. His voice remained cold, unwavering.
"The people I hired were slaughtered because of you."
His eyes narrowed.
"I know the truth. The dragonkin weren't after them..."
His gaze locked onto Broken.
"They were after you."
Unfortunately, Broken hadn't hidden his name, nor had SexyGrill. Which meant this player already knew exactly who they were.
Not that it mattered. Broken had no intention of explaining himself. It wouldn't make a difference.
But something caught Broken's attention.
This man... had said that the players from earlier were people he hired.
So he was their boss?
The real reason behind whatever mission had brought them to this forest?
Interesting.
But no matter what his intentions were, the fact remained—his entire group was gone. And now, he was alone.
Broken didn't care. He had zero interest in getting involved with this guy any further. Especially not when he suddenly appeared just to throw accusations like this.
His presence here was suspicious.
Was he here for revenge?
Did he actually think he could do something about what happened to his men?
It didn't matter.
Without a word, Broken moved.
He rushed forward, spear in hand, fully prepared to end this encounter before it dragged on.
"Wait, stop! Don't move!" the man shouted.
But Broken didn't stop.
"Wait! Stop! I know you—King Broken! Please don't attack!"
The moment Broken's spear was about to strike, the man shielded his face with his arms, flinching hard.
He knew who Broken was. Which, honestly, wasn't surprising.
After all, Broken had been in the spotlight quite a lot lately—from the Dissidia War to the Eternal Challenge.
But what was this guy trying to do? Was he planning to use his knowledge of Broken's identity to pressure him?
To threaten him?
To force him into a corner?
"I know you! Please, don't hurt me! I don't mean any harm!"
Broken's expression remained cold, unreadable.
"First." His voice was calm but firm. "I don't care about whatever business you had here. You came to me, and I don't like that."
"Second." His grip on the spear tightened. "I simply don't like you."
"Please, stop! Don't do this!"
Then, to Broken's surprise, the man dropped to his knees, raising both hands in surrender.
"Please, let me explain! Don't kill me! I'm not a threat to you!"
A notification popped up.
[Valrick Lv. 176 has sent you a friend request.]
Broken rejected it immediately.
"See? My level is low." Valrick spoke quickly, almost desperate. "I can't do anything to you. Just give me a chance to explain!"
Broken narrowed his eyes.
"Why should I?"
The man lifted both hands higher, showing that he had no weapons drawn.
"I know who you are. You're King Broken... a hero admired by so many."
His voice almost sounded convinced of his own words.
"I know you won't kill me."
Turns out, the man's attempt to flatter Broken had the opposite effect. Instead of calming him down, it only made him more irritated.
Hero admired by so many, my ass!
It was clear as day—this guy was trying to suck up just to save himself. And Broken hated it.
The man realized Broken wasn't buying it, so he kept talking, scrambling for anything that might spare his life.
"I'll pay you! Just don't kill me!"
Broken scoffed. "I don't need your money.
"Soul Stone! Level 220! Epic-grade!" the man blurted out.
At that moment, a crystal materialized in his hand, its surface shimmering faintly under the thin moonlight.
Epic-grade Soul Stone?
Broken paused for a second.
Now that was interesting.
The man caught onto his hesitation immediately.
"I have plenty of valuable things. I know you like collecting materials—I mean, we can make this mutually beneficial. Just hear me out."
Then, to prove his sincerity, he tossed the Soul Stone toward SexyGrill, making no attempt to hold onto it.
He just gave it up.
An Epic-grade Soul Stone—something that valuable, and he let it go so easily?
Who the hell was this guy? His level was low, but his resources clearly weren't.
"Now, please, I just want to talk." The man kept his hands up, still kneeling. "And I have an offer. That Soul Stone? It's yours."
Broken narrowed his eyes. "Why should I trust you?"
There had to be something bigger at stake. No one gave away an item like that unless they were desperate—or had something far more valuable they were after.
"How do I know you're not lying?"
The man nodded quickly. "Let me explain. And once you hear me out, you decide whether to believe me or not."
Broken held his position, his spear still raised, but he didn't strike—not yet.
Behind him, SexyGrill had already picked up the Soul Stone, rolling it over in her hands as she inspected it closely.
"Broken, it's real." Her voice carried a hint of surprise. "This is actually an Epic-grade Soul Stone. He's not lying."
Broken's gaze remained locked on the man before him.
Just who was this guy? A low-level player, yet wealthy enough to hire 40 mercenaries—who were now all dead at the hands of the dragonkin.
And what exactly was he looking for in a place like this?
He turned slightly toward SexyGrill. "Grill, do you recognize him? His name? His face?"
SexyGrill stepped closer, squinting as she gave the man a good, long look.
Then, with absolute certainty, she shrugged. "Nope."
Her tone was casual, completely unimpressed.
"Not even a little?"
"Not at all. His name and face don't ring a bell."
Broken nodded slowly, his attention shifting back to the kneeling man.
"Fine." His tone was cold and firm. "I'll let you explain. But if even a single word sounds like a lie to me—"
He tapped his spear against the ground, sending a faint crackle of energy through the dirt.
"I'll kill you."
The man's tense expression shifted instantly.
"Yes, sure! Of course!" he smiled, nodding quickly.
But then—he suddenly paused, his face shifting into realization.
"Wait! No!" His eyes widened in panic. "I mean—I'm not happy about the killing part! I'm just glad I got to talk!"

chapters.title: Chapter 802: Too Good to Trust
paragraphs: Broken kept his spear in hand, even though he had allowed the suspicious man to explain himself.
The man's eyes kept flicking toward the spear, his throat bobbing as he swallowed nervously.
"That spear..." he muttered, his voice uncertain. "It looks even more beautiful in person."
Broken didn't respond.
But from the corner of his eye, he saw SexyGrill smirking, clearly entertained for whatever reason. That girl really found amusement in the smallest things.
Then, the man finally spoke properly.

"I have a quest." He exhaled before continuing. "To kill a monster... Well, not exactly to kill. More like to deal damage to it. But—the requirement still says the monster must die. That's the quest."
Broken tilted his head slightly.
A kill quest requiring 40 players at level 200? That was definitely a raid monster.
But why the hell did a player under level 200 have a quest with this kind of difficulty?
The man noticed Broken's confusion and immediately continued.
"You're wondering why my quest is this difficult, aren't you? Well, I... can't tell you why. Not yet. But I'm not lying. I swear. I can even tell you exactly what kind of monster I'm hunting."
Broken let out a low breath, eyeing him carefully.
"A monster that required 40 people?" His voice was skeptical. "Surely, you're useless now. The people you hired are all dead."
The man winced but nodded. "Yeah... I know."
"Then why are you still here?"
"Because this quest is my priority." His voice was urgent, like he couldn't afford to let it go. "I can't just abandon it."
"And you expect me to believe that?" Broken arched a brow.
"I already gave you an Epic-grade Soul Stone!" The man insisted. "That alone should prove I'm not lying!"
"If anything," Broken muttered, "giving me something that valuable makes me even more suspicious."
The man sighed. "It was the only way to get you to listen. And now, at least you know my real reason for being here."
Broken inhaled deeply, already feeling exhausted by this conversation.
This guy was either insanely stubborn... or completely desperate.
Spending this much money and effort for a single quest?
This had to be something huge.
A Divine Blessing quest, maybe?
Or the chance to obtain a high-grade class?
Or maybe...
A legendary item.
After thinking it over, Broken finally made up his mind—he had no reason to keep talking to this guy.
"Now, you can leave." His tone was final. "We have no further business."
Without waiting for a response, he turned away.
But just as he did, the man scrambled forward on his knees, doing everything he could to keep Broken from walking away.
"Wait, King Broken! Listen to me!"
"Just 'Broken' is enough." Broken sighed, glancing over his shoulder. "I have things to do. And your business here is already over, isn't it? I'm letting you go."
"Wait! I have a proposal!"
Broken didn't bother responding.
He just wasn't interested.
This guy was too mysterious, too suspicious, and something about him just didn't sit right.
But seeing Broken's lack of interest, the man desperately lunged forward—grabbing onto Broken's right leg.
"Wait! King Broken, wait! Please, hear me out!"
"What now?" Broken exhaled, clearly exasperated. "I already let you live..."
The man looked up, eyes filled with desperation.
"Let me join you."
"No." Broken immediately shut him down.
"I'll pay you more! Let me come with you!"
"No."
"I'll give you more valuable items! Another Soul Stone! Money! Anything! Just let me come with you!"
The man tightened his grip around Broken's leg, physically stopping him from leaving.
For a solid minute, Broken tried to walk forward, but the man clung to his leg even harder, practically hugging it.
"Please, let me come with you!" The man pleaded desperately. "I won't bother you! I just need to follow you—wherever you go in this forest!"
Broken took a deep, frustrated breath.
Why the hell did he have to run into someone like this, in a place like this?
"Listen, man." His voice was strained with pure annoyance. "This forest is crawling with high-level monsters. Even we move carefully. We can't afford to bring you along."
He sighed sharply.
"And besides, you'd just be a burden. I won't protect you. I'm not a damn mercenary."
The man didn't hesitate.
"I can survive on my own."
Broken paused.
Because when he really thought about it...
That was true.
This guy had somehow survived—even after the dragonkin massacre wiped out his entire hired group.
Despite being alone, he had made it this far, following Broken without being detected, waiting for the right moment to reveal himself.
Which meant...
He wasn't completely useless.
Still, Broken wasn't convinced.
"And what exactly do you gain from following me?"
"A chance." The man answered without hesitation. "A chance to still complete my quest."
"You won't last."
"I will." The man insisted instantly.
Then, he finally let go of Broken's leg, stepping back without drawing any weapons.
A silent moment passed.
Then—
The man vanished.
Stealth skill.
SexyGrill raised an eyebrow, impressed despite herself.
A few seconds later, the man reappeared, his expression awkwardly confident.
"See?" He grinned sheepishly. "I can disappear anytime I need to. I can keep this up for a long time."
He gestured vaguely.
"I'll be fine. No one will detect me. Except... if we're in a party, of course. Then you'd see me on the map.
Broken considered the man's proposal, his mind running through the possibilities.
There was still something suspicious about him—his level, his quest, the fact that he was so insistent on following them.
But at the same time...
He didn't seem dangerous.
Just annoyingly persistent.
The real problem was that if Broken allowed him to tag along, it meant he couldn't summon Blaze.
He had kept the demon horse a secret, only revealing it to those he truly trusted.
With that in mind, he turned to SexyGrill for her thoughts.
The girl, who had been watching the whole thing with pure amusement, simply shrugged.
She grinned. "As long as he doesn't slow us down, I don't see a problem."
Broken sighed.
Honestly... he felt the same way.
But he still had his doubts.
"I can tell you more about myself if that'll make you feel better." The man quickly offered.
Broken didn't reply.
He simply turned around and started walking.
Not saying yes.
Not saying no.
SexyGrill smirked and followed after him.
Seeing this, the man's face lit up with excitement.
"Alright! I'll just take that as a yes!" he grinned and started following them. "Don't worry, I can keep up! I run fast! I won't slow you down!"
Broken ignored him completely as they made their way toward where Pawpaw had last been.
But then—
The man kept talking.
"By the way, you're so cool—especially in the Eternal Challenge, King Broken, hehe."
"Broken."
"Right, right! Just Broken!"
And he didn't stop.
For the entire walk, he kept running his mouth, talking about random things for no clear reason—just rambling endlessly.

"Like, your fight with Elincia? That was amazing! Seriously, I enjoyed every second of it! You both really looked like you were having fun, and I can't wait to see you fight Frostedge in the final! That's gonna be incredible—"
Broken exhaled sharply, his patience thinning.
"Can you shut up? Your voice is going to attract monsters."
The man perked up. "Oh! No worries! I can make my voice only audible to you guys!"
Broken stopped walking.
Turned his head slightly.
"That'll just make me the one getting angry."
The man froze.
Then let out a nervous laugh.
"Ah... okay. I'll shut up now."

Then let out a nervous laugh.
"Ah... okay.
I'll shut up now."

chapters.title: Chapter 803: Sounds Like Your Problem
paragraphs: Broken continued the journey, occasionally dealing with waves of monsters that appeared along the way.
As usual, he summoned his Gaia Beasts and quickly eliminated the creatures before they could attract even more.
Meanwhile, the man trailing them?
He stayed completely out of the fight, hiding in a corner, waiting until everything was over before reappearing like nothing happened.
He didn't even try to help.
Which was strange.
For someone with a decent level, he should at least be capable of fighting.
SexyGrill finally called him out.
"Hey, go fight the monsters too, if you want." She glanced at him. "You're not completely useless, right?"
The man grinned sheepishly.
"Ah, but if I attack, won't that mess up the experience point distribution?"
SexyGrill rolled her eyes.
"If you actually help and speed things up, that's better than doing nothing." She crossed her arms. "Unless, of course... you actually can't fight?"
The man waved his hands.
"No, no! I can fight!" He laughed awkwardly. "I'll help next time, hehe."
Broken didn't react.
At this point, he was already used to the guy's excuses.
But one thing was certain—even after telling him to be quiet, the man just couldn't stay silent. Every chance he got, he kept talking. And strangely enough, most of what he said was just... praise.
Constantly complimenting Broken, bringing up his achievements, as if he was trying to gain favor.
Unfortunately for him—
Broken wasn't the type to be swayed by flattery. So whether the guy was genuine or just sucking up...
It didn't matter.

As the journey continued, SexyGrill finally started engaging in conversation with Vallrick, making it so that he was no longer just talking to himself. At least now, the conversation wasn't entirely about flattering Broken.
"Hey, Vallrick," SexyGrill said casually. "What kind of monster are you hunting, anyway? Tell us."
Vallrick grinned sheepishly.
"Ah, well... hehe... are you two interested in helping me hunt it?"
SexyGrill raised an eyebrow, pretending to be shocked.
"Seriously? Are you joking?" She let out a small laugh. "There are only two of us. Meanwhile, you brought forty people. That would be suicide."
Vallrick quickly shook his head.
"But..." He leaned in slightly. "I'm sure the two of you are stronger than all forty of them combined."
His voice grew more enthusiastic.
"I mean, I saw you two fight in the Dissidia War! The way you weaved through the battlefield, dodging, striking—every movement was so precise, so perfect, it was like—"
Broken tuned him out completely. His voice blurred into background noise.
SexyGrill, however, cut him off. "Just tell me—what monster is it?"
Vallrick hesitated. "It's a high-grade monster.
"What grade?"
A pause.
Then, he briefly glanced at Broken before answering.
"It's a Legendary-grade monster."
Those words snapped Broken's attention back. His gaze sharpened immediately.
A Legendary-grade monster? That was a whole new level.
And in a place like this?
That meant the rewards would be massive.
For the first time since meeting Vallrick...
Broken was actually interested.
"Yes... it's a Legendary-grade monster." Vallrick nodded eagerly. "If you help me kill it, I'll give you a reward... and you can take all the loot for yourselves."
His tone turned even more desperate, yet hopeful.
"I just need to deal a single hit. That's all."
SexyGrill raised an eyebrow, now genuinely intrigued. She turned to him. "And where exactly is this monster?"
Vallrick hurried forward, pulling up his map system and marking a location.
Broken slowed his steps, finally coming to a stop as Vallrick circled an area on the map with his finger.
"The monster should be somewhere around here."
Broken studied the location.
It was conveniently along the path they were already taking—the same general area where Pawpaw had tracked the dragonkin.
A Legendary-grade monster...
It would definitely be a difficult fight. But even if he couldn't defeat it now, Broken was still curious. At the very least, he wanted to find it, test its strength, and gather information.
And if it proved too powerful...
He could always return later with a stronger team.
Vallrick watched Broken carefully, noticing how he seemed deep in thought.
Meanwhile, Broken discreetly gave an order to Pawpaw, instructing the demon cat to scout the area Vallrick had marked.
Almost instantly, Pawpaw retreated from where he had been observing the dragonkin and shifted his focus to the new target.
SexyGrill, still intrigued, tilted her head and smirked.
"That must be a high-rating quest, huh?" She glanced at Vallrick. "You got a mission to kill a Legendary-grade monster despite having such a tiny little level."
Vallrick laughed awkwardly.
"Ah, hehe... yes, I guess I'm lucky to have gotten this quest."
SexyGrill snorted.
"That's not luck, that's a curse." She crossed her arms. "You'd probably die just fighting normal monsters in this forest."
Vallrick chuckled nervously. "Hehe... yeah, I suppose that's true."
As they continued their journey, Broken switched to party chat, speaking privately with SexyGrill to keep Vallrick out of the conversation.
"Do you believe what he's saying, Broken?"
"I don't know. What do you think?"
"Hard to tell." SexyGrill hesitated. "But honestly, I don't see why he'd lie—not after going through all the effort just to get here.
"Still, we should stay cautious."
"Agreed."
She glanced slightly at Vallrick, who was still walking cheerfully ahead, unaware.
"His story doesn't completely make sense, so we should keep an eye on him."
Broken nodded slightly and responded.
"I already sent Pawpaw to scout for any potential high-level monster locations."
"Good call."
SexyGrill exhaled, then added,
"That said... if what he's saying is true, then a Legendary-grade monster being hidden in a place as remote as this actually makes a lot of sense. And if we find it, that's a huge opportunity."
"Yeah—if we can beat it."
They both knew that was the real challenge.
Then, after a few more hours of walking, with the night slowly fading into early morning—
Pawpaw finally sent a signal.
Broken immediately activated his Shared Sense skill.
Through Pawpaw's eyes, he saw—
An elevated part of the forest, where the trees were sparser than before. But that wasn't what caught his attention. Because right there in the middle of the clearing...
Was a massive cave entrance.
Big.
Unnaturally big.
Like something far larger than a normal monster could easily fit inside.
A cave that massive... There had to be something interesting inside.
But if Broken decided to check it out, it meant delaying his journey toward the dragonkin.
Was it worth it? They had no idea what could be waiting in there.
After a moment of thought, he made his decision. They'd check it out. After all, the cave wasn't far—and this was too big of a find to ignore.
By the time they arrived, the morning sunlight was barely starting to break through the dense forest canopy, casting faint golden rays over the misty ground.
And there it was.
The massive cave entrance.
The mysterious guy, Vallrick, was the first to rush ahead, staring in awe.
Then, he turned around with that same awkward grin.
"Are you guys planning to go inside? You know, to check what kind of monster is in there? Hehe."
SexyGrill smirked and casually crossed her arms.
"Why don't you go in first?"
Her tone was playfully mocking.
"You're the one who needs it, right?"

chapters.title: Chapter 804: That’s Not a Hot Spring, Is It?
paragraphs: Broken had no idea how deep this cave went or what might be lurking inside.
Considering the relentless waves of monsters they had already fought just getting here—he wasn't about to rush in blindly.
Pawpaw, the demon cat, was still lounging near the cave's entrance, casually licking his paws as if he had no care in the world.
Hah... still a cat, after all.
"Pawpaw, why didn't you check inside while you were here?"
The demon cat tilted his head up, his large, round eyes staring at Broken blankly.
"You didn't tell me to. So, I waited."
"Then go scan the cave now." Broken instructed. "And make sure you're not detected."
Pawpaw didn't bother responding, simply vanishing into the shadows before slipping into the cave's depths.
Vallrick, watching this, grinned and chuckled.
"That's an incredibly useful beast for scouting... you're so cool, Broken... hehe."
Broken ignored him completely and walked over to join SexyGrill near the cave's entrance.
They found a few large boulders nearby and sat down, taking the moment to finally eat something.
They had been fighting nonstop, and resting wasn't exactly an option with the sheer number of monsters attacking them.
Surprisingly, the area right outside the cave was completely clear. Not a single monster in sight.
Still, Broken hadn't redeployed Zepy, not wanting to risk the dragonkin spotting it again.
But honestly?

Traveling without Zepy was proving to be a pain. Without the flying golem's early warning detection, they had already fallen into multiple ambushes, attacked by monsters from completely unexpected angles.
Broken occasionally activated his Shared Sense Skill, viewing the cave through Pawpaw's eyes.
It was dark—completely suffocatingly dark—with only a few mana crystals scattered along the walls, casting faint, eerie glows in certain areas.
But what really caught his attention...
Were the shadows moving deep inside.
Massive shapes. Things coiled, shifting, breathing.
At one point, Pawpaw's vision briefly passed over a monstrous figure curled in the distance.
A huge snake—coiled so thickly that Broken couldn't even tell where its body ended.
He swallowed hard.
That thing was just a normal monster? Not even the Legendary-grade target they were supposed to be investigating? That alone made him wary.

Thankfully, Pawpaw was built for this. In his shadow form, the demon cat could move completely undetected. On top of that, he had full invisibility capabilities, meaning he could go anywhere without being seen.
Still, the scouting process took longer than expected.
Which was fine—it gave Broken and SexyGrill time to rest. Besides, analyzing the area was just as important as moving forward.

If they wanted to reach the dragonkin's location before nightfall, they could. But charging in blind wasn't smart. If they suddenly ran into a hostile dragonkin group, only to also be ambushed by high-level monsters like the ones in this cave...
It could be a complete disaster.
So right now?
Understanding all possible threats was just another strategy for survival.
Almost an hour later, Pawpaw finally sent a signal to Broken. Without hesitation, he activated Shared Sense again.
And—
He was not expecting what he saw. He had been ready for darkness—but instead, his vision was flooded with blazing red light.
What's that...?
Through Pawpaw's eyes, Broken saw a massive cave chamber—so huge that it almost didn't even feel like a cave anymore.
And at its center...
A huge pool of lava.
Thick, bubbling, and violently churning—as if something was being cooked beneath its surface.
A lava pool?
Before Broken could fully process it, the entire cavern trembled. The lava rippled violently in one area—
Like something enormous was stirring beneath it.
If this cave really did contain a high-level, Legendary-grade monster...
Then this had to be its lair.
From everything Pawpaw had scouted so far—this was by far the most unique location. It had to be hiding something.
Broken waited a little longer, still watching through Pawpaw's vision—
But nothing emerged.
Only the occasional tremor—subtle, yet powerful. Like whatever was inside the lava... was breathing.
For some reason, Broken felt the strong urge to see it for himself. If he could get a closer look, maybe he could analyze what kind of creature lived here.
Without wasting more time, he sent an order to Pawpaw.
"Come back."
And immediately, the demon cat turned and vanished into the shadows, making his way back toward the cave entrance.
"A massive lava pool?" SexyGrill repeated, her expression intrigued as Broken relayed Pawpaw's findings.

Vallrick, on the other hand, looked excited but remained completely silent. He was usually the type to talk non-stop, but the moment Broken spoke, he would always go quiet, listening intently like he was absorbing every word.
"Yeah. And I want to see what's inside." Broken continued. "I'll go in alone—with Pawpaw."
SexyGrill nodded without hesitation.
"That's probably the best move. I'll stay here with our mysterious human companion."
Vallrick simply grinned awkwardly—but still said nothing.
SexyGrill then glanced toward the cave, thoughtful.
"If there really is a monster inside that lava pool... and it's a high-grade one..."
She trailed off, leaving the rest unspoken.
Broken finished the thought for her. "The monsters scattered throughout the cave will already be tough enough to deal with." He exhaled. "Let alone the actual raid boss."
SexyGrill giggled.
"Exactly."
As soon as Pawpaw returned to the cave entrance, Broken stood up and stepped inside without hesitation.
At the same time, the demon cat leaped onto his shoulder, perching comfortably.
And then—
Shadow tendrils emerged, swirling around them, completely engulfing their bodies in darkness.
Within seconds—
They vanished.
Vallrick, who had been watching, let out a small, awkward laugh and turned to SexyGrill.
"He's so cool..."
SexyGrill giggled.
"You're worshipping him a little too much." She smirked. "He might start thinking you're just sucking up to him."
Vallrick scratched his head nervously but laughed anyway.
"He's just really that cool..."
Broken summoned Polly, swiftly mounting the spirit beast as they darted deeper into the cave.
With Pawpaw's invisibility skill completely cloaking them, they moved undetected.
And now, everything Broken had seen through Pawpaw's eyes earlier...
He was seeing firsthand.
High above, massive spiders the size of fully grown humans dangled from the cavern ceiling, their legs twitching slightly as if sensing movement.
On the ground, huge serpents lay hidden in the shadows, their scales blending into the darkness.
Further ahead, giant scorpions patrolled the rocky terrain, their deadly tails glowing faintly with venom.
Every single one of them was at least level 250.
Some were even as high as 270.
Damn.
Everything in this cave was insanely high-leveled.
Broken couldn't help but imagine what kind of loot he could get if he cleared this place out—
Weapons, armor, rare monster cores, or even monster soul stones.
But that could wait.
For now, his focus was the lava pool.
After a while, Polly's footsteps slowed as they entered the massive cavern chamber where the lava pool was located.
The blazing red glow from the molten magma illuminated Broken's face, though he remained hidden within the shadows.
His eyes widened as he took in the sight up close.
So massive.
Even after seeing it through Pawpaw's vision, experiencing it in person was something else entirely.
Then—
A deep, violent tremor shook the cave.
And in the next instant—
A massive explosion erupted from the center of the lava pool.
Molten rock shot high into the air, sending waves of lava surging outward, crashing toward the edges of the pool.

chapters.title: Chapter 805: A Raid Too Big to Handle
paragraphs: Broken darted backward, swiftly avoiding the crashing waves of molten lava as they slammed into the cave floor.
He couldn't afford to take damage. If he did, his invisibility would cancel—and that was the last thing he wanted right now.
The lava rippled violently for a few moments before settling again, though the entire cavern still trembled.
Chunks of rock broke loose, tumbling into the magma below, causing another series of tremors to shake through the chamber.
Carefully, Broken unsummoned Polly, leaving only himself and Pawpaw, still maintaining their invisible state.
Then, he hesitated.
Would external interference trigger the creature inside to emerge?
He was certain that something was lurking beneath that lava, but he couldn't afford to recklessly bait it out when he wasn't even prepared for what might appear.
After a brief moment of thought—
[Nature's Herald (Active Skill) Lv. 2 activated]
A summoning circle flickered to life, and moments later, a massive beast emerged beside him.
A dragon—a fusion of nature and shadow—materialized, its form twisting through the air.
The Elder Abyss Dragon Tree.
Broken remained hidden, watching as his summon soared toward the lava pool, circling above the molten surface.
He took a few steps further back, carefully adjusting his position.
The Abyss Dragon suddenly let out a powerful roar, then unleashed a barrage of magical blasts, striking the surface of the lava.
The reaction was immediate. The lava convulsed, surging violently.
And then—
Another explosion. A massive burst of magma shot into the air—
As if something beneath was rebelling against the disturbance.
As the next surge of magma erupted, something massive began to rise from the depths. It was fast—almost too fast—its entire form still engulfed in molten lava.
At first, the shape was unclear—just a towering mass of searing heat and molten rock.
But then—
A hand emerged. A massive, armored hand—formed from hardened lava, jagged and clawed, its molten veins glowing like cracks in volcanic stone.
Broken's eyes widened.
That wasn't just a beast. That was something else.
[Legendary-grade Fragment of the Abyssal Demon: Marquis Sabnock Lv. 280]
Broken's eyes widened as sheer awe washed over him.
A Legendary-grade monster. And its level—280.
Damn.
His entire body tensed at the sight. This was an insane discovery.
But more than that—
Fragment of the Abyssal Demon: Marquis Sabnock?
Wait.
That title.
It followed the same pattern as Named Demons—bearing a noble rank, like "Marquis."
Did that mean... this was only a part of a greater demon?
Was this just its hand?
Or...
Was there an entire body still hidden beneath the lava pool?
The massive hand suddenly lunged upward, moving so fast that the entire lava pool erupted violently, sending waves of molten rock crashing outward.
Before Broken could even blink, the hand shot forward—gripping the Elder Dragon.
A deafening roar echoed through the chamber—
And then—
The demon's grip tightened.
In an instant, the Elder Abyss Dragon was completely crushed, vanishing without a trace.
Broken swallowed hard. This thing was beyond powerful. Fighting it would be hell. Even without directly attacking, the lava pool alone was already a massive hazard—
Just being near it could burn through their health.
And actually killing this thing? Damn near impossible.
The demonic hand moved again—
This time, slamming its palm against the lava pool's surface.
The impact sent another massive surge of magma sky-high, an enormous wave of molten destruction rushing outward.
Broken's instincts screamed at him to move..
Without hesitation, he summoned Polly and leaped onto the spirit beast's back.
The moment Polly took off, Broken could see the tunnel entrance below—
Now completely flooded with lava.
If he had been even a second slower... He would've been swallowed whole.
Broken hovered in place, still seated on Polly, watching as the waves of molten lava slowly receded back into the lava pool.
Even after settling, the entire chamber was still burning hot—
The scorched ground left behind would deal continuous damage to anyone foolish enough to step on it.
And this was just from the monster existing. It hadn't even fought seriously yet. Just how terrifying would it be in actual combat?
He exhaled sharply.
"Gaia..." he murmured.

At his call, Gaia's form materialized, floating near Polly, her radiant energy swirling gently in the air. But as always, she said nothing—simply appearing, watching with her calm, unreadable expression.
Broken turned to her.
"What do you think... if we fought that thing?"
A brief silence.
Then, Gaia finally spoke, her tone as flat and monotone as ever.
"It would surely be... a pain in the ass."
Broken blinked. "Good word choice, Gaia."
Gaia remained unbothered, floating effortlessly.
"I do not believe our current strength is sufficient, Master. Even if you were to use the Golden Paragon."
Broken sighed, reluctantly agreeing with her assessment.
"Yeah... I figured as much."
But still. This thing was Legendary-grade and level 280.
If they could kill it...
The loot would be insane.
He'd need a solid strategy—probably an entire raid team if he wanted a chance at victory.
For now, though—
He needed to regroup.
With one last glance at the lava pool, Broken turned Polly around, soaring back toward
Where SexyGrill and Vallrick were still waiting.
"A Legendary-grade monster, level 280?!"
SexyGrill's reaction was explosive as Broken finished recounting what he had seen.
She immediately turned toward Vallrick, who was grinning smugly, clearly satisfied that he had finally proven he wasn't lying.
"So... turns out you're not as crazy as I thought." She crossed her arms. "I really thought you were just making things up."
Vallrick let out an awkward laugh.
"Hehe... yeah, well, thanks to Broken and SexyGrill, now I've finally confirmed where the monster actually is... hehe."
His eyes gleamed with excitement. "And I was wondering if you two might be interested in—"
Before he could finish, SexyGrill was already back to focusing on Broken.
"Any plan?" she asked. "Because from what you described, that thing isn't something we can take down just the two of us."
"Wait! Why only two?" Vallrick interjected. "I could help with—"
But neither of them were listening.
Broken nodded in agreement. "Yeah, it'd be a waste of time to fight it now."
That was all it took. Without another word, they turned and started walking away from the cave entrance, completely ignoring Vallrick.
"Wait, wait!" Vallrick quickly scrambled after them. "You're really just gonna leave?! You're not even gonna try killing it?!"
SexyGrill suddenly paused and glanced back at him.
"Vallrick, tell me—what kind of quest would require you to kill a monster like that?"
Vallrick stiffened. "That..."
"Not willing to share?" she tilted her head. "Okay."
She turned back around and kept walking.
"No, no, it's not that I don't want to tell you—" Vallrick hurried after them, flustered. "But if I do... does that mean you'll help kill it?"
Broken finally spoke, his tone completely indifferent.
"Go take a look for yourself."
Vallrick's steps faltered.
"If you think you can fight it, that's great." Broken shrugged. "Go ahead."
Broken and SexyGrill kept walking, not even looking back.
Without breaking his stride, Broken spoke. "We're moving on. You can stay or go back."
"Wait!" Vallrick hurried after them. "Didn't you already say I could come with you? I'll follow you guys anywhere!"
"You're still not trustworthy enough."
"I can prove myself! I'll give you my real-life address, my actual identity—whatever it takes!"
No response.
"I also want to join the Vensalor Guild."
That—
Made Broken stop.
For a second, he turned his head slightly, as if acknowledging the words.
Then, without saying anything—
He simply turned back around, and kept walking.
SexyGrill snickered at the reaction.
Vallrick, undeterred, kept pushing.
"Let me join the Vensalor Guild, please! Please—"

chapters.title: Chapter 806 806 - The Shattered Peaks
paragraphs: Broken continued his journey toward what he suspected to be the dragonkin's territory, still accompanied by SexyGrill—and, unfortunately, one uninvited guest who had somehow managed to tag along.
At the very least, the guy finally started pulling his weight in battles.
As it turned out, Vallrick was an Assassin-type player who fought using dual daggers. More than that, he had an exceptional skill—one that allowed him to vanish even while in battle mode.
It was... ridiculous.
With that ability, he could easily escape combat entirely, something that shouldn't have been possible under normal mechanics.
Maybe that was how he had survived in this nightmare of a forest, even when the forty players he hired had all been slaughtered by the dragonkin.
After what felt like endless traveling, they finally reached their destination, it was a clearing—
Just beyond the tree line, a towering cliffside stretched high into the sky, its jagged peaks blocking their view of whatever lay behind it.
And just as Broken had learned before, this vast area was completely protected by a barrier—an invisible domain covering the entire space.
A shimmering veil of magic stretched across the rocky expanse, preventing any unauthorized entry.

From where they stood, it was impossible to see what lay beyond the peaks. Some rock formations were packed tightly together, leaving only narrow gaps between them, while others jutted out at odd angles, obscuring the terrain beyond.
No visible movement.
But every now and then, a wyvern would soar through the sky, dipping low over the cliffs before disappearing behind the rock formations—
Only to fly off again moments later.
If the dragonkin truly lived here, this would be the perfect location for them. The barrier kept outsiders from entering, and the sheer height of the cliffs made it impossible to climb—
But for those who could fly? They could come and go as easily as they pleased.
That meant...

The dragonkin's home might not be on top of the cliffs at all. They could have built structures hanging off the rock face... Or even hollowed out the cliffs entirely to live inside the mountain itself.
Broken moved forward in stealth mode, shrouded by Pawpaw's invisibility, as he approached the barrier surrounding the cliffs. And the moment he got close, information appeared in front of him.
[The Shattered Peaks Veil - Lv. 300]
The Shattered Peaks? So that was the name of this place.
But... level 300?
There had to be someone among them with a level of 300 or even higher—someone powerful enough to maintain a barrier of this magnitude.

Broken let out a slow breath. He could usually force his way through barriers if they were around 100 levels higher than him, but this...? He wasn't even level 200 yet. There was no way he could breach it on his own.
...Unless he had external support to make it possible.
But... should he?
What if the dragonkin could sense intruders the moment someone entered? What if they had abilities that could detect invisibility?
He had come all this way to find them—to find the information about Ivana. If she had come here, this was the best place to start looking.
But how should he approach this?
Option one: He could just wave his hands and yell, hoping the dragonkin would come out.
"HEY, HAVE YOU SEEN THE DRAGON PRINCESS?"
...Yeah, no.
Or...
Option two: He could go in himself and gather information directly.
Broken ran through the options in his head again and again until he finally made up his mind.
He sent a message to SexyGrill through the party chat.
"I need your blessing."
"The barrier?"
"Yes. It's level 300."
SexyGrill chuckled when he returned and explained the situation.
"So your current level isn't enough to break through the barrier?"
She was grinning. Like she had just won a bet.
Great.
Of course she would enjoy learning something new about his abilities.
Well, it wasn't like he was trying to hide it. After all, they were already allies in the game—even if not officially.
The plan was simple. SexyGrill would use her blessing, temporarily boosting Broken's level by the difference between hers and his. That would be enough for him to slip through the barrier.
But, of course, once inside... he wouldn't be able to get back out the same way. SexyGrill would be stuck on the outside, and he would be trapped inside the domain.
Unless he used his Moonlight Dimension to teleport back to Dissidia Capital City or Slumdon Town. So, this was a one-way trip.
Whatever he found inside—whether it was information, allies, or enemies—he would have to handle it on his own.
And if things went south? His only option would be to retreat back to the South Continent.
Well... technically, there was another option. He could let the dragonkin kill him. That way, he would respawn in the nearest city. No lost experience points. No long trek back.
But...
There was a chance his items would drop. And hell no was he about to risk that. His inventory was full of expensive gear!
SexyGrill watched as Broken stepped forward. "So, you're really going through with this?"
Broken nodded. "Yeah. And once I'm inside, you two need to get far away from here."
"Wait... what?" Vallrick's eyes widened. "You're actually going in? But there's a barrier! How—?"
Broken only smirked.
Vallrick took a step back. "Damn, did I just overhear something I wasn't supposed to?"
SexyGrill chuckled. "Yeah, honestly, at this point, we should probably kill you."
"No! No! I swear, I won't say a word! You want proof? I'll even give you my real-life address if that makes you trust me!"
Ignoring his rambling, Broken focused on his plan. SexyGrill activated her blessing, and instantly, his level skyrocketed just enough to bypass the restriction.
Still in stealth mode, Broken took a deep breath and moved forward, Pawpaw close by his side. Hopefully, the dragonkin wouldn't notice someone slipping into their domain.
He glanced back once, spotting SexyGrill and Vallrick already making their exit. Good. They should be able to log out safely before anything unexpected happened.
Facing forward again, he focused on the shimmering barrier. The moment he stepped in, it felt like pushing through an invisible wall of dense air.
Pawpaw, who had momentarily stayed behind, vanished from sight... but the second Broken was fully inside—
Pawpaw reappeared right next to him.
It worked.
Without hesitation, the demon cat wrapped them both in stealth mode once more. Broken scanned his surroundings, eyes sharp for any sign of movement. Nothing. No alarms, no sudden disturbances.
He exhaled quietly.
After waiting a moment to ensure all was clear, he found a nearby spot for cover, crouching low as he summoned Polly. With their invisibility intact, the three of them moved as one.
"Let's go, Polly," he muttered. "Let's find out what this place is hiding."

Polly soared higher, gliding toward the towering cliffs that stretched into the clouds. The sheer size of the domain was staggering—just what kind of magic was powerful enough to set up a barrier this vast?
From this distance, it was still difficult to make out the details. But as they drew closer, moving in a wide arc around the area...
Broken finally saw what lay hidden between the massive peaks.

chapters.title: Chapter 807 807 - The Hidden City
paragraphs: Just as Broken had suspected, the dragonkin had built their structures clinging to the cliffside. Parts of the rock had clearly been carved out, creating solid foundations for wooden dwellings nestled against the mountains. A hidden city, suspended in the air.

The structures, though appearing simple, were masterfully arranged—firmly secured, their wooden beams blending seamlessly with the natural rock formations. And as he watched, figures moved between them.
Dragonkin.
They flew gracefully between the cliffs, carrying food, bundles of fruit, and supplies, moving as if this was nothing more than another peaceful day.
Broken urged Polly closer, wanting a better look. If he could get close enough, he might be able to analyze their levels. But from what he saw...
These weren't warriors preparing for battle. They were simply people, living their lives in peace.

Broken exhaled slowly. So far, so good. They were still invisible, and this was the perfect scenario to truly appreciate just how valuable Pawpaw's stealth ability was. Without it, he would've never been able to get this close.
Polly continued to glide silently, drawing nearer to the dragonkin settlement. Now, from this distance, Broken could see them clearly.

Their appearances were striking—beastkin-like features mixed with human traits. Though most of them had humanoid faces, parts of their bodies were covered in shimmering scales, and of course, each one bore a pair of powerful wings.

Unlike the battle-ready dragonkin he had encountered before, these ones wore normal clothing. No heavy armor, no visible weapons. It seemed not all dragonkin were focused on warfare—many of them were just living their daily lives.
When he analyzed their stats, the pattern became clear. The average level of the civilians here was around 150. Not weak, but not particularly powerful either.
Suddenly, his attention was drawn to four young dragonkin zipping through the air, chasing one another in a playful game.
And then—they flew straight toward Polly. But at the last second, Polly gave a strong flap of its wings, shifting just before the kids could collide.
The powerful gust from Polly's wings brushed against the smallest dragonkin at the back, making the child waver mid-air.
The kid stopped, hovering in place, looking confused.
"Hey, what's wrong?" one of the other children asked, pausing as well.
The little dragonkin blinked a few times, then shook his head before breaking into a laugh and resuming the chase.
Broken let out a silent breath of relief.

Broken observed everything carefully, taking in the structure of this hidden settlement. The kids were strong—level 50 to 80 already—but that made sense. Growing up in a place like this, they were probably used to hunting monsters from an early age.
But again, he wasn't here just to admire their way of life. He needed answers.
Anything that could lead him closer to understanding what the dragonkin were doing here. And to find the trace of Ivana.

Polly glided forward, heading toward the central area of the settlement. Massive chains stretched between the peaks, acting as bridges between different sections. The closer he got, the clearer he could see another group—a formation of dragonkin warriors mid-training.
They clashed in the air, moving at high speed, wielding swords and spears with precision. There were about a dozen of them, their levels hovering around 200.
Definitely fighters in training. Future warriors of their people.
Still... something about this place felt oddly peaceful.
Despite their hidden nature, despite their isolation, the dragonkin here didn't seem like they were living in fear. If anything, they had built a home—a real one.
For a second, Broken wondered. Wouldn't it be nice to live in a place like this? A secluded sanctuary where strong individuals could gather, train, and exist away from outside threats?
Then again, he already had a secret haven of his own—the Moonlight Dimension.
A floating island entirely to himself. A space where, in theory, he could welcome others... if only he had more keys to grant them entry.
Maybe one day, that would change.
Broken kept scanning the area, slowing Polly's flight as much as possible, taking in every single detail.
He was searching.
For her.
Ivana.
Down below, a group of dragonkin sat outside a house, drinking and laughing loudly.
"Hey! Get off your asses and train!" Another dragonkin flew over, shouting at them.
"For what? Hah! We live in peace!" one of them called back, laughing even harder.
The others joined in, raising their drinks, completely carefree.

Polly floated silently through the air, gliding past one house after another. Some had open balconies where dragonkin lounged with ease, speaking in quiet murmurs. Others kept their doors tightly shut, concealing whatever lay inside.
Should he start searching each house?
No. Not yet.
First, he needed to map everything out.
If simply observing wasn't enough to find any trace of Ivana, then he would take the next step—eavesdropping, listening for even the slightest mention of the Dragon Princess.
And if that still led nowhere?
Then he would remain here for as long as it took.
After some time spent quickly scanning the lower and middle areas of the Peaks, curiosity gnawed at him. What lay at the very top, right in the center?
From a glance, the houses in that area appeared more polished, their structures refined and well-maintained. The residents, too, seemed of a higher status—more powerful, more distinguished.
Polly soared upward, cutting through the sky as if reaching for the clouds. And the moment he broke through them, there it was... at the peak.
A vast open space stretched before him, its ground neatly paved with stone. At the center stood a massive structure—something akin to a castle's main grounds.
And in the courtyard below, around forty dragonkin stood in formation, clad in battle armor, their stances rigid and disciplined.

At the front of the ranks, a handful of dragonkin stood apart, and Broken immediately recognized one of them—one of the five warriors responsible for the brutal slaughter of forty players the day before.
They were here. The dragonkin warriors.
But why were they all assembled like this, fully armored and standing in perfect formation?
Were they preparing for war?
Or was this nothing more than a routine training exercise?

Broken paused, weighing his options. Was it really a good idea to fly in closer and eavesdrop on their conversation? The dragonkin below were already high-level, and those stationed here at the peak were undoubtedly even stronger.

If a battle broke out, his chances of survival were slim. Sure, he could wipe out a large portion of them with his massive area attacks, but the high-level dragonkin would never let him escape unscathed.
After considering his options once more, he made his decision. He instructed Polly to glide in slowly, hoping to catch snippets of their conversation without drawing attention.

Polly drifted toward the edge of the peak, moving with careful precision. As she neared, she landed almost soundlessly at the left side of the formation, keeping a fair distance from the group gathered at the center.
Broken held his breath, waiting to see if any of the dragonkin would react.
And then—
One of the dragonkin at the very front of the formation suddenly turned his head toward him.
Without hesitation, he spread his wings and shot into the air, flying straight for Broken!

chapters.title: Chapter 808 808 - The Hidden City’s Guardians
paragraphs: One of the dragonkin flew straight toward Broken, his wings beating slowly as he came to a stop right in front of him.
Had he been discovered?
But then, after a brief moment, the dragonkin simply glanced around in several directions without saying a word. His expression remained serious, his gaze sharp and focused.
This one... he had to be at least level 260.
Yet, after failing to find anything unusual, the dragonkin turned and flew back toward his formation.

Broken let out a small, quiet breath of relief. It seemed they hadn't actually noticed him—at least, not completely. Maybe they had heard the faint sound of Polly's wings or sensed something out of place.
After all, Pawpaw's Shadow Veil skill only concealed them from sight; their physical presence could still be detected, and any movement might leave an impact.
Fortunately, they had landed on a hard stone-paved surface. Their footsteps left no visible imprints, making it impossible for the dragonkin to spot any traces of their presence.
The dragonkin who had confronted him returned to their formation.
For the moment, Broken felt a sense of security, though he remained cautious.
He stayed in place, straining to pick up any useful information from their conversations.
Why were dozens of dragonkin warriors gathered in formation like this?
What exactly was their purpose here?
Then, one of their leaders finally spoke.
"The barrier is getting weaker because of that damn Demon Hand."

Broken sharpened his focus, his ears catching onto those words. It was a brief statement, but strangely, it lined up perfectly with the information he had just discovered about the high-grade monster lurking nearby.
The Demon Hand?
Of course, it wasn't surprising that the dragonkin were aware of such a powerful creature in the area. A monster of that level and grade wouldn't go unnoticed.
But... the barrier is getting weaker?
That meant the dragonkin were facing a real threat because of the Demon Hand's presence.
"The higher-ups are already considering launching a raid on the Demon Hand," the dragonkin continued.
"But it seems we have to deal with some other insignificant and disgusting problems first."
Insignificant and disgusting problems?
"That bastard high elf." The dragonkin's voice carried a sharp edge.
Demon Hand. Problems. High Elf.
Piece by piece, the puzzle in Broken's mind was coming together.
"We need to reinforce the outer defenses. Kill any players you come across—no questions asked."
Broken processed the information carefully. So the dragonkin were dealing with two major threats: the Demon Hand and the High Elf.
Did this mean the High Elf Queen was making a move in this area as well?
If she had also sent her people here, then she was likely searching for Ivana, just like he was.
Which also meant... she hadn't found Ivana yet.
But what did that say about Ivana's whereabouts? Was she not here after all? Or was it the opposite—was she here, and the dragonkin were deliberately keeping it a secret?
So far, not a single mention of the Dragon Princess had slipped from their lips. Either she truly wasn't here, or they were being extremely careful about keeping her existence hidden.
Broken knew one thing for sure—he needed to stay longer and gather more information.
But then, he tried to think from Ivana's perspective.
If she had discovered her true identity, and perhaps even regained memories of her past... what would be the most logical course of action for her?
Then again, logic alone wasn't enough to predict Ivana.
It wasn't that she acted without thought, but rather that her decisions weren't driven by logic alone. Her approach to the world was different.
Broken, for example, responded to situations head-on. He processed things logically, took action, then analyzed and adapted based on what he learned.
But Ivana?
She was someone who led with her emotions. Someone who placed the well-being of others above herself.
So, given everything she had learned about herself, about the truth—what would she do?
Would she seek revenge?
Seeing how Ivana had continued fighting for Dissidia and battling against the demons, it was clear—she hadn't lost herself. She still had full awareness of who she was. She hadn't changed.
And yet, without any warning, she suddenly left.
Not just him. Not just the battlefield. But everyone she knew.

She didn't even leave a single word of explanation for Fokil, despite how close they had always been. And that alone raised even more questions. Why would she disappear without saying anything, especially to someone she trusted that much?
The most logical explanation for her actions was that...
She didn't want her presence to bring harm to the people she cared about the most.
Which meant—most likely—she had chosen to distance herself. To disappear.
To hide.
But where?
But then again... there was no way Ivana hadn't expected Broken to come looking for her here, right?
Especially now that she knew the dragonkin played a major role in her past.
Long ago, the dragonkin had been slaughtered for trying to protect and hide her when she was just a child.
She had to know. She had to realize that Broken would come here—and that, most likely, the High Elf Queen would as well.
And if Ivana had predicted all of this... then wasn't it highly possible that she was still somewhere nearby?
That she wasn't distance herself—but instead, staying close, watching from the shadows, prepared to step in if the dragonkin were ever threatened and needed her help?
Because wouldn't that be exactly the kind of thing she would do? A girl who always put others before herself?
At the same time, Broken knew he needed to log out soon—the team battle in the Eternal Challenge was about to begin.
Luckily, it wouldn't be an issue. He could just slip into the Moonlight Dimension, log out from there, and return to this exact spot later without any trouble.
But just as he was about to do that, a message came through from Goldrich.
[Goldrich]: "Take your time, we can handle things for now... prioritize your current mission. No need to worry."
Even so... no.

Broken knew better than to completely set aside one responsibility for another. He had to balance his duty to his companions with his mission in the game. Both were important. And he had to find a way to handle them both.
Only then... without realizing it, Broken felt Pawpaw shift uncomfortably on his shoulder.
"They found us." The demon cat said.
His body tensed instantly.
At the same moment, their invisibility state had been completely canceled.
His focus had been locked onto the dragonkin troops in front of him, but—
A voice rang out from behind.
"Intruder! Kneel and surrender immediately!"
He had been discovered!
Turning slightly, he saw several dragonkin standing behind him.
His instincts kicked in—he braced himself for a fight.
At the same time, the dragonkin ahead also took action. In perfect unison, they launched into the air, spreading their wings wide as they closed in, surrounding him from all sides.
Their weapons were already drawn, their eyes locked onto him.
Damn it.
Since when?
Hadn't they been completely hidden this whole time?
"Submit now, or we will cut you down where you stand!"
"You dare trespass on sacred ground? Foolish. You will regret this."
"Insolent intruder! I'll make sure you regret ever stepping into this area!"

chapters.title: Chapter 809 809 - Words Won’t Work
paragraphs: How did the situation suddenly escalate like this, damn it.
Broken hadn't made any aggressive moves. He stood in the middle of the encirclement, his weapons still untouched.
This scenario... he had already considered the possibility of being caught. But it had happened too fast.
Still—at least he had managed to gather some valuable information before this. He had learned about the dragonkin's current situation, their problems, and their position in this whole conflict.
Then, the dragonkin began speaking amongst themselves.
"How did someone get in here?"
"Has the barrier weakened that much?"
"No, impossible. Only someone at level 300 or higher could enter."
"Even then, he shouldn't have been able to make it through. He's just a player."
They think I'm level 300?
Broken kept his expression unreadable.

This was something he could use. If they truly believed he had the power to bypass the barrier, he could play into that misunderstanding—because if it really came down to a fight, he wasn't sure he could make it out of here alive.
And honestly... he had no real desire for an all-out battle with them anyway.
After seeing what the dragonkin had already been through, he understood.
There were non-combatants here. Even children.
They had already suffered a massacre once before—that's why they had isolated themselves like this.
And that was exactly why he wasn't going to be the one to bring them another war.
"State your purpose for coming here. Who are you?"
"There's no need to drag this out. Let's just kill him like we did the other players."
"We can't. He already knows about this place. He's seen our secrets. If we kill him, he'll just come back—he's a player."
The dragonkin were arguing among themselves.
Broken remained silent, letting them debate for now. This was his chance—to find the right moment to interject and steer the conversation in his favor.
But what should he say first?
Some of the dragonkin descended to the ground, weapons drawn, their sharp tips pointed directly at him.
Pawpaw, still perched on his shoulder, whispered, "Should we kill them?"
Before Broken could respond, one of the dragonkin suddenly shouted in hysteria.
"He has a demon with him! He's an ally of the demons!"
Tch. This was getting worse.
Broken exhaled slowly, keeping his composure.
"Pawpaw, go for now. I'll handle this."
Without hesitation, Pawpaw let out a yawn—then vanished into thin air.
"Who are you? State your purpose here!" They barked at him once again.
Broken remained silent for a moment, carefully choosing his words. He needed to say this in the most precise way possible.
"I'm here to find the Dragon Princess."
The moment those words left his mouth, the dragonkin exchanged glances.
Of course, they could easily misinterpret his intentions. They might think he was a messenger from the High Elf Queen.
"He's a servant of the High Elves! This is war!" One of them shouted.
Broken held his ground. His voice remained calm, steady.
"I'm a friend of the Dragon Princess. Let me explain first—you can confirm the truth of my words yourselves. I'm not here to cause harm or chaos."
"We can't trust him. He's a player." One of them sneered.
Broken exhaled.

"I knew how to enter this place—that alone should prove I deserve a chance to explain. I am a friend of the Dragon Princess. I'm looking for her because she left, and I believe she came here. She once showed me a bracelet... a bracelet that pointed to this place."
"What proof do you have that your words can be trusted?!"
Broken simply lifted a hand and pointed above his head—at his name.
"I don't know if you keep up with what happens outside, but I, alongside Ivana—the Dragon Princess—was the one who defended Dissidia Kingdom from Duke Focalor, the Named Demon ranked 34!"
A murmur spread through the gathered dragonkin. Some exchanged uncertain glances.
"I've heard of that... Dissidia Kingdom in the South Continent was attacked by demons, and a major player guild played a key role in stopping the invasion."
Another dragonkin snapped back at him.
"Don't tell me you're from that guild?"
Broken remained calm as he gave his answer.
"I am Broken, leader of the Vensalor Guild... and the King Consort of Dissidia Kingdom."

Hearing Broken's explanation, the dragonkin once again exchanged glances—especially among the army. But the five dragonkin who appeared to be their leaders remained silent, their expressions unreadable.
It was clear. They weren't convinced.
Even with everything he had just told them, it wasn't enough to earn their trust or improve his position in this situation.
Damn it.
Did every problem in this world have to be solved through sheer force?
One of the dragonkin finally spoke, his tone cold and final.
"We have no ties to the Dragon Princess. If you believe she came here, you're gravely mistaken. We live here, free from the outside world. And you have disturbed that peace.
Broken exhaled slowly. "I can understand that."
"If you understand, then it's better for you to die here—so you never show yourself again."
If Broken chose to believe their words, then logically, he had no reason to stay here any longer.
But could he really trust that they knew nothing about Ivana's whereabouts?
Or... were they deliberately hiding the truth because they didn't want it to be uncovered?
Regardless, one thing was clear—leaving peacefully was not an option.
First, he couldn't exit the barrier directly. The only way out was to slip into the Moonlight Dimension and return to Dissidia Kingdom.
And second... if this situation escalated into a fight, he was still reluctant to cause unnecessary casualties among the dragonkin.
They weren't attacking him out of pure hostility. They were defending their home—protecting what little peace they had left. From their perspective, he was the intruder.
And no matter what, Broken still believed that at least some of them had ties to the dragonkin of the past.
If that was true... then somewhere among them, there had to be those who still remembered Ivana.
Or at the very least—had a reason to care about her.
"Enough talk. Kill him now."
Even after Broken had stated clear facts—that he was part of the team that defeated a Named Demon and that he was the King Consort of Dissidia Kingdom—the dragonkin showed no hesitation.
Not even a flicker of doubt.
They were confident—in their strength, in their defenses, in their home. Their response made that crystal clear.
At the same time, they had already begun preparing to strike.
And while Broken wouldn't be easily defeated, he knew that if he fought back seriously, he would end up killing many low-level dragonkin.
Damn it.
With a sharp motion, he summoned the Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear.
He had tried talking. He had tried reasoning.
But he wasn't the type to beg for mercy—or to plead for understanding.
"Let me make one thing clear." His voice was firm, unwavering. "I can fight. I can die and come back. But the dragonkin here— they won't."
This was his final warning.
"That is—if you can even land a hit on me." One of the dragonkin sneered. "You're outnumbered. You're outmatched. You're nothing here."
Broken exhaled slowly.
Fine.
Activating every defensive skill in his arsenal, he braced himself—preparing to unleash massive AOE attacks from his spear.

This scenario... he had already considered the possibility of being caught.

They think I'm level 300?

There were non-combatants here.

chapters.title: Chapter 810 810 - A Tribe’s Sacrifice
paragraphs: Broken had already activated all of his defensive skills, and Pawpaw had reappeared on his shoulder.
They were both ready.
This was about to become a full-scale battle.
No matter how hard Broken had tried to avoid fighting, the dragonkin had left him no choice. They weren't willing to settle this peacefully.
This fight was unavoidable.
With a swift motion, Broken equipped the Abyssal Crown and Flowing Tide Cape.
[Water Domain (Conditional Active Skill) activated.]
The cape flowed like liquid, releasing a surge of water that expanded into a domain, swallowing the dragonkin closest to him.
Their instincts kicked in— they immediately flew back, trying to put distance between themselves and the domain.
They weren't reckless. They were strong, but they weren't underestimating him.
They knew Broken was a melee fighter, so they were smartly shifting to long-range attacks to suppress him.
Not bad.
Even though they were powerful, they weren't just charging in blindly—they were using their numbers and his disadvantages against him.
But Broken wasn't just a close-range fighter. He had plenty of massive area attacks.
"Attack with everything you've got! Overwhelm him—full power, long-range barrage!" one of the dragonkin commanders ordered.
Broken spun his spear, preparing to counter.
Until—
"STOP THE ATTACK!"
A booming voice echoed from the distance.
Who was that?
Broken immediately scanned the area, searching for the source.
From one direction, the dragonkin army turned their heads.
And then, someone flew closer. A dragonkin— noticeably older than the others. His presence alone seemed to command instant respect. His name was Zephero.
One of the dragonkin turned toward him, speaking urgently.
"Elder Wing! He infiltrated our home—he knows too much. We can't let him live!"
Zephero landed on the ground, folding his wings, his gaze steady.
The other dragonkin hesitated, but slowly, they began lowering their weapons.
Zephero said. "This player was able to enter our barrier. That alone means he's no ordinary intruder. Let me speak with him for a moment."
"But Elder Wing, he's too strong! He's a threat to all of us!"
The elder dragonkin's eyes narrowed.
"From what I see... you didn't even give him the chance to speak."
The elder dragonkin now stood close—even stepping into Broken's Water Domain without hesitation.
Broken didn't lower his guard. Not yet. He hadn't deactivated his skill.
"You came here looking for the Dragon Princess?" the elder dragonkin—Zephero—asked.
Broken met his gaze, his voice firm.

"I suspected she came here. And yes, I am her ally. I've known her since before she even realized she was the Dragon Princess—back when she was still living among humans, raised by the ones who took her in as a child in Deadbay City, within Dissidia Kingdom."
He paused, then continued.
"It wasn't until the great war—when Dissidia Kingdom was attacked by demons—that her true self was revealed. That war... six Named Demons were involved."
Zephero nodded slowly.
"I have heard that story. In truth, we were both directly and indirectly affected by those events."
Broken noted the change in tone. The elder dragonkin wasn't hostile. Seeing this, Broken finally deactivated his Water Domain and dismissed his weapon.
Zephero sighed, folding his arms.

"Forgive us for acting too late. I know you trespassed into our home, and that is not a welcome action for a guest... but I also understand why you came. We are a protective people—perhaps too much so."
His gaze steadied on Broken.
"Let's talk properly. Let's get to know each other first."
Finally...
At least the escalation had been avoided.
A fight wasn't necessary.
Because at least one dragonkin among them had the clarity to think rationally.
Though, to be fair, the elder dragonkin's response was almost too welcoming, while the rest were far from friendly.
Well...
In the end, Broken was invited inside the mini-castle standing at the peak—a rare chance to speak directly with the elder.
The interior was open and spacious, with seating made entirely of solid stone.
Why?
Why did they choose to sit on such uncomfortable-looking rock chairs?
Broken took a seat, now facing Zephero—the Elder Wing, as the others had called him.
Was he their leader?
Zephero introduced himself, explaining that he was one of the elders of their tribe. While they had no official leader, he was someone the others looked up to.
It sounded strange, honestly. But seeing how the other dragonkin respected his words, it was safe to say that—unofficially—he was their leader.
In return, Broken shared his own background once more—King Consort of Dissidia Kingdom, husband of the current ruler, Queen Alora.
Zephero listened carefully, then spoke.

"I was there..." he said, his voice carrying the weight of old memories. "I was there when the High Elf Queen's forces came and attacked our tribe... It all started because our leader at the time chose to protect the Dragon Princess's egg. She was born here, in this very place."
Broken froze for a second.
Ivana had been saved by the dragonkin even before she was born?
Even when she was still an egg?
Zephero continued, his expression softening slightly.

"The Dragon Princess was a kind girl. She greeted everyone she met and cared deeply about even the smallest problems around her. She was our source of joy—playing with the children, laughing, and even showing interest in learning how to cook when she was little."
Broken listened intently. The way Ivana's journey began—it was both unexpected and fascinating.
But the real question was...
"At that time, did you know she was the Dragon Princess? And did she herself know?"
The Elder Wing responded without hesitation.
"Only the tribe leader knew the truth at first. Even the Dragon Princess herself was unaware of her own origins."
Broken tilted his head slightly.
So Ivana didn't know about her true identity from childhood?
Zephero continued, his voice carrying a new weight.
"The raid came from the High Elf Queen."
His tone sharpened, emphasizing every word.
"Five massive dragons, alongside the High Elf warriors, attacked and burned our tribe to the ground."
His voice slowed, as if every word he spoke carried the burden of the past.
"And that... was the moment most of us learned the real truth behind the slaughter."
Broken frowned slightly.
Something felt off.
This massacre—this tragedy—felt like it happened too long ago, far beyond what would align with Ivana's current age.
Unless...
Could it be that Ivana's real age was much older than she appeared?

"Most of us couldn't defend ourselves against the attack. The children, the younger ones... they were slaughtered effortlessly by just five massive dragons. While the High Elf warriors descended from the skies, striking from above and below, killing swiftly—giving us no chance to fight back."
Broken stayed silent, letting the Elder Wing finish his story.
But one question weighed on his mind.
"What about the Dragon Princess?"
Zephero lifted his gaze, his eyes locking onto Broken's.
"She was saved... by the Sloth Champion."
Wait—
"The Sloth Champion? Are you talking about King Elandorr? The past king of Dissidia Kingdom?"
Zephero nodded.

"There is no other Sloth Champion besides him. Yes, that King came and took the Dragon Princess away, while the rest of us were left behind—to be destroyed by the attack that nearly wiped us out completely."
