chapters.title: Chapter 811 811 - No One Can Stop Her
paragraphs: King Elandorr saved Ivana from the High Elf Queen's attack in the past.
That was how she ended up in the South Continent, in Dissidia Kingdom—where she ultimately fell into the hands of an ordinary woman in Deadbay City.
Broken replayed the scenario in his mind.
After all, it was King Elandorr who had given him the quest to find the Dragon Princess—Ivana.
But if Elandorr had known Ivana was in Deadbay City, then why didn't he just give a clearer clue?
Something as simple as "Find her in Deadbay City" would have saved so much time.
This ancestral Sloth Champion...
Sigh.
And then—
"So the Sloth Champion only saved the Dragon Princess... and did nothing to help the dragonkin?"
Broken voiced his thoughts aloud.
The Elder Wing simply shook his head, silent.
But in his gaze, there was something heavy—a weight of memories that had never faded.
What had he gone through to bring his people back from the brink of extinction, to rebuild this hidden tribe into what it was now?
They had completely cut themselves off from the outside world.
Even the smallest bits of information about them had barely reached beyond these peaks.
And yet, here they were—still training, still growing stronger, still living in isolation.
All while knowing the threat of another attack could come at any moment.
"Do you have any clue where the Dragon Princess is now?"
Broken voiced the question he was most desperate to get a real answer to.
The Elder Wing exhaled before responding.

"As one of us already told you... we have long been disconnected from anything related to the Dragon Princess. We isolated ourselves here, and the only reason we've been disturbed again... is because of her reappearance in Dissidia Kingdom."
Broken's eyes narrowed. "And..." he added, "you also said that the High Elf Queen might come here again."
Zepheros gave a slow nod.
"That is why we have strengthened our defenses—to prepare for that possibility... though the barrier has weakened due to a certain presence affecting it."
Broken stayed silent for a moment.
Zephero was being surprisingly open about this information, despite the fact that he shouldn't trust him yet.
"You must have already heard about it." Zephero finally spoke again.
Broken let out a quiet breath.
"I saw it. The Demon Hand."
His voice was steady.
"A Legendary-grade monster... with a dangerously high level."
At this point, Broken could just leave this place. It was clear—he wasn't going to find Ivana here. He could move on, try searching for her somewhere else...
But where?
He still had no other leads.
And then... there was this place.
If the High Elf Queen really did return and attacked this tribe again—what would happen to them?
Would he even care?
The barrier should be strong enough to hold, right?
Would it be his problem?
As Broken weighed his next move, his thoughts were suddenly interrupted by the elder wing's next words.
"The High Elf Queen is not someone you can fight..." the dragonkin said, his voice heavy.
"She is simply too powerful. If she merely sends an army to attack... perhaps we could hold out, depending on the strength of her forces. But if she herself decides to come—"
Zephero shook his head slowly.
"The High Elf Queen... she can do whatever she wants. If she wished, she could erase Yunatea with her power alone. She is unmatched—there is no one in Yunatea who can stand against her."
A silence settled between them before he continued.

"The other Ancestral Wielders of the Sin Blessings care little for this world. The rest have disappeared—like the Lust Champion, the Faery Queen... or the Sloth Champion, King Elandorr, who has been gone for years. And then there is the Gluttony Champion, King Bael, who isn't even in Yunatea anymore."
He let out a slow breath.
"If she comes here... it will be the end of us."
Was this... despair?
Had this elder dragonkin already accepted that there was no hope if the High Elf Queen arrived?
Before Broken could respond, the Elder Wing continued.

"This is a warning for you... if you choose to stand by the Dragon Princess, if you continue searching for her, then you must understand—one day, you will come face to face with the High Elf Queen. And anything that crosses her path... is destined for extinction."
Zephero paused for a moment, watching as Broken remained silent, absorbing his words.
Then, he spoke again.
"Have you met her before?"
"No..." Broken finally answered. "I never have."
The Elder Wing gave a slow nod before speaking again.
"So, I believe everything is clear now."
He fell silent once more.
Broken lifted his gaze, watching the elder's expression carefully.
"You may leave this place. And please—never return, nor bring anyone else here. Let us live our way and survive on our own terms."
Broken exhaled.
"You said that you're facing a threat from the High Elf Queen, right? You warned me not to cross paths with her... but are you certain you can handle it?"
Zephero met his eyes.
"We might stand a chance... if we can kill the Demon Hand."
Broken's brow furrowed.
"Then why haven't you done it? You have an entire force of high-level warriors."
The Elder Wing let out a slow breath before answering.
"That's the problem. We lack someone with enough water-element damage to weaken the demon. Without that, even if we attack, we risk massive casualties."
Water element?
Broken's mind immediately made the connection. His Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear was a water-element weapon. His main source of damage was exactly what they needed.
He could be the key to slaying this Legendary-grade monster.
And more than that—he had already planned to defeat the Demon Hand.
But even with his strength, he had been lacking the power to take it down alone.
So why not offer a deal?
If he and the dragonkin worked together, they could kill the monster with minimal risk. It would benefit both sides.
Wouldn't that be the smartest move?
Before Broken could even voice his thoughts, a dragonkin suddenly descended at high speed, landing near them with urgency.
"Elder Wing, we have visitors!" the dragonkin reported, his voice rushed.
Zephero immediately rose from his seat. "What did you say?"
The dragonkin, still bowing, spoke again—his voice trembling. "Th-the High Elf Queen's army... has arrived."
Broken's eyes widened.
A tense stillness filled the air, the weight of those words sinking into everyone present.
Without hesitation, Zephero spread his wings and took off, flying toward the castle grounds where the other dragonkin were already gathering.
Broken stood up as well, following swiftly behind.
By the time he reached the gathering point, the dragonkin forces were already in motion.
They took to the skies, weapons in hand, wings spread wide in readiness for battle.
But where were the enemies?
Broken searched the sky.
He couldn't see them yet.
Until—
A deep, thunderous wingbeat echoed through the sky, followed by a powerful roar.
Broken's head snapped upward.
From behind the clouds... a colossal figure emerged.
A massive dragon—its wings so powerful that they scattered the clouds with each beat.
And it wasn't alone.
More dragons appeared, soaring toward them from a distance.
The High Elf Queen's army had arrived.

sentences.text: King Elandorr saved Ivana from the High Elf Queen's attack in the past.
That was how she ended up in the South Continent, in Dissidia Kingdom—where she ultimately fell into the hands of an ordinary woman in Deadbay City.
Broken replayed the scenario in his mind.
After all, it was King Elandorr who had given him the quest to find the Dragon Princess—Ivana.
But if Elandorr had known Ivana was in Deadbay City, then why didn't he just give a clearer clue?
Something as simple as "Find her in Deadbay City" would have saved so much time.
This ancestral Sloth Champion...
Sigh.
And then—
"So the Sloth Champion only saved the Dragon Princess... and did nothing to help the dragonkin?"
Broken voiced his thoughts aloud.
The Elder Wing simply shook his head, silent.
But in his gaze, there was something heavy—a weight of memories that had never faded.
What had he gone through to bring his people back from the brink of extinction, to rebuild this hidden tribe into what it was now?
They had completely cut themselves off from the outside world.
Even the smallest bits of information about them had barely reached beyond these peaks.
And yet, here they were—still training, still growing stronger, still living in isolation.
All while knowing the threat of another attack could come at any moment.
"Do you have any clue where the Dragon Princess is now?"
Broken voiced the question he was most desperate to get a real answer to.
The Elder Wing exhaled before responding.
"As one of us already told you... we have long been disconnected from anything related to the Dragon Princess.
We isolated ourselves here, and the only reason we've been disturbed again... is because of her reappearance in Dissidia Kingdom."
Broken's eyes narrowed.
"And..." he added, "you also said that the High Elf Queen might come here again."
Zepheros gave a slow nod.
"That is why we have strengthened our defenses—to prepare for that possibility... though the barrier has weakened due to a certain presence affecting it."
Broken stayed silent for a moment.
Zephero was being surprisingly open about this information, despite the fact that he shouldn't trust him yet.
"You must have already heard about it." Zephero finally spoke again.
Broken let out a quiet breath.
"I saw it.
The Demon Hand."
His voice was steady.
"A Legendary-grade monster... with a dangerously high level."
At this point, Broken could just leave this place.
It was clear—he wasn't going to find Ivana here.
He could move on, try searching for her somewhere else...
But where?
He still had no other leads.
And then... there was this place.
If the High Elf Queen really did return and attacked this tribe again—what would happen to them?
Would he even care?
The barrier should be strong enough to hold, right?
Would it be his problem?
As Broken weighed his next move, his thoughts were suddenly interrupted by the elder wing's next words.
"The High Elf Queen is not someone you can fight..." the dragonkin said, his voice heavy.
"She is simply too powerful.
If she merely sends an army to attack... perhaps we could hold out, depending on the strength of her forces.
But if she herself decides to come—"
Zephero shook his head slowly.
"The High Elf Queen... she can do whatever she wants.
If she wished, she could erase Yunatea with her power alone.
She is unmatched—there is no one in Yunatea who can stand against her."
A silence settled between them before he continued.
"The other Ancestral Wielders of the Sin Blessings care little for this world.
The rest have disappeared—like the Lust Champion, the Faery Queen... or the Sloth Champion, King Elandorr, who has been gone for years.
And then there is the Gluttony Champion, King Bael, who isn't even in Yunatea anymore."
He let out a slow breath.
"If she comes here... it will be the end of us."
Was this... despair?
Had this elder dragonkin already accepted that there was no hope if the High Elf Queen arrived?
Before Broken could respond, the Elder Wing continued.
"This is a warning for you... if you choose to stand by the Dragon Princess, if you continue searching for her, then you must understand—one day, you will come face to face with the High Elf Queen.
And anything that crosses her path... is destined for extinction."
Zephero paused for a moment, watching as Broken remained silent, absorbing his words.
Then, he spoke again.
"Have you met her before?"
"No..." Broken finally answered.
"I never have."
The Elder Wing gave a slow nod before speaking again.
"So, I believe everything is clear now."
He fell silent once more.
Broken lifted his gaze, watching the elder's expression carefully.
"You may leave this place.
And please—never return, nor bring anyone else here.
Let us live our way and survive on our own terms."
Broken exhaled.
"You said that you're facing a threat from the High Elf Queen, right?
You warned me not to cross paths with her... but are you certain you can handle it?"
Zephero met his eyes.
"We might stand a chance... if we can kill the Demon Hand."
Broken's brow furrowed.
"Then why haven't you done it?
You have an entire force of high-level warriors."
The Elder Wing let out a slow breath before answering.
"That's the problem.
We lack someone with enough water-element damage to weaken the demon.
Without that, even if we attack, we risk massive casualties."
Water element?
Broken's mind immediately made the connection.
His Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear was a water-element weapon.
His main source of damage was exactly what they needed.
He could be the key to slaying this Legendary-grade monster.
And more than that—he had already planned to defeat the Demon Hand.
But even with his strength, he had been lacking the power to take it down alone.
So why not offer a deal?
If he and the dragonkin worked together, they could kill the monster with minimal risk.
It would benefit both sides.
Wouldn't that be the smartest move?
Before Broken could even voice his thoughts, a dragonkin suddenly descended at high speed, landing near them with urgency.
"Elder Wing, we have visitors!" the dragonkin reported, his voice rushed.
Zephero immediately rose from his seat.
"What did you say?"
The dragonkin, still bowing, spoke again—his voice trembling.
"Th-the High Elf Queen's army... has arrived."
Broken's eyes widened.
A tense stillness filled the air, the weight of those words sinking into everyone present.
Without hesitation, Zephero spread his wings and took off, flying toward the castle grounds where the other dragonkin were already gathering.
Broken stood up as well, following swiftly behind.
By the time he reached the gathering point, the dragonkin forces were already in motion.
They took to the skies, weapons in hand, wings spread wide in readiness for battle.
But where were the enemies?
Broken searched the sky.
He couldn't see them yet.
Until—
A deep, thunderous wingbeat echoed through the sky, followed by a powerful roar.
Broken's head snapped upward.
From behind the clouds... a colossal figure emerged.
A massive dragon—its wings so powerful that they scattered the clouds with each beat.
And it wasn't alone.
More dragons appeared, soaring toward them from a distance.
The High Elf Queen's army had arrived.

chapters.title: Chapter 812 812 - The Sky Burns
paragraphs: Broken stared up at the sky, his breath caught in his throat as the five massive dragons circled above, their enormous bodies weaving through the clouds.
It was...
A sight beyond anything he had ever witnessed.
The sheer scale of it was unbelievable.
He quickly analyzed their levels—
Each one was above level 300.
And the largest one? Level 320.
Oh, really...
The bitter irony of it all hit him like a punch to the gut.
Ivana—the Dragon Princess—was finally rising, finally fighting for her race.
Yet here was the High Elf Queen, commanding five of the strongest dragons to fight against her own kind.
She had come for Ivana.
And by sheer coincidence—or maybe fate—Broken was here to witness it.
But... could he even do anything against this level of power?
Before he could dwell on that thought, the dragons struck.
One of them slammed into the barrier, shaking the very air around them.
Another let out a massive burst of fire, the flames so intense that the temperature inside the barrier spiked instantly.
Dragonkin near the front lines recoiled—some, unable to withstand the sudden heat, lost their balance and plummeted toward the ground.
The five dragons roared, continuing their relentless assault, testing the strength of the barrier with each powerful strike.
Could it hold?
Because if it couldn't...
These dragons would wipe out the dragonkin once again—just as they had in the past.
And worst of all?
Ivana wasn't even here.
Broken watched as the dragonkin warriors hovered behind the barrier, preparing to defend themselves.
But it was obvious—they couldn't do anything.
Not against this.
Just five dragons... and they were already this powerful.
That was the reality of dragons.
That was why the High Elf Queen had wiped them out in the past—because she refused to let anything exist that was stronger than her.
And the ones she couldn't kill? She enslaved.
Like these five dragons. They weren't fighting of their own free will. They were controlled.
"We must protect our tribe!"
"We have to fight back!"
"Whatever you're looking for isn't here! We have no connection to the Dragon Princess!"
The dragonkin forces were panicking. Even if they stood their ground, even if they held their formation, they knew the truth.
If the barrier fell...
They would be wiped out.
And this wasn't even the full attack.
The High Elves hadn't arrived yet.
This was just the dragons.
Once the High Elf warriors landed—that would be the end.
Because High Elves weren't just any elves. They were the strongest of their kind. Even the Forest Elves—like Alora and her people—were nothing compared to them.
"You lowly dragonkin..."
The largest dragon spoke, its thunderous voice shaking the entire area.
Just the beat of its wings sent violent winds crashing into the barrier, strong enough to shake the ground beneath them.
Even the barrier itself couldn't fully block the force of its presence.
"Surrender the Dragon Princess, or what happened in the past will happen again today."
The dragon's voice boomed like an earthquake.
Zephero, the Elder Wing, immediately shouted back.
"We have already told you—the Dragon Princess is NOT here! There is nothing for you to find in this place! We severed our ties with the dragons long ago! Leave now, and let us live in peace!"
The massive dragon's eyes narrowed.
"You dare raise your voice at me, lowly dragonkin?!"
Its mouth opened wide, and with a single breath, it unleashed a torrent of fire.
The flames blazed down from the sky like a falling sun. The heat alone was overwhelming.
Even the high-level dragonkin warriors couldn't withstand it—some staggered in the air, struggling against the sheer force of the attack.
Broken swallowed hard.
Damn.
Even he wasn't sure if he could handle one of these dragons—and there were five.
"This weak barrier will not save you from the judgment of the Majestic High Elf Queen. You will be destroyed."
"Surrender the Dragon Princess."
Broken gritted his teeth.
And for a brief moment, a terrifying thought crossed his mind.
What if Ivana hadn't left the Dissidia Kingdom?
Would this have happened there instead?
The kingdom still hadn't fully recovered from the war against the demons. If an attack of this scale struck Dissidia now...
It would be reduced to nothing.
"Zephero!"
Broken shouted from below, trying to get the elder dragonkin's attention amidst the chaos.
Despite everything, Zephero heard him. The Elder Wing quickly turned, flying down toward Broken, landing just in front of him.
His face was tense.
He had lived through this nightmare before. And now, it was happening again.
"You should leave. This is no longer your problem. The Dragon Princess isn't here."
Zephero's voice was firm, but Broken wasn't here to argue about Ivana.
"Will the barrier hold against these dragons?" he asked instead.
The elder dragonkin fell silent.
Then, after a long pause, he finally answered.
Another pause.
So, it will hold?
Then, Zephero continued.
"Maybe for one day. But if these dragons keep attacking like this, I'm not sure how much longer the barrier—already weakened—will last."
Damn.
So the barrier really wouldn't last forever.

One thing was clear—whoever had cast this barrier in the first place had to be incredibly powerful. It had managed to withstand the test of time, and even now, it was still holding up against assaults from dragons this strong.
"Is this because of the Demon Hand?" Broken pressed.
Zephero, his face still tight with tension, gave a slow nod.
"If only we could kill that damn creature... but I fear we no longer have the time."
And surely, escaping was no longer an option. The dragons had them completely surrounded. If the dragonkin left the barrier now, they would be slaughtered instantly.
"If someone had a powerful water-element attack, how many of your dragonkin would it take to kill the Demon Hand?"
Zephero's gaze sharpened at Broken's question.
"Forty... I believe that would be enough. The chances of victory would still be slim, but at least not impossible—unlike without massive water-elemental damage."
"Forty..." Broken repeated. "Do you have forty fighters?"
Zephero took a slow breath.
"No... only about thirty dragonkin have the qualifications to take part in the raid."
Damn it.
Was this still possible?
If Broken truly intended to help these dragonkin defeat the Legendary-grade monster, this was the only way out of this mess.
And it was still a better option than waiting for the dragons to break through the barrier and slaughter them all.
"I have high water-elemental damage. I can fill the missing role. What if we try to take down the Demon Hand while we still have time?"
The Elder Wing fell silent, clearly weighing Broken's words. "What is your reason for offering this?"

Broken met his gaze without hesitation. "Your tribe is in danger. And all of this is happening because of the Dragon Princess. Yes, I am her ally. I am looking for her. And I know that if she were here, she wouldn't just stand by and let this happen."

He let that sink in before continuing. "But if you still have doubts... then let me put it simply. I will take all the loot from the monster. You get what you need—your barrier, restored and stronger than before. We take this chance, and if it works, it might just be enough to make those dragons leave for good."
Zephero was silent again, his expression unreadable.
Then, after a moment, he asked:
"How do we even reach the Demon Hand? We are surrounded on all sides."
Broken let a small smirk cross his lips.
"I have a way."

chapters.title: Chapter 813 813 - A Temporary Alliance
paragraphs: Surprisingly, the Elder Wing agreed to Broken's proposal rather easily.
Of course, some of the other dragonkin leaders still questioned the plan, but in the end, with Broken's already having a solid reputation, they had no real reason to refuse.
This was a life-or-death situation.
Whether they died fighting or died waiting—it didn't make much of a difference.
And besides—
Broken had already killed a Named Demon, ranked 34, and saved Dissidia Kingdom from destruction. That alone proved he was no ordinary person.

But even with the plan in motion, they couldn't just disappear all at once. If 30 of the strongest dragonkin suddenly vanished from the place, it would immediately alert the dragons outside the barrier.
So, they created a diversion.
They staged a scene where the dragonkin appeared to be frightened, retreating into their homes, hiding in fear of the assault.
And the plan worked.

The dragons outside the barrier seemed to have grown bored of their relentless assault. Their attacks were less frequent, and instead of continuing their full-force onslaught, they began to circle the skies above, their massive wings casting shadows over the land.
Instead, they resorted to hurling threats at the dragonkin below.
But everyone knew the truth. The dragonkin would never willingly lower the barrier. Not when they were being hunted. Because if the barrier fell, their fate was sealed. They would be wiped out.
One by one, Broken transported the dragonkin out of the barrier using Pawpaw's invisibility skill.
Since they could fly, the process didn't take long—though Pawpaw had to go back and forth multiple times between the cave and the main village.
Fortunately, despite being a lazy, moody demon cat, Pawpaw still listened to Broken's orders— albeit with his usual grumbling attitude.
But in the end—
Broken and all 30 dragonkin warriors reached the cavern where the Demon Hand awaited them.
As soon as they arrived, Pawpaw let out a grumble.
"Broken, give me the monster soul from this boss."
Broken let out a sigh, rubbing his temples before flicking the cat's forehead.
"A monster soul stone from a Legendary-grade monster? You're getting greedy. You know those aren't easy to come by."
Pawpaw huffed.
"Boring. I've done a lot. None of this would've happened without me. If you get a monster soul stone, I wanna eat it."
Broken shook his head.
"I'm sure a monster soul stone from something this strong would suit you... so yeah. If we manage to get one, you can have it."
"Ha! Haha!"
Pawpaw's eyes gleamed with excitement.
"I'm going to become an even stronger demon!
The Elder Wing, Zephero, stepped up beside Broken just as the Demon Hand began to emerge before them.
The massive, grotesque hand slammed its enormous palm against the lava pool, sending violent tremors throughout the entire cavern.
The very ground beneath them shook wildly, a force so overwhelming that any ordinary person would have already fled in terror.
This level of power...
It wasn't something just anyone could stand against.
But fortunately, the dragonkin could fly.
That gave them an advantage—allowing them to avoid the incoming waves of molten magma that the Demon Hand would inevitably hurl in every direction.
Zephero turned his gaze toward Broken.
"What's the plan, King Broken?"
Broken glanced at him, slightly surprised. It was the first time Zephero had addressed him as King. It felt strange... but not unfamiliar anymore.
Broken smirked slightly before answering. "We wait for another reinforcement to arrive."
Zephero gave a small nod.
Even if the chances of success were low, Broken could see it in the dragonkin's eyes. They weren't afraid. Every single warrior in that massive cavern stared ahead with unwavering resolve.
This raid—no matter what happened—
They were ready to give everything. Even their lives. Because this was their only chance to save their tribe. And they had no doubts about it.
They waited for a while until, finally, Pawpaw returned—this time, bringing another set of guests to their party.
Broken turned to see who had arrived. It was SexyGrill and SexyBloom.
"Hi, Broken~" SexyGrill greeted enthusiastically, waving her hand as cheerfully as ever.
SexyBloom, standing beside her, offered a simple smile. "Hi, brother."
SexyBloom had actually logged out in the nearest city to this area. And since she had the ability to fly, with Pawpaw's help, she was able to reach this place quickly and effortlessly.
Broken gave them a nod before asking, "How's the team battle for Eternal Challenge going so far?"
SexyBloom just grinned. "Let's hope we can finish this quickly. But honestly, I'm pretty sure Goldrich and the others are strong enough to handle it without you."
With that, they shifted focus back to their strategy and final preparations. Because SexyBloom's presence here wasn't just for extra firepower—
It was to give both Broken and SexyGrill the ability to fly.
Without flight, this battle would be near impossible.
After all, who in their right mind would try to approach a monster sitting in the middle of a massive lava pool?
They would be burned alive before they even got a chance to fight.
Broken then turned to SexyGrill.
"What about Vallrick? Have you contacted him?"
SexyGrill let out a small laugh at that. "Didn't expect you to care about our mysterious guy.

Broken exhaled. "Well, without him, we wouldn't have even known about this monster's existence. And for some reason, I get the feeling he knows a lot more than he's letting on. He's still suspicious."
SexyGrill nodded in agreement. "Yeah, well, he gave me his contact info. Even his real-world identity. That guy is a total pushover. But, I'm sure he'll be here soon."
The battle was finally ready to begin.
Broken stood at the very front, side by side with the Elder Wing, Zephero.
"Focus on attacking. I'll do my job while you handle the dragonkin on your end." Broken instructed.
Zephero gave a firm nod. "Understood."
At that moment, the cavern trembled violently.
The Demon Hand slammed its massive palm into the lava pool once again, sending a wave of molten lava surging toward the edges of the battlefield.
SexyGrill activated her blessing, and immediately—
Broken, SexyGrill, and SexyBloom began to levitate, their feet leaving the ground.
At the same time, Gaia's ethereal form manifested, floating effortlessly nearby.
The dragonkin warriors then took flight, their wings beating in unison, filling the massive cavern with a thunderous roar as they soared into position.
Broken summoned his full set of Invincible Paragon armor, his body glowing with power.
Then, in his hand, his Mythic-grade Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear appeared.
But first—he needed to soften up the battlefield.
He summoned his Golden Bow of Artemis.
This would be the first massive AoE water-element attack against their foe.
[Sniper's Focus (Active Skill) Lv. 6 Activated]
Above them, the ceiling of the cavern seemed to split open.
A colossal spear of water materialized high above, its form crackling with raw elemental power.
The dragonkin warriors gasped in awe, their eyes fixed on the weapon above.
And then—
The spear was released.
It descended at incredible speed, crashing into the lava pool below.
BOOM!
The entire area was suddenly flooded with a tidal wave of water, steam hissing as the lava was forcefully cooled.
At that exact moment—
The dragonkin attacked!

Fortunately, despite being a lazy, moody demon cat, Pawpaw still listened to Broken's orders— albeit with his usual grumbling attitude.
But in the end—
Broken and all 30 dragonkin warriors reached the cavern where the Demon Hand awaited them.
As soon as they arrived, Pawpaw let out a grumble.
"Broken, give me the monster soul from this boss."
Broken let out a sigh, rubbing his temples before flicking the cat's forehead.
"A monster soul stone from a Legendary-grade monster?
You're getting greedy.
You know those aren't easy to come by."
Pawpaw huffed.
"Boring.
I've done a lot.
None of this would've happened without me.
If you get a monster soul stone, I wanna eat it."
Broken shook his head.
"I'm sure a monster soul stone from something this strong would suit you... so yeah.
If we manage to get one, you can have it."
"Ha!
Haha!"
Pawpaw's eyes gleamed with excitement.
"I'm going to become an even stronger demon!
The Elder Wing, Zephero, stepped up beside Broken just as the Demon Hand began to emerge before them.
The massive, grotesque hand slammed its enormous palm against the lava pool, sending violent tremors throughout the entire cavern.
The very ground beneath them shook wildly, a force so overwhelming that any ordinary person would have already fled in terror.
This level of power...
It wasn't something just anyone could stand against.
But fortunately, the dragonkin could fly.
That gave them an advantage—allowing them to avoid the incoming waves of molten magma that the Demon Hand would inevitably hurl in every direction.
Zephero turned his gaze toward Broken.
"What's the plan, King Broken?"
Broken glanced at him, slightly surprised.
It was the first time Zephero had addressed him as King.
It felt strange... but not unfamiliar anymore.
Broken smirked slightly before answering.
"We wait for another reinforcement to arrive."
Zephero gave a small nod.
Even if the chances of success were low, Broken could see it in the dragonkin's eyes.
They weren't afraid.
Every single warrior in that massive cavern stared ahead with unwavering resolve.
This raid—no matter what happened—
They were ready to give everything.
Even their lives.
Because this was their only chance to save their tribe.
And they had no doubts about it.
They waited for a while until, finally, Pawpaw returned—this time, bringing another set of guests to their party.
Broken turned to see who had arrived.
It was SexyGrill and SexyBloom.
"Hi, Broken~" SexyGrill greeted enthusiastically, waving her hand as cheerfully as ever.
SexyBloom, standing beside her, offered a simple smile.
"Hi, brother."
SexyBloom had actually logged out in the nearest city to this area.
And since she had the ability to fly, with Pawpaw's help, she was able to reach this place quickly and effortlessly.
Broken gave them a nod before asking, "How's the team battle for Eternal Challenge going so far?"
SexyBloom just grinned.
"Let's hope we can finish this quickly.
But honestly, I'm pretty sure Goldrich and the others are strong enough to handle it without you."
With that, they shifted focus back to their strategy and final preparations.
Because SexyBloom's presence here wasn't just for extra firepower—
It was to give both Broken and SexyGrill the ability to fly.
Without flight, this battle would be near impossible.
After all, who in their right mind would try to approach a monster sitting in the middle of a massive lava pool?
They would be burned alive before they even got a chance to fight.
Broken then turned to SexyGrill.
"What about Vallrick?
Have you contacted him?"
SexyGrill let out a small laugh at that.
"Didn't expect you to care about our mysterious guy.
Broken exhaled.
"Well, without him, we wouldn't have even known about this monster's existence.
And for some reason, I get the feeling he knows a lot more than he's letting on.
He's still suspicious."
SexyGrill nodded in agreement.
"Yeah, well, he gave me his contact info.
Even his real-world identity.
That guy is a total pushover.
But, I'm sure he'll be here soon."
The battle was finally ready to begin.
Broken stood at the very front, side by side with the Elder Wing, Zephero.
"Focus on attacking.
I'll do my job while you handle the dragonkin on your end." Broken instructed.
Zephero gave a firm nod.
"Understood."
At that moment, the cavern trembled violently.
The Demon Hand slammed its massive palm into the lava pool once again, sending a wave of molten lava surging toward the edges of the battlefield.
SexyGrill activated her blessing, and immediately—
Broken, SexyGrill, and SexyBloom began to levitate, their feet leaving the ground.
At the same time, Gaia's ethereal form manifested, floating effortlessly nearby.
The dragonkin warriors then took flight, their wings beating in unison, filling the massive cavern with a thunderous roar as they soared into position.
Broken summoned his full set of Invincible Paragon armor, his body glowing with power.
Then, in his hand, his Mythic-grade Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear appeared.
But first—he needed to soften up the battlefield.
He summoned his Golden Bow of Artemis.
This would be the first massive AoE water-element attack against their foe.
[Sniper's Focus (Active Skill) Lv.
6 Activated]
Above them, the ceiling of the cavern seemed to split open.
A colossal spear of water materialized high above, its form crackling with raw elemental power.
The dragonkin warriors gasped in awe, their eyes fixed on the weapon above.
And then—
The spear was released.
It descended at incredible speed, crashing into the lava pool below.
BOOM!
The entire area was suddenly flooded with a tidal wave of water, steam hissing as the lava was forcefully cooled.
At that exact moment—
The dragonkin attacked!

chapters.title: Chapter 814 814 - Molten Chaos
paragraphs: [Legendary-grade Fragment of the Abyssal Demon: Marquis Sabnock Lv. 280]

Honestly, this was exactly as expected. The monster Broken was facing this time was a Legendary-grade. Even though its level didn't seem overwhelmingly high—comparable to some of the dragonkin in this raid—the fact that it was a raid monster made it exponentially stronger than a normal one. And on top of that, this was the first Legendary-grade raid monster Broken had ever attempted to fight.

The moment a massive surge of water, as if from the ocean itself, crashed down onto the lava pool dominating the area, the demon hand instantly reacted with fury. It clenched its palm tightly, seething with rage, and right after that, lava erupted from multiple spots, creating a massive tornado of molten fire within the cavern chamber.

Five towering tornadoes of lava spiraled violently around the demon hand, forming massive pillars that extended its attack range. Even before the attackers could get close, the sheer force of the tornadoes began pulling everything within the cave toward them.

However, the dragonkin seemed unfazed by the threat. They swiftly soared through the air, dodging with incredible speed before striking the demon hand and retreating again. Their attacks played out like insects avoiding a swatting hand—swift, precise, and always landing a hit before pulling back to avoid retaliation.
They were fearless. Even though death here wouldn't just mean defeat—it would mean the end, for real.

Broken immediately activated his water domain. Though the area it covered wasn't too large, he had to stay close enough to the monster for the water element to have any real effect on it. And yes, that meant he would be acting as a semi-tanker here, constantly positioned at the very front, dodging the magical attacks that the demon hand seemed capable of unleashing.

He dashed forward, weaving through the raging lava tornadoes, and the moment his domain fully enveloped the demon hand, he activated all his defensive skills. At the same time, he had to focus on avoiding the demon's attacks while maintaining his position as the dragonkin launched their strikes against the monster.

It was anything but easy—damn, even with four dragonkin fully dedicated to tanking, continuously pressing the demon hand from four different angles in a coordinated effort, Broken still had to do the same. That was the only way he could keep his water domain active, ensuring it remained locked onto the demon hand.

And this raid monster... it had an absurd variety of attacks. Just as the massive pillar-like tornadoes kept sweeping through the battlefield, the enormous hand suddenly began slamming its palm down repeatedly in different directions, sending massive waves of molten lava crashing against every surface within the cavern.
Just imagine fighting this thing without the ability to fly—it would be a guaranteed death sentence. This wasn't an opponent that could be taken down easily.
Only in moments like this did Broken truly realize that he needed a powerful shield!
He had never really thought of himself as someone who would need one. But if he had to stand on the frontline, unable to do much besides endure attacks, then he definitely needed a shield.

He had already made up his mind—his next masterpiece would be a shield! He needed it, especially since he still wasn't truly versatile. If he wanted to be a real tanker, someone who could take massive damage and hold the line while the rest of his team launched their attacks, then a shield was essential.
Thankfully, Broken had received a level boost from SexyGrill's blessing, allowing him to keep up with the sheer damage output of the demon hand—even though it was overwhelming.

He had also summoned Gaia, who hovered not far from him. While she couldn't take direct damage—since she didn't have a physical, damageable form—her healing abilities were more than enough to help Broken sustain himself in this intense raid.

At this point, the only summon Broken could bring out was the Elder Abyss Dragon Tree—simply because it was the only one that could fly. Any of his other Gaia Beasts would be instantly annihilated if summoned into this kind of environment.

And to make things even worse, the real challenge wasn't just the raid monster itself—it was the dragonkin army fighting alongside him. They were all... melee fighters! Like, seriously? Why? Why was there not a single archer or mage among them?
Seriously, dragonkin? Had they been isolated from the outside world for so long that they had no clue how a proper team composition was supposed to work?
Not even a healer. Well, technically, they did have healers—but their levels were too low. Instead of contributing to the battle, those healers would just become liabilities if they joined the fight.
No buffers. No support units. Every single one of them was a melee fighter, wielding either spears or greatswords. And yeah... most of them were spear users!
This whole setup was making Broken seriously stressed out.

To make things even worse, this Legendary-grade monster was an absolute pain in the ass for close-range fighters! Its skills dealt massive amounts of magic damage in the area surrounding its hand, making it a nightmare for melee combatants.

And as if the towering tornado pillars weren't enough, the massive demon hand was now playing with the lava pool—scooping up chunks of molten rock and hurling them randomly at the "insects" attacking it from every direction.
It didn't take long before the dragonkin began feeling the consequences of this terrible raid team setup.

Some of them suffered severe burns, their bodies scorched by the intense heat. Even though they kept attacking and dodging, their movements were no longer as swift as before. Still, they pushed forward—until disaster struck.
A massive splash of lava erupted, crashing down on a group of dragonkin. Two of them lost their balance instantly, spiraling out of control before plunging straight into the lava pool.
Broken let out a deep breath. There it is... the first casualties among the dragonkin.
Another fighter was hit directly, nearly getting sucked into one of the raging lava tornadoes—until SexyBloom dashed in, moving at lightning speed to grab him just in time.
His lower body was severely burned, the damage brutal. But SexyBloom wasted no time, quickly pulling him away and carrying him to a safer place.

"King Broken! We fight on! We will not falter!" Zephero, the Elder Wing, roared as he zipped between the demon's massive fingers, his greatsword slicing through the air in wide arcs. Each strike landed with force, carving into the demon hand before crashing against the surface of the lava pool.
None of them wavered. Not even for a second. The dragonkin remained completely focused, undeterred by the loss of three of their comrades.
But... was this battle truly worth it? Were they simply throwing their lives away in a fight that was leading them toward an inevitable death?

The demon hand seemed to be growing even more enraged. Instead of casually splashing molten lava in every direction like before, its massive fingers curled tightly into a fist. And as if all the devastating magic attacks it had already unleashed weren't enough...
Molten lava from the pool surged toward its clenched hand, flowing like liquid metal, spiraling upward until it solidified into a massive lava sword gripped tightly in its grasp.
Damn.
Round 2?

chapters.title: Chapter 815 815 - The Price of Pride
paragraphs: This was getting even more dangerous!
Broken kept darting between the demon hand's relentless attacks, now made even deadlier by that massive lava sword. The molten blade slashed wildly in all directions, its speed utterly insane!
Damn!
Broken was forced to retreat multiple times, barely avoiding strikes that were simply impossible to dodge.

And the moment his water domain lost its hold on the demon hand, things got even worse—the towering lava tornado pillars began spinning even faster, whipping across the battlefield with terrifying force.
This was bad!
Gritting his teeth, Broken forced himself forward, pushing through the chaos to reestablish his water domain on the target. But just as he closed in—
SLASH!

A single, direct hit landed on him. The impact sent Broken flying. Luckily, he was thrown upward instead of being blasted into the lava below. Twisting his body midair, he quickly regained control and dove straight back into the fight, refusing to back down.

Zephero was still going strong, his attacks relentless as he clashed directly with the demon hand. Their swords met in an earth-shaking impact, the sheer force of their collision reverberating through the entire cavern.
Because let's be real—this wasn't a normal raid. No group of players would ever attempt something like this, especially when their levels were so far below that of a Legendary-grade monster!
If it weren't for the fact that these dragonkin had no other choice, even Broken would have hesitated before taking on a raid this insane.
And then—
Another three dragonkin were struck down, their bodies flung mercilessly into the lava pool below!
One of them was even a tanker!
With their frontline dwindling fast, this battle was creeping dangerously close to the impossible.
Was it time for Broken to use Golden Paragon?
That would be a last resort. The moment its duration ended, he would be completely useless.
His eyes scanned the battlefield again. The demon hand was taking damage—there were visible wounds across its form. But the rate of destruction was far worse for the attackers.
At this pace... the dragonkin would be wiped out long before they could bring this thing down.
And then—Broken's attention was suddenly pulled away as a message from SexyGrill popped up.
What?! Vallrick?!
He whipped his head toward the entrance of the cavern chamber—and there he was.
The mysterious player stood at the entrance, looking like he had just arrived.
What the hell is he doing here?! This is the worst possible place for him!
"Broken! Why did you leave me behind?!" That incredibly annoying player shouted at the top of his lungs.
"Vallrick! Get the hell out of here! You won't last a second in this fight!" Broken yelled back, his voice sharp with urgency.
But Vallrick didn't budge. Instead, he shouted something even more absurd.
"Broken! I can do something! But I need to deal damage to that monster first!"
Before Broken could even process that ridiculous statement, another massive wave of lava surged through the battlefield—heading straight for Vallrick.
There was no way he could survive an attack like that.
This guy...!
It wasn't that Broken didn't want to invite him into the fight, but with his ridiculously low level, a single hit would be enough to instantly kill him.
But then—
Even as Broken tried to keep his focus on the demon hand, he saw it.
Vallrick dodged the incoming lava wave.
Not just that—he was now running along the cavern walls, his feet gripping the rock as if he had some kind of ability that allowed him to do it.
SexyGrill, still caught between the chaos of the battle, shouted at him. "Vallrick! Why the hell do you want to deal damage to this monster?!"
Vallrick's response was desperate but firm. "Please! Trust me! I can do something—I just need to land one attack! Just one hit, that's all I need! Someone, help me get close!"
Broken clenched his jaw. "Vallrick! This isn't a play! You're going to die the second it lands a hit on you!"

Molten lava rained wildly across the battlefield, splashing and scorching everything in its path. But Vallrick—kept running along the cavern walls, dodging every single one of them with almost infuriating ease. And, as expected, he just would not shut up.
"Someone, just get me close! I only need one hit!"
"Vallrick! Your damn quest means nothing if you die, you idiot! Get out of here, now!" SexyGrill yelled, still trying to drive him away.
But then—someone actually responded to him.
"Vallrick! I'll get you closer. How close do you need to be?!"
It was SexyBloom.
Vallrick, still sprinting along the wall, actually faltered for a second, shocked that someone was listening to him. "Just close enough for me to throw my dagger...!"
SexyBloom, who had been zipping through the battlefield, saving dragonkin from falling into the lava, suddenly turned toward Broken, seeking his approval.
Broken, still hyper-focused on the battle, barely spared a glance before replying in the party chat.
[Broken]: "Do it if you think it's the right call, Bloom."

SexyBloom nodded. Her face was tense, her expression sharp with determination. Without wasting another second, she maneuvered through the battlefield, weaving past the raging tornado pillars of lava, closing in on Vallrick.
And just as she reached him—
WHOOSH!
She grabbed the back of his armor and yanked him into the air—just before a massive splash of lava crashed down, narrowly missing them both.
SexyBloom had been keeping her distance for most of the battle—because, truthfully, she wasn't built to take heavy hits. What she was doing now was incredibly risky.

But at the same time, Broken couldn't do it himself—he had to stay focused on keeping the water domain applied to the demon hand. The dragonkin were all locked into their own roles, each one too busy to spare any attention elsewhere.
Up above, SexyBloom darted through the air, dragging Vallrick along as she dodged the pure chaos of the battlefield.
"King Broken, do you need us to assist in getting him closer?" The Elder Wing, Zephero, called out.
Broken's eyes flicked toward SexyBloom again.
What the hell was Vallrick even planning? He kept saying he needed to "deal damage"—but what kind of damage could possibly turn this battle around?
This guy was just making things even more complicated. And he hadn't even given a proper explanation for why this was so important.
But... if SexyBloom got taken out here, things would become even worse. Because if she died, the flying ability she had been lending to Broken and SexyGrill would disappear as well.
Damn it.
Broken clenched his jaw before finally giving his answer.
"Yes! Please assist!"
He had no choice.
And just like that, the dragonkin moved in, shielding both SexyBloom and Vallrick from incoming damage. Some of them even took severe injuries because of it.
Vallrick, you better do something useful. Because if he didn't—their sacrifices would be for nothing.

The battle had already reached a terrifying level of intensity. More and more fighters were sustaining critical injuries, and the number of casualties was climbing fast. Seven dragonkin had already lost their lives. Two more were badly wounded and had no choice but to retreat.
Broken gritted his teeth, keeping his focus locked on his role—until suddenly, a flash of light caught his attention from the other side of the battlefield.
And at that exact moment—
Vallrick threw his dagger.
The blade flew at incredible speed, slicing through the air before—
Vanishing.
The second it touched the demon hand's lava form, it just... disappeared.
What the hell?!
Vallrick?!
Broken's frustration was about to explode—until he noticed something.
And judging by the stunned reaction from the Elder Wing, he saw it too.
The monster's level...!
[...Marquis Sabnock Lv. 279]
[...Marquis Sabnock Lv. 278]
[...Marquis Sabnock Lv. 264]
[...Marquis Sabnock Lv. 260]
How the fuck?!
The monster's level dropped by 20?!
Because of Vallrick's attack?!
Broken could hardly believe it—but the numbers didn't lie.
That one dagger throw had somehow shaved twenty whole levels off the Legendary-grade monster.
What kind of bullshit broken skill is that?!
Broken's head snapped toward Vallrick, who was now being carried away from the battlefield by SexyBloom.
"What?! Are you a Divine Champion?"
His voice was almost drowned out by the chaos of battle, but the shock in his expression was unmistakable. SexyGrill, just as stunned, turned toward the mysterious player as well.
And then—
"Yes!" Vallrick shouted back, loud and clear. "I'm a Pride Champion... I can sacrifice my own levels to decrease an enemy's level too, hehehe."
The annoying bastard actually grinned like he was proud of himself.
Damn it!
Would it have killed him to just say this from the start instead of pulling that whole dramatic stunt?!

I can do something—I just need to land one attack!
Just one hit, that's all I need!
Someone, help me get close!"
Broken clenched his jaw.
"Vallrick!
This isn't a play!
You're going to die the second it lands a hit on you!"
Molten lava rained wildly across the battlefield, splashing and scorching everything in its path.
But Vallrick—kept running along the cavern walls, dodging every single one of them with almost infuriating ease.
And, as expected, he just would not shut up.
"Someone, just get me close!
I only need one hit!"
"Vallrick!
Your damn quest means nothing if you die, you idiot!
Get out of here, now!" SexyGrill yelled, still trying to drive him away.
But then—someone actually responded to him.
"Vallrick!
I'll get you closer.
How close do you need to be?!"
It was SexyBloom.
Vallrick, still sprinting along the wall, actually faltered for a second, shocked that someone was listening to him.
"Just close enough for me to throw my dagger...!"
SexyBloom, who had been zipping through the battlefield, saving dragonkin from falling into the lava, suddenly turned toward Broken, seeking his approval.
Broken, still hyper-focused on the battle, barely spared a glance before replying in the party chat.
[Broken]: "Do it if you think it's the right call, Bloom."
SexyBloom nodded.
Her face was tense, her expression sharp with determination.
Without wasting another second, she maneuvered through the battlefield, weaving past the raging tornado pillars of lava, closing in on Vallrick.
And just as she reached him—
WHOOSH!
She grabbed the back of his armor and yanked him into the air—just before a massive splash of lava crashed down, narrowly missing them both.
SexyBloom had been keeping her distance for most of the battle—because, truthfully, she wasn't built to take heavy hits.
What she was doing now was incredibly risky.
But at the same time, Broken couldn't do it himself—he had to stay focused on keeping the water domain applied to the demon hand.
The dragonkin were all locked into their own roles, each one too busy to spare any attention elsewhere.
Up above, SexyBloom darted through the air, dragging Vallrick along as she dodged the pure chaos of the battlefield.
"King Broken, do you need us to assist in getting him closer?" The Elder Wing, Zephero, called out.
Broken's eyes flicked toward SexyBloom again.
What the hell was Vallrick even planning?
He kept saying he needed to "deal damage"—but what kind of damage could possibly turn this battle around?
This guy was just making things even more complicated.
And he hadn't even given a proper explanation for why this was so important.
But... if SexyBloom got taken out here, things would become even worse.
Because if she died, the flying ability she had been lending to Broken and SexyGrill would disappear as well.
Damn it.
Broken clenched his jaw before finally giving his answer.
"Yes!
Please assist!"
He had no choice.
And just like that, the dragonkin moved in, shielding both SexyBloom and Vallrick from incoming damage.
Some of them even took severe injuries because of it.
Vallrick, you better do something useful.
Because if he didn't—their sacrifices would be for nothing.
The battle had already reached a terrifying level of intensity.
More and more fighters were sustaining critical injuries, and the number of casualties was climbing fast.
Seven dragonkin had already lost their lives.
Two more were badly wounded and had no choice but to retreat.
Broken gritted his teeth, keeping his focus locked on his role—until suddenly, a flash of light caught his attention from the other side of the battlefield.
And at that exact moment—
Vallrick threw his dagger.
The blade flew at incredible speed, slicing through the air before—
Vanishing.
The second it touched the demon hand's lava form, it just... disappeared.
What the hell?!
Vallrick?!
Broken's frustration was about to explode—until he noticed something.
And judging by the stunned reaction from the Elder Wing, he saw it too.
The monster's level...!
[...Marquis Sabnock Lv.
[...Marquis Sabnock Lv.
[...Marquis Sabnock Lv.
[...Marquis Sabnock Lv.
How the fuck?!
The monster's level dropped by 20?!
Because of Vallrick's attack?!
Broken could hardly believe it—but the numbers didn't lie.
That one dagger throw had somehow shaved twenty whole levels off the Legendary-grade monster.
What kind of bullshit broken skill is that?!
Broken's head snapped toward Vallrick, who was now being carried away from the battlefield by SexyBloom.
"What?!
Are you a Divine Champion?"
His voice was almost drowned out by the chaos of battle, but the shock in his expression was unmistakable.
SexyGrill, just as stunned, turned toward the mysterious player as well.
And then—
"Yes!" Vallrick shouted back, loud and clear.
"I'm a Pride Champion...
I can sacrifice my own levels to decrease an enemy's level too, hehehe."
The annoying bastard actually grinned like he was proud of himself.
Damn it!
Would it have killed him to just say this from the start instead of pulling that whole dramatic stunt?!

chapters.title: Chapter 816 816 - The Champion’s Sacrifice
paragraphs: 20 levels!
The monster they were facing had dropped a full 20 levels—a massive reduction. And the difference was immediate.

Its attack speed had slowed noticeably. The magic damage wasn't nearly as overwhelming as before. Even its massive lava sword—previously an unstoppable force—was now something the Elder Wing could hold his ground against.
This fight had suddenly become way more manageable.
But still...
Why stop at just 20?
"Vallrick! Just lower it even more while you're at it!" Broken shouted at the mysterious assassin, who was still running along the cave walls, dodging waves of lava crashing in all directions.
"Sorry, Broken... that's the max I can do! That cost me 40 of my own levels."
"Forty levels?!"
Broken's head snapped toward Vallrick, utterly stunned.
The Pride Champion just scratched the back of his head with a sheepish grin—but before he could say anything else, another lava wave nearly hit him, and he panicked, sprinting away again.
He sacrificed 40 levels... to drop the monster's level by 20?!
That was an insane trade-off!
Forty levels weren't something you could just farm overnight. That kind of progress could take a year—maybe even two years in Yunatea time.
Was he serious?
No wonder his level was ridiculously low for someone dealing with such an extreme quest.

But then again... maybe he had some kind of mechanism that let him regain levels faster. That would actually make sense. Because if he kept sacrificing his level like this without a way to recover it, he'd eventually drop to level 1 and be completely useless.
Still...
This ability was absolutely insane against high-level enemies.
If they'd had him back when they fought Focalor, just dropping that thing's level by 20 would have made the fight so much easier—maybe even reduced the number of casualties.
These Pride Champions were seriously just cheaters in disguise, huh? Their abilities were beyond broken.

The battle continued—but now, the dragonkin was suffering far less damage. They could hold their ground better, withstand the hits more effectively, and for the first time—Broken could finally shift his focus to attacking.
He unleashed a relentless barrage, chaining together every high-damage skill he had. Strike after strike, the fight tipped further in their favor—until finally...
CRASH!
The demon hand's massive sword shattered, crashing to the lava pool.
This was it.
Broken prepared his strongest single-target finishing move.
[⚔️ Abyssal Spear - Piercing Spear of the Abyss (Active Skill) activated]

The Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear shone brilliantly, its form enveloped in a swirling vortex of pure water energy. Every droplet hummed with power, condensing into a single, devastating lance of destruction.
Broken tightened his grip. This was it.
The air around it ruptured, a shockwave exploding outward as the colossal spear of abyssal water ripped through the battlefield—unstoppable.
The demon hand twitched—as if sensing its own doom—just before the spear collided.
BOOOOOOM!!!
The impact was instantaneous.
The spear pierced straight through, water surging into every crack and crevice of the molten flesh. The lava hissed and boiled, steam exploding outward in violent bursts.
The hand quivered—its massive fingers twitching in agony—before the flames in its core flickered... and died.
The once-molten surface darkened. Cracks splintered across its form, light bleeding through like veins about to rupture—
And then—
KRAKOOOOOOM!!!
The demon hand exploded.

Fragments of obsidian-like rock blasted outward, scattering across the battlefield like shattered remains of a fallen titan. The sheer force of the detonation sent a shockwave roaring through the cavern, causing the very walls to tremble.
And then—
For a few stunned moments, the dragonkin floats there, almost unable to process it.
The legendary raid was over.
They won!
The tension finally broke.
A wave of relief swept through the battlefield, and the dragonkin roared in victory, their voices echoing through the cavern.
It took a few moments for the aftermath of the battle to truly settle.
The demon hand was gone. The once-chaotic lava pool below had begun to stabilize, its surface no longer churning as violently as before—though it hadn't disappeared entirely.

The scattered lava that had spilled from the pool was slowly cooling and hardening, turning black and solid, especially after being relentlessly hammered by so much water elemental damage throughout the fight.
And then—
A soft glow shimmered in the air, right where the demon hand had once been.
The light rippled before suddenly shooting toward Broken, sinking into his body.
[You have obtained: Legendary-grade Fragment of the Abyssal Demon: Marquis Sabnock Monster Core Lv. 280]
A monster core. Not bad.
Wait... hold on—
[You have obtained: Legendary-grade Fragment of the Abyssal Demon: Marquis Sabnock Monster Core Lv. 280]
Two monster cores?!
Bountiful Harvest never failed to come in clutch at moments like this.
[You have obtained...]
[You have obtained...]
[You have obtained Legendary-grade...]
[You have obtained Legendary-grade...]
The loot notifications kept flooding in. Alongside the monster cores, Broken also received several rare materials from the fallen demon, along with—
A Legendary-grade item.
A bracelet. And a ring.
But Broken didn't check them just yet.
Not now.
He watched as the dragonkin slowly regrouped, checking on one another's condition. SexyBloom was moving between them, helping stabilize the injured and making sure no one was in critical danger.
Seeing this, Broken quickly moved toward the ones who were most severely wounded.

He still had enough Mana and Stamina left—he could do something for them. While he wasn't a full-fledged healer, he did have some healing skills, even if they weren't the kind that could be spammed endlessly.
He worked for as long as he could, restoring as much as possible—until his Mana finally ran dry, forcing him to step back and recover.
For now, the dragonkin needed time to rest and regain their strength.
Because soon, they had to return to their lands—to ensure the dragons and the looming threat of the High Elf Queen didn't escalate into something even worse.
And then—
Vallrick.
Standing there, grinning like a fool, right in the middle of them all.
The moment Broken turned toward him, Vallrick flashed his signature wide smirk.
"That was insanely close! Good thing we won, huh? Hehe."
Broken sighed, pinching the bridge of his nose. "Why didn't you tell us from the start?"
Vallrick tilted his head. "Tell you what?"
"That you can reduce a monster's level."
"I did tell you..." Vallrick replied, shrugging.
SexyGrill groaned, rubbing her temples. "Yes, but next time, answer the damn question clearly. You nearly got more people killed because of that nonsense."
"Ah, haha, okay, okay, sorry," Vallrick said, still grinning. "And thanks for helping me take that thing down! I'll just—"
But before he could finish, Broken had already turned away, resuming his conversation with the dragonkin, completely ignoring him.
SexyBloom giggled.
Seeing that he was being blatantly ignored, Vallrick turned his attention to her instead. "And... SexyBloom—"
"Bloom! Just Bloom, okay?" She cut him off sharply.
Vallrick blinked, then chuckled. "Ah, okay, hehe. Bloom, you're so cool... You are Broken's little sister, right?"
Bloom just rolled her eyes as they continued chatting, their conversation quickly turning into playful banter.
After that, the Elder Wing stepped forward, approaching Broken.
"King Broken, I believe we can return now."
Broken nodded. "It'll take as long as before."
The Elder Wing nodded in agreement. "The barrier has returned to normal."
Yes... but would the dragons retreat now that the barrier was no longer weakened?

chapters.title: Chapter 817 817 - A Threat from the Sky
paragraphs: "We need to get everyone back to the village," Broken said after summoning Pawpaw again.
The Demon Beast was sprawled lazily on the cave floor, resting his head on the ground while staring up at Broken.

During the battle, Pawpaw had fought alongside them, repeatedly tanking devastating attacks that would have otherwise injured several dragonkin. So, it was no surprise that he looked completely drained now.
It was clear that his stamina was nearly depleted—just a little more, and he'd probably need a long period of rest.
Even before this battle, Pawpaw had consumed a ton of resources—devouring monster cores, even absorbing soul stones he had found along the way.
This Demon Beast truly devoured anything in its path.
And yet... his progress was still slower than expected.
Despite everything he had eaten, he hadn't undergone any noticeable upgrades since the day he was born.
Was it because he was a Demon Beast? Was his growth different from that of a spirit?
After all, the same thing didn't happen for Blaze. Blaze had undergone a massive transformation after Broken had fed him high-quality materials.
As Broken thought about this, he sat down on the cave floor, pulling out the monster core he had just obtained from the demon hand.
A Legendary-grade Monster Core.
Its value was immeasurable.
If Broken crafted an item using this core, he was certain it would result in something incredible.
But... this wasn't just any monster core.
It came from a fragment of a demon.
A named demon, most likely.
Still, something was off. Even after killing this monster, Broken's kill count for named demons hadn't increased.
That meant... this wasn't a complete named demon. Somewhere out there, the rest of it still existed.
And if just the hand had been this powerful...
Then how strong was the demon's full form?
If its complete body was still out there, Broken had no doubt that it could be even stronger than Duke Focalor. That was a level of difficulty he couldn't even imagine facing anytime soon.
As he held out the legendary monster core, Pawpaw's ears twitched. The Demon Beast gazed at it with an unusual hesitation.
"You're giving it to me?" Pawpaw asked, sounding almost... reluctant.
That actually made Broken smirk. Because this was probably the first time Pawpaw had ever hesitated to devour something valuable.
In reality, Broken was pretty lucky to have gotten two monster cores from this Legendary-grade monster. That meant... he could keep one in reserve for whatever situation might call for it.
But—if this monster core actually gave Pawpaw a positive upgrade, he wouldn't mind giving him both.

After all, Pawpaw had already proven himself to be an invaluable companion beast in countless situations—especially with his unique ability to teleport between Broken and Alora, ensuring that Alora always had a reliable backup whenever she needed it.
So, the stronger Pawpaw became, the better it would be—not just for Broken, but for Alora as well.
With that thought, Broken placed the monster core on the ground, right near Pawpaw's head.
The demon cat sniffed at it curiously before finally opening his mouth and swallowing it whole.
For a moment, he just sat there, processing it—then let out a small burp.
"Good?" Broken asked.
Pawpaw licked his lips lazily. "Not bad."
That was good enough.
Now, Broken needed him focused.
Because they still had one last job to do.
There were 23 dragonkin and 4 players that needed to be transported back to the village. Which meant Pawpaw would have to teleport back and forth at least 16 times.
It wasn't that far of a distance—but the real danger was the risk of being discovered by the dragons or the High Elves, who might have already arrived at the battlefield.
They needed to move fast. Before more enemy forces showed up.
Broken was the last to be transported back to the dragonkin village.
He arrived at the highest peak of the village, where he could still see five dragons circling above the barrier.
This time, however, they weren't attacking. Instead, they simply hovered, watching.
Their presence was unnerving—but for now, they remained inactive.
Back inside the castle, Broken stayed with SexyGrill, SexyBloom, and Vallrick, all of them waiting in tense silence.
"Dragons that strong..." SexyGrill murmured, her gaze still locked on the massive creatures circling above. "I wonder what kind of loot we'd get if we killed them?"
She giggled softly, clearly amused by the dangerous thought.
Standing beside her, SexyBloom nudged her shoulder. "You do realize they're dragons, right? The same race as Ivana!"
"I know, I know..." SexyGrill shrugged. "But they're under the control of the High Elf Queen..."
Her expression darkened slightly as she continued. "Just what kind of power does she have to control dragons that strong?"
Broken finally spoke up, adding his own thoughts. "This is the first time five dragons like these have appeared in front of so many people."
He crossed his arms, his gaze sharp. "Because from what most people know—the dragons guarding the High Elf Queen's kingdom are different from these."
For a while, the dragonkin simply stood there, watching the dragons that had yet to make a move.
And then—
A thunderous roar echoed through the skies once more.
"I will burn this entire forest to the ground... if you do not hand over the Dragon Princess."
The threat was clear.
The dragons had given up on trying to destroy the barrier. But in doing so, they had shifted their strategy.
Their assault had, in a way, strengthened the barrier itself—but now the question remained...
How long would they have to wait until the dragons finally gave up?
Hours passed.
Broken remained inside the castle, seated in silence, making sure to stay out of sight from the dragons above. The others stayed with him, all waiting—watching.
During this time, he took a moment to check on the Eternal Challenge, where Goldrich and the team were still holding their ground.
Even though most of the other teams were trying to corner them, they were still winning.
This match would last for several more hours, and Broken realized that if he logged out now, he could still jump in and help secure their victory.
But...
Was this really the right time to log out?
He kept debating it over and over.
Until—
Something changed.
From his spot inside the castle, Broken suddenly noticed something strange.
The dragonkin outside were stirring, their heads turning upward.
"...What is it?" he murmured.
At that moment, SexyGrill, who had been monitoring the area through the flying golem, suddenly stiffened in shock before she stood up abruptly.
"Grill?" Broken glanced at her, sensing the tension in the air.
At the same time, SexyBloom stepped closer toward the open balcony, trying to see what had caught the dragonkin's attention.
Above the barrier.
Broken moved to stand beside her, Vallrick and SexyGrill following close behind.
And there—
They saw the figure.
A woman.
She floated above the barrier, her elegant white silk gown flowing like water, accentuated by simple yet regal light gold armor.
Her long silver hair cascaded down her back, swaying with the wind.
Even from this distance, they could see her presence was overwhelming.
Is that...?
For a moment, no one spoke.
It was as if the very reality of what they were seeing was too much to accept.
Some of the dragonkin even shook their heads in disbelief, refusing to believe their own eyes.
Until—
SexyGrill whispered the name.
"...Yvaeris Aranwyn."
"...No way." Vallrick exhaled, his voice barely above a breath.
Because the woman standing before them was none other than—
The High Elf Queen.
The Ancestral Wielder of the Pride Champion.
