There were 23 dragonkin and 4 players that needed to be transported back to the village.
Which meant Pawpaw would have to teleport back and forth at least 16 times.
It wasn't that far of a distance—but the real danger was the risk of being discovered by the dragons or the High Elves, who might have already arrived at the battlefield.
They needed to move fast.
Before more enemy forces showed up.
Broken was the last to be transported back to the dragonkin village.
He arrived at the highest peak of the village, where he could still see five dragons circling above the barrier.
This time, however, they weren't attacking.
Instead, they simply hovered, watching.
Their presence was unnerving—but for now, they remained inactive.
Back inside the castle, Broken stayed with SexyGrill, SexyBloom, and Vallrick, all of them waiting in tense silence.
"Dragons that strong..." SexyGrill murmured, her gaze still locked on the massive creatures circling above.
"I wonder what kind of loot we'd get if we killed them?"
She giggled softly, clearly amused by the dangerous thought.
Standing beside her, SexyBloom nudged her shoulder.
"You do realize they're dragons, right?
The same race as Ivana!"
"I know, I know..." SexyGrill shrugged.
"But they're under the control of the High Elf Queen..."
Her expression darkened slightly as she continued.
"Just what kind of power does she have to control dragons that strong?"
Broken finally spoke up, adding his own thoughts.
"This is the first time five dragons like these have appeared in front of so many people."
He crossed his arms, his gaze sharp.
"Because from what most people know—the dragons guarding the High Elf Queen's kingdom are different from these."
For a while, the dragonkin simply stood there, watching the dragons that had yet to make a move.
And then—
A thunderous roar echoed through the skies once more.
"I will burn this entire forest to the ground... if you do not hand over the Dragon Princess."
The threat was clear.
The dragons had given up on trying to destroy the barrier.
But in doing so, they had shifted their strategy.
Their assault had, in a way, strengthened the barrier itself—but now the question remained...
How long would they have to wait until the dragons finally gave up?
Hours passed.
Broken remained inside the castle, seated in silence, making sure to stay out of sight from the dragons above.
The others stayed with him, all waiting—watching.
During this time, he took a moment to check on the Eternal Challenge, where Goldrich and the team were still holding their ground.
Even though most of the other teams were trying to corner them, they were still winning.
This match would last for several more hours, and Broken realized that if he logged out now, he could still jump in and help secure their victory.
But...
Was this really the right time to log out?
He kept debating it over and over.
Until—
Something changed.
From his spot inside the castle, Broken suddenly noticed something strange.
The dragonkin outside were stirring, their heads turning upward.
"...What is it?" he murmured.
At that moment, SexyGrill, who had been monitoring the area through the flying golem, suddenly stiffened in shock before she stood up abruptly.
"Grill?" Broken glanced at her, sensing the tension in the air.
At the same time, SexyBloom stepped closer toward the open balcony, trying to see what had caught the dragonkin's attention.
Above the barrier.
Broken moved to stand beside her, Vallrick and SexyGrill following close behind.
And there—
They saw the figure.
A woman.
She floated above the barrier, her elegant white silk gown flowing like water, accentuated by simple yet regal light gold armor.
Her long silver hair cascaded down her back, swaying with the wind.
Even from this distance, they could see her presence was overwhelming.
Is that...?
For a moment, no one spoke.
It was as if the very reality of what they were seeing was too much to accept.
Some of the dragonkin even shook their heads in disbelief, refusing to believe their own eyes.
Until—
SexyGrill whispered the name.
"...Yvaeris Aranwyn."
"...No way." Vallrick exhaled, his voice barely above a breath.
Because the woman standing before them was none other than—
The High Elf Queen.
The Ancestral Wielder of the Pride Champion.

chapters.title: Chapter 818: The Queen's Absolute Rule
paragraphs: Broken stepped slowly out of the castle, his gaze immediately locking onto a figure of overwhelming power—feared across the entire surface of Yunatea—the High Elf Queen. A living legend, her name had echoed through the long history of this world, even before the arrival of the players.
She was the only Ancestral Wielder of the Sin Blessing still known to this day, a being said to possess the power to flatten the entire land of Yunatea if she so desired.
And now... that very figure stood right before them. Right before Broken.

This High Elf Queen was not just a feared ruler; she was also the greatest enemy of Ivana—the one he treasured most. And now, for the first time, she was truly standing before him, no longer a distant threat but a real presence.

From above, through the eyes of Zepy, the flying golem, Broken could see that High Elf forces had surrounded the entire area. Their numbers were impossible to determine, but they filled every corner of his vision.

Further up, soaring in the sky, dozens of wyverns flew in formation. They had approached from the distance and were now circling the area. Seated atop each wyvern were High Elves, their presence solidifying the weight of the situation.
Had the High Elf Queen truly come here with such an overwhelming force? Wasn't this excessive? What could have compelled her to take this so seriously?
Was it because the barrier had been restored? Or was it because the legendary-grade monster had been slain? Could she have been the one who planted that monster there in the first place?
If their victory over the raid monster was the reason for her arrival, then the most likely possibility was clear—she had indeed been the one behind the creature's presence all along.
"What should we do, Broken?" SexyGrill murmured softly.
"We stay... there's no way we can just leave in a situation like this."
"She..." SexyBloom added, her voice uncertain. "She really went this far just to find Ivana..."

Seriously... with such an extreme display of force from the Queen, it was clear this wasn't something she was taking lightly. She didn't just send an envoy. She had come here herself. That alone proved how important this was to her, how determined she was to see it through.
Besides, wasn't Ivana still in the midst of her awakening? Was she truly that much of a threat already? Enough for the Queen to take such drastic measures?

Or perhaps... The Queen saw something in Ivana's potential that made her a serious concern. Or maybe, after so long spent sitting idly in her palace, she had finally found something interesting enough to act upon.
Even the dragonkin stood frozen, unable to mask their shock at the catastrophe unfolding before them. Like... no matter what they did now, it felt as if destruction was inevitable.
But the barrier... there was still the barrier protecting this place, wasn't there?

And yet, at that very moment, the Queen, still hovering in the air, began to descend—slowly, deliberately—toward the barrier's surface. And then, all at once... a massive crack spread across it, like a fracture splitting through reality itself. The next second, the barrier shattered, scattering like shards of glass dissolving into the empty air.
The barrier... it had been destroyed in an instant, crushed under the sheer power of the Queen.
The dragonkin, no longer hesitating, raised their weapons, preparing themselves for the calamity that was about to begin.
[The absolute authority of the Ancestral Pride Champion does not allow anyone except a Divine Champion to wield their weapon.]
A notification appeared before everyone, and in an instant, the weapons held by the dragonkin slipped from their grasp, clattering onto the ground.
Absolute authority? What kind of terrifying ability was this, one that prevented anyone from even holding their own weapons?

At the same time, SexyBloom attempted to retrieve her weapon from her inventory, only to shake her head—she was affected by the rule as well. Everyone was... except for three individuals. Broken, SexyGrill, and Vallrick—the only Divine Champions present.
But why... Why were the Divine Champions the only exception? Was this merely a way for the Queen to flaunt how effortlessly she could impose any rule upon everything around her?

She surely knew there were Divine Champion players present here. And yet, she allowed the three of us to remain capable of fighting at full force. Was this some kind of twisted invitation? A chance for us to strike?
It felt like she was saying: I can do anything. I can win anything. I am untouchable. Just don't bother me. But if you dare to resist... I'll guarantee doom for all of you.
Slowly, the Queen descended from the sky, her movements as graceful as they were deliberate. Her feet touched the ground with effortless elegance, as if the very earth welcomed her presence.

The moment she stood upright, poised and commanding, the dragonkin erupted into murmurs of panic, their instincts at war with the reality before them. Yet, despite their fear, they held each other back.
The Elder Wing had already signaled them—no one was to resist.
Like... their weapons had already been stripped from them without a fight. What else could they possibly do in a moment like this?
The Queen stood there in silence, her gaze flat and unreadable, carrying the weight of absolute authority as she looked upon the dragonkin.
The Elder Wing, still holding the others back from making any reckless moves, once again repeated the same explanation. The very same thing he had told Broken before.
This was now the second time Broken had heard those words—almost identical—spoken by the dragonkin.
The Dragon Princess was not here. They no longer had any ties to her.
And yet... the Queen had still come.

It seemed Broken wasn't the only one doubting the dragonkin's claim. Even the great and all-powerful High Elf Queen didn't seem convinced. Otherwise, she wouldn't have gone through the trouble of coming here herself.

The tension in the air was thick—so thick that even the faintest whisper of the wind could be heard. The rapid, anxious heartbeats of the dragonkin filled the silence, each pulse amplifying the suffocating pressure weighing down on them.
The Queen, clearly unimpressed by their answer, tilted her head slightly upward, her gaze shifting toward her airborne forces. It was a silent command.
And then—without hesitation—all the wyverns, ridden by High Elves, dived downward in rapid streaks, cutting through the peaks as they sped toward the dragonkin's settlement.
At the same time, the High Elf soldiers stationed on the ground suddenly sprang into motion, rushing toward the dragonkin's homes with frightening speed.
If she couldn't confirm it directly, she wouldn't believe them.

Moments later, screams and desperate cries for help rang out from below. High Elves stormed through the dragonkin's dwellings, shoving, kicking, and striking down anyone who stood in their way. Resistance was futile—they were thrown aside, cut down, and overpowered without effort.
And in the midst of all of this, as Broken stood there, merely watching...
The Queen moved.
A single step.
Then, she turned—her piercing gaze locking onto him.
She was now looking straight at Broken, who stood at the entrance of the castle.
And for the first time since the tension had begun escalating to this extreme, Broken found himself meeting the eyes of the Queen.
This overwhelmingly powerful figure.
She surely knew about his connection to Ivana.

chapters.title: Chapter 819: Kneel Before Power
paragraphs: Yvaeris Aranwyn, the High Elf Queen, stared at Broken for a brief moment. And in that instant... he felt it. That gaze—calm and cold—carried an undeniable weight of authority. Even in just a fleeting glance, he could feel her presence pressing down on him.
Broken swallowed hard. But just as suddenly as she had looked at him, the Queen turned away, as if he were of no significance to her.
Around him, some of the dragonkin took flight, swiftly descending toward their settlement below, likely to check on the lower level members of their kind, offering aid where it was needed.
Yet, the Elder Wing remained.
He stood his ground, unmoving.
Like... with how composed and confident he seemed, was he truly certain that the Queen would be satisfied simply by confirming that what she sought wasn't here?
Or... would her wrath consume this place if Ivana was truly nowhere to be found?

The search carried out by the High Elves felt agonizingly long—dragging on for what seemed like an eternity. In reality, it had only been five minutes, yet their presence was everywhere. From the eyes of his flying golem, Broken could see the sheer scale of the chaos they were creating.
No one dared to fight back.

The dragonkin could only scream in frustration, helpless as their homes were ransacked. Children clung to their parents, wailing as their dwellings were torn apart—some structures simply crushed without a second thought.
Then, finally, one of the High Elves, mounted atop a wyvern, descended and knelt before the Queen.
The Queen turned her gaze toward him, silent.
"Your Majesty, we have searched every inch of this place. There is no sign of what we seek."
The Queen remained still, her expression unreadable. Then, slowly, she turned her eyes toward the dragonkin.
At that moment, the entire group tensed.
They stood there, frozen in place, drowning in uncertainty—unsure of what fate awaited them next.

No words were spoken. No sudden movements disrupted the heavy silence of that moment. The only signs of motion were the wyverns above, flapping their wings as they resumed their circling patterns in the sky.
[The absolute authority of the Ancestral Pride Champion applies 5000 weight to anyone in her presence.]
Another notification appeared before everyone.
And in an instant—like they had been crushed under an unbearable force—Vallrick and SexyBloom collapsed onto their knees.

Broken felt it too. The sheer weight pressing down on him was immense, threatening to drag him down. But since his weight capacity was still within manageable limits, he managed to stay on his feet—barely.

SexyGrill, however, wasn't as lucky. She soon followed, falling to her knees, struggling against the crushing pressure. Around them, several dragonkin also dropped to the ground, forced into submission. Those who remained standing could hardly move, their bodies trembling under the overwhelming force.
"Just damn..." Broken muttered under his breath.
If this person could impose any rule at will, then... How was anyone supposed to fight her? Just how far did this woman's power reach?
And then—before he even realized it—she was already standing before him!
Close.
So close that he could see the elegant curve of her neck, the way her skin gleamed under the dim light.
She was tall. Even among High Elves, who were naturally taller than humans, she stood out—imposing, towering over him.
Broken swallowed hard.
Slowly, he tilted his head up, careful not to meet her gaze directly.
Even without looking into her eyes, he could feel it.
Her presence. Her overwhelming strength. Her absolute authority.
Anyone who stood before this woman... forget about fighting her—they couldn't even lift their weapons.
Like, seriously—how could anyone possibly stand against her when they weren't even allowed to wield their weapons? How?
And the weight capacity? She could casually apply 5000 weight at will, forcing anyone to their knees as if they were nothing.

With that kind of pressure bearing down on him, even though Broken could still reach for his weapon, he knew the truth—he wouldn't be able to do anything to her. He would just stand there, utterly powerless.
"Pathetic..."
The Queen finally spoke.
Her voice.
It was beautiful—so beautiful that it was almost mesmerizing. Yet at the same time, it was chillingly cold, utterly devoid of emotion.
Broken stiffened, swallowing hard as the sound of her voice echoed in his ears.
"I like resistance," the Queen continued.
"Whoever stands before me to obstruct my goal..."
She paused.
And then—right in front of Broken—her lips shifted into the faintest hint of an expression.
"Make sure you provide resistance that is entertaining for me."
Broken swallowed again.
This woman—this Queen—was clearly telling him that he was insignificant. That right now, he was nothing to her.
And if he truly wanted to stand before Ivana and protect her... then he better make sure he was strong enough to be worth the Queen's time.
But just how long would it take for him to reach that level?
Even now, Broken didn't dare to inspect her stats.
That wasn't something you did in front of a figure this powerful.
The Queen turned away, and in an instant, she was already in the distance again.
Then—just like that—a massive crack split open beneath her feet.
And with a sudden burst of motion, she shot into the sky. A thunderous explosion erupted below, shaking the very ground as she ascended.
Now, she stood atop one of the great dragons.
There was a throne there—a seat meant specifically for her, resting upon the creature's back.
And like a dream... the catastrophe, the disaster, the looming doom that had gripped the entire area...
It all began to fade.
The dragons turned in unison, soaring toward a single direction before vanishing into the clouds.
The wyverns soon followed, their riders guiding them away without hesitation.
They were leaving?
They were really leaving?
[The absolute authority of the Ancestral Pride Champion has been lifted.]
The moment that notification appeared, the weight crushing everyone—both physically and mentally—was lifted all at once.
Breaths that had been held for what felt like an eternity were finally released.
Air filled their lungs again.
Relief washed over them like a long-awaited salvation.
Broken could see it—the sheer exhaustion and disbelief on the faces of the dragonkin.
Many of them had truly believed that their lives had ended the moment the Queen had arrived.
Vallrick let out a deep breath and said, "That was insanely intense... though I won't lie, I kinda freaked out seeing the Queen appear right in front of me. Hehe."
"Still, the Queen didn't acknowledge you, even though you're a Pride Champion, huh?" SexyGrill remarked.
"Well, I don't exactly have a superstar aura on my face, so I can't really blame her. Hehe." Vallrick chuckled.
"If only..." he continued. "If only I was allowed to join Vensalor... I'd definitely look way cooler right now."
SexyBloom gave him a side glance. "You sure have a lot of confidence, thinking you can join a top guild like Vensalor with your level that low."
"I can recover my level easily..." Vallrick smirked. "I'll prove my worth—way more than this!"
Some time later, the dragonkin finally began to move again.

The warriors quickly spread out, checking the area and assessing the damage they had sustained. No one knew the full extent of the destruction yet, but one thing was certain—the barrier had not returned.
Even after the Queen's departure, there was no sign of it being restored.
Had it been completely destroyed? Or was there still a chance for it to recover?
Soon, the Elder Wing approached Broken and answered the unspoken question weighing on his mind.
The barrier... was gone. Completely.
There was nothing left to protect the dragonkin from unwanted intruders. Anyone could now enter their territory freely, without resistance.
The Queen's arrival had completely changed their way of life.
But again... if the dragonkin couldn't restore the barrier, then who had set it up in the first place?
The Elder Wing offered no further explanation, and Broken didn't press the matter any further.
Now... even the High Elf Queen herself had confirmed that Ivana wasn't here.
So what was Broken supposed to do next?

"We owe you, King Broken," the Elder Wing said solemnly. "We will repay this debt however we can... Please, let us know if there is ever a way we can return the favor in the future. But for now, we must focus on rebuilding and recovering..."
Broken pushed aside the lingering questions swirling in his mind.
Because right now, it was time for him to log out.
A major update had just arrived from The Eternal Challenge.

And like a dream... the catastrophe, the disaster, the looming doom that had gripped the entire area...
It all began to fade.
The dragons turned in unison, soaring toward a single direction before vanishing into the clouds.
The wyverns soon followed, their riders guiding them away without hesitation.
They were leaving?
They were really leaving?
[The absolute authority of the Ancestral Pride Champion has been lifted.]
The moment that notification appeared, the weight crushing everyone—both physically and mentally—was lifted all at once.
Breaths that had been held for what felt like an eternity were finally released.
Air filled their lungs again.
Relief washed over them like a long-awaited salvation.
Broken could see it—the sheer exhaustion and disbelief on the faces of the dragonkin.
Many of them had truly believed that their lives had ended the moment the Queen had arrived.
Vallrick let out a deep breath and said, "That was insanely intense... though I won't lie, I kinda freaked out seeing the Queen appear right in front of me.
Hehe."
"Still, the Queen didn't acknowledge you, even though you're a Pride Champion, huh?" SexyGrill remarked.
"Well, I don't exactly have a superstar aura on my face, so I can't really blame her.
Hehe." Vallrick chuckled.
"If only..." he continued.
"If only I was allowed to join Vensalor...
I'd definitely look way cooler right now."
SexyBloom gave him a side glance.
"You sure have a lot of confidence, thinking you can join a top guild like Vensalor with your level that low."
"I can recover my level easily..." Vallrick smirked.
"I'll prove my worth—way more than this!"
Some time later, the dragonkin finally began to move again.
The warriors quickly spread out, checking the area and assessing the damage they had sustained.
No one knew the full extent of the destruction yet, but one thing was certain—the barrier had not returned.
Even after the Queen's departure, there was no sign of it being restored.
Had it been completely destroyed?
Or was there still a chance for it to recover?
Soon, the Elder Wing approached Broken and answered the unspoken question weighing on his mind.
The barrier... was gone.
Completely.
There was nothing left to protect the dragonkin from unwanted intruders.
Anyone could now enter their territory freely, without resistance.
The Queen's arrival had completely changed their way of life.
But again... if the dragonkin couldn't restore the barrier, then who had set it up in the first place?
The Elder Wing offered no further explanation, and Broken didn't press the matter any further.
Now... even the High Elf Queen herself had confirmed that Ivana wasn't here.
So what was Broken supposed to do next?
"We owe you, King Broken," the Elder Wing said solemnly.
"We will repay this debt however we can...
Please, let us know if there is ever a way we can return the favor in the future.
But for now, we must focus on rebuilding and recovering..."
Broken pushed aside the lingering questions swirling in his mind.
Because right now, it was time for him to log out.
A major update had just arrived from The Eternal Challenge.

chapters.title: Chapter 820: The Roar of the Stadium
paragraphs: Leon stepped out of the capsule device and glanced toward the center of the home bus. There, a brown-haired woman sat with her legs crossed, engrossed in whatever she was reading on her device.
He walked over to Freya, who waved at him. "Hey... got enough sleep?"
"How was the match, Freya?"
"Uhm... I'm not sure you'll make it even if you rush..." she replied with a small smile.
Without wasting another second, Leon stepped out of the home bus, with Freya following closely beside him, ready to recount everything that had happened during the match.

"It seems your team's reputation is so massive that plenty of teams were eager to take down Destroyer right from the start," Freya explained as they walked side by side toward the stadium where the match had taken place.

"But since Charmelyn managed to eliminate key players from the opposing side, their formation fell apart. That gave Goldrich and Starfall the opening they needed to corner the enemy and secure the overall victory."
Freya hesitated for a moment before continuing, "However... I think our other team..."
Leon turned to her. "Team Elincia?"
"Yes..." Freya nodded. "Elincia and Maylock..."
Leon chuckled. "I guess everyone was too focused on Destroyer and forgot that the most brilliant player in Vensalor is also in this competition."
They rushed into the stadium just as a loud cheer erupted from the crowd. At the same time, the players had already stepped out of the capsule devices, and the winners of the match were clear.
As Freya had predicted, Team Elincia claimed first place, while Team Destroyer secured second.
At that moment, the cameras zoomed in on Leon from afar, his face appearing on the big screen, triggering another wave of cheers from the audience.
Why did they always have to put the camera on him? These people really loved stirring up drama and hyping up the crowd.
With the trophy ceremony wrapped up, Leon quickly regrouped with his team. On the same day, the final match for the raid race was also set to take place.
That meant he had completely skipped the team battles—but no worries. At the very least, this victory gave Elincia and her team a well-earned reward. It was still a win for the Vensalor Guild.
And even without Leon in this match, Team Destroyer still managed to secure second place.
Were there just too many top-tier players not participating in this first-year competition? Leon couldn't help but wonder. After all, so many Vensalor players had been dominating different matches.

Ronald and Freya went over the full lineup of teams they would be facing in the final match of the raid race, pointing out that several Divine Champions were among the competitors. And just like in the previous match, most of them would likely try to take down Team Destroyer right from the start.
Had they been showing off too much lately? Why did it feel like Leon was always the prime target of so many teams? Or was that just his own paranoia?
But in a competition like this, it was only natural for the strongest contenders to be ganged up on first—it was simply how things worked.

Soon after, the raid race began. However, this time, Broken joined in from the very first second, unlike before, when he had only stepped in once Starfall and Charmelyn were the last ones left standing.
Wasting no time, he immediately summoned Gaia and all of his beasts, clearing the monster waves at lightning speed—so fast that other teams had barely begun dealing with theirs.
With Goldrich on their side and Charmelyn's expertise in puzzles, they cracked the puzzle challenge before any other team had even gotten started.

Seeing the pace at which Team Destroyer was advancing, the other teams hesitated to attack them. If they wasted time trying to take down Team Destroyer, there was a real chance the raid boss would end up being taken down by them alone.
Eventually, the puzzle phase wrapped up, and two other teams finally caught up to Team Destroyer.

But the moment that happened, Broken went all out, unleashing massive damage on the raid boss without holding back in the slightest. He had no reason to conserve his abilities, given that his cooldowns would be ready for the final match against Frostedge in the Duel of Champions.
Oddly enough, the entire match dynamic had shifted—none of the other teams dared to challenge Team Destroyer. This drew laughter from Melliandra, who couldn't resist mocking them.
"You guys aren't going to gang up on us this time? Hah? Is Broken really that terrifying to you? He's just a blacksmith, huh...? Come on, attack us already!"
But despite her taunts, no one took the bait.
As the final blow landed on the raid boss, a deafening explosion of light filled the arena. The system announcement flashed across the massive screens—"RAID BOSS DEFEATED! TEAM DESTROYER VICTORIOUS!"
Brando, the caster, practically jumped out of his seat.

"UNBELIEVABLE! TEAM DESTROYER DOES IT AGAIN! They didn't just win; they DOMINATED this raid race from start to finish! Look at that execution! Look at that precision! And BROKEN—what kind of monstrous damage output was THAT?! This is sheer destruction, ladies and gentlemen!"
The stadium erupted in chaotic cheers and screams as the crowd went absolutely wild.

The camera panned across the audience, capturing people jumping, throwing their arms in the air, some even banging on the railings in sheer excitement. Fans of other teams sat in stunned silence, unable to believe what they had just witnessed.
Brando, still caught in the adrenaline rush, kept going.

"And look at this! Not a SINGLE team dared to challenge them this time! What a complete reversal from the early rounds, where they were the number one target! And now? Now, Team Destroyer stands UNCONTESTED at the top!"
The energy in the stadium was electric, the roar of the crowd refusing to die down. Team Destroyer had just cemented their dominance in the tournament, and everyone knew it.
Leon and the others stepped out of the capsule devices, greeted by a wave of cheers as they made their way to claim their first-place trophy!
With this victory, Leon had now secured three trophies—one from the Blacksmith Competition, a second-place finish in the Team Battle, and now, another first-place win in the Team Raid Race.
If he could win the Duel of Champions, there was a real chance he'd be crowned MVP of the entire tournament.
But even before that, the energy in the stadium was already off the charts. The grand final—the ultimate showdown, the closing match of the competition—was happening today.
And at this moment, the entire audience was buzzing with speculation, theories, and debates. Who would emerge victorious in this all-out battle?
Frostedge... or Broken?
The match was set to take place in just one hour, and preparations for the closing ceremony were already underway.

And of course, taking center stage was Starfall—Heejin herself—the one who had performed this competition's theme song. The moment she stepped onto the stage, the entire stadium erupted in excitement. Then, as soon as her divine, breathtaking voice filled the air, the crowd was completely spellbound.
Leon sat among his guildmates, watching this spectacular moment unfold.
The Eternal Challenge was entering its final phase, and already, a familiar wave of nostalgia swept over him.
It was moments like these that made it all worth it—the chance to reunite with so many friends, people he only ever got to see within this game.
But there was no time to dwell on that just yet.
With his entire soul, he was ready—ready for the final match.

chapters.title: Chapter 821: The Grand Final Begins!
paragraphs: Brando was visibly ecstatic, his energy practically radiating off the screen as he sat before none other than Frostedge—a legendary player, a national pride of China, and the last remaining contender fighting to uphold their honor in the Duel of Champions.

"Frostedge, I've followed your journey—since your days dominating the Olympic ice-skating scene, all the way to where you stand now. And I have to admit, I'm one of your biggest fans!" Brando exclaimed, his enthusiasm undeniable.
Frostedge offered a calm smile and bowed slightly in response. "Thanks, Brando. That truly means a lot to me."

Brando, still brimming with excitement, pressed on. "I have to ask—I know you and Broken have crossed paths before in Immortal Legacy. There was even that incredible sparring match of yours that went viral online. Not to mention, the two of you fought side by side during the Dissidia Kingdom War. And now, here you both are, standing at the grand finals. I need to know—what's on your mind?"

Frostedge's expression remained serene as he nodded thoughtfully. "Broken is an exceptional player—humble, skilled, and incredibly sharp. We even had a chance to sit down and chat at a café a few days ago. I respect him a lot. This is the match I've been looking forward to."

Brando clapped his hands eagerly, his excitement growing by the second. Then, lowering his voice as if sharing a secret, he added, "And... There's been a lot of speculation online. People have noticed you haven't been using your signature countless spell rotations, something analysts have picked apart frame by frame. Is there a reason for that?"

Frostedge shook his head, his demeanor effortlessly composed. "No, there's no specific reason. It's not about holding back, and it's certainly not about underestimating anyone. But..." his eyes gleamed with determination, "...I promise to give it my all in the grand final."
Brando immediately turned to the camera, his voice booming with excitement.
"I want to hear from ALL of you! Who do you think will claim victory in the grand final?! Because this... this is going to be LEGENDARY!"
In another discussion session, Brando was joined by Stormbreaker, a well-known Chinese player who had once been a strong favorite to make it to the grand final himself.
"I want to hear your thoughts, Stormbreaker. After facing Broken head-on... what's your take on him? And what are his chances against Frostedge?" Brando asked eagerly.

Stormbreaker gave a small, knowing smile before answering. "Well, I have to admit, Broken has a lot of unique items, and some of them have pretty... out-of-the-box effects. Like that greatsword he used against me yesterday."
Brando chuckled. "That was interesting—especially since, in the end, you decided to surrender."

Stormbreaker let out a short laugh. "That..." he said with a shrug, "...was because I didn't want to risk my sword getting destroyed before another important match. But... I don't think that kind of scenario will happen in the grand final. Because I know for a fact that both of them are going all out. And I can confidently say—a simple trick like that won't work on Frostedge."

He shook his head slightly before continuing. "Frostedge is just that talented. He has an incredible range of abilities and is already a widely recognized force in Immortal Legacy. I have no doubt—Broken is in for a real challenge this time. And yes... if you ask me, victory belongs to Frostedge!"

As always, the internet's reaction was what truly made this entire competition legendary. Everyone had their own favorite, their own predictions, and they couldn't wait for the final showdown to unfold that very day!
The internet exploded with reactions after the discussion session, filling forums and social media with everything from serious analyses to downright hilarious takes.
[Josh_Minton_5566]: "BROKEN isn't even a fighter, he's just a blacksmith who went WAY TOO FAR! Stormbreaker was more scared of losing his sword than losing the match! 🤣🤣"
[AatroxVoid]: "Frostedge: Known as one of the most talented players in the world. Broken: 'I'm just a humble blacksmith.' THE WORLD: shaking in fear 😭"
[Marvin_Delawder]: "Honestly, if Broken wins... China might shut down the internet for a week to mourn. 😂"
[Frendscham]: "BROKEN VS FROSTEDGE?? BRO THIS AIN'T A MATCH, THIS IS A SHONEN ANIME FINALE. WHERE'S THE OPENING SONG?!!"
[Drewacord]: "Frostedge and Broken are like two final bosses accidentally placed in the same game. The devs are just sitting back like, 'Oops.'"
[Fredvic]: "Frostedge is out here with insane mechanics and reaction speed. Meanwhile, Broken is probably crafting an 'Auto-Win' button in his inventory as we speak."
[Michael_Hogue]: "Both of these guys are too OP. Honestly, the real loser here is the GAME'S BALANCE TEAM."
[Nate_K]: "Fun fact: The devs are watching this match to decide what needs to be nerfed next season."
A few minutes before the match, Leon sat with Maylon and Euna, discussing the upcoming battle.
"Honestly, I still can't figure out what kind of blessing Frostedge has." Maylon was the first to speak.
Euna turned to him with an eager smile. "Looks like we'll only get our answer once the final begins, Maylon."

Maylon shook his head. "I have to admit, Frostedge has been extremely cautious throughout this competition—like he's been saving everything for this one final match against Broken. If anything, I'd say he's about to give it everything he has. This is going to be one hell of a match to watch."
Leon, sitting between them, nodded slowly. "Well, that's fine. I'm going all out too. Seriously, this will be my first time seeing Frostedge fight at full power—without holding back."

Even when Broken had teamed up with Frostedge against Galactron, Leon had the feeling that Frostedge hadn't gone all in. Maybe it was because Galactron was a genius in his own right, positioning himself so well that he made things difficult for both of them.
But still... There had to be a reason why Frostedge had survived all this time as a solo player in Immortal Legacy, while still remaining one of the top-ranked players in the game.
And today, that answer would finally be revealed.

As the match was about to begin, Leon and Han Feng entered the arena from opposite directions. The tension in the air was palpable. And as always, someone accompanied Frostedge, pushing his wheelchair toward the stage.
The moment they stepped onto the grand stage, the host grabbed the mic, his voice booming across the packed stadium, igniting an explosive wave of cheers from the audience.
"LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, THIS IS IT! THE GRAND FINAL OF THE DUEL OF CHAMPIONS!"
"You've watched the battles! You've seen the rivalries! And NOW—we stand at the PEAK of this tournament, where only TWO remain!"

"On one side—we have FROSTEDGE! A legend, an icon, a warrior of ICE and PRECISION! A player who has dominated battlefields across Immortal Legacy, proving time and time again why he is one of the GREATEST of all time!"

"And on the other side—we have BROKEN! A blacksmith who DEFIED ALL ODDS, climbed the ranks, and turned an entire game world upside down! A player who crafts his own fate, breaks the limits, and now stands as the FINAL CHALLENGER to Frostedge's reign!"
"TWO UNSTOPPABLE FORCES. TWO PLAYERS AT THE PEAK OF THEIR POWER. AND ONLY ONE CAN TAKE THE CROWN!"
"STADIUM, ARE YOU READY?! INTERNET, ARE YOU READY?! WORLD, ARE YOU READY?!"
"THEN LET THE GRAND FINAL—BEGIN!"
The crowd ERUPTED, the entire arena shaking from the sheer volume of cheers. This was it.
The final battle was about to begin.
READERS, ARE YOU READY?!
That's a Wrap for February! See You in March!

The moment they stepped onto the grand stage, the host grabbed the mic, his voice booming across the packed stadium, igniting an explosive wave of cheers from the audience.
"LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, THIS IS IT!
THE GRAND FINAL OF THE DUEL OF CHAMPIONS!"
"You've watched the battles!
You've seen the rivalries!
And NOW—we stand at the PEAK of this tournament, where only TWO remain!"
"On one side—we have FROSTEDGE!
A legend, an icon, a warrior of ICE and PRECISION!
A player who has dominated battlefields across Immortal Legacy, proving time and time again why he is one of the GREATEST of all time!"
"And on the other side—we have BROKEN!
A blacksmith who DEFIED ALL ODDS, climbed the ranks, and turned an entire game world upside down!
A player who crafts his own fate, breaks the limits, and now stands as the FINAL CHALLENGER to Frostedge's reign!"
"TWO UNSTOPPABLE FORCES.
TWO PLAYERS AT THE PEAK OF THEIR POWER.
AND ONLY ONE CAN TAKE THE CROWN!"
"STADIUM, ARE YOU READY?!
INTERNET, ARE YOU READY?!
WORLD, ARE YOU READY?!"
"THEN LET THE GRAND FINAL—BEGIN!"
The crowd ERUPTED, the entire arena shaking from the sheer volume of cheers.
This was it.
The final battle was about to begin.
READERS, ARE YOU READY?!
That's a Wrap for February!
See You in March!

chapters.title: Chapter 822 822 - No Holding Back
paragraphs: Broken stood in the center of the arena, taking in the surroundings. Unlike the previous matches, this time, the setting was different.

He and Frostedge stood on a wide, open battlefield, bordered by towering trees and dense forest. But the most striking feature was the transparent screens positioned on all four sides of the arena, displaying the real world beyond the game.

Through those screens, he could see the crowds—thousands upon thousands of spectators cheering with unrelenting energy. Their voices echoed faintly into the battlefield, a constant mix of chants for Frostedge and Broken, shouted back and forth in a chaotic but electric rhythm.
Broken hadn't expected this. He had never imagined that so many people would be cheering for him. Him.
He never thought he'd end up here, at the grand finale of Immortal Legacy's biggest event, standing at the very edge of something this massive.
It had all happened so fast.
Less than a year ago in the real world, he had been nothing more than a manual laborer, just barely getting by, working tirelessly to pay for his living expenses and education.
Now?

Now, he was someone who had broken past every limit, someone who had built something greater than he ever imagined. His bank balance had skyrocketed, far beyond what he could even spend at this point. Everything had changed.
Broken turned his full attention to the opponent standing before him—Frostedge, the legendary solo player of Immortal Legacy.
He wasn't just a famous name in the game—he had built his reputation long before Immortal Legacy even went public.
To be here, to stand on this stage, to face Frostedge in an all-out fight, and to have a real chance of defeating him—
Broken would not hold back. Not even for a second.
Frostedge had already drawn his sword—the legendary Ice Sword—as a powerful aura of frost surged around him.

At the same time, Broken activated his battle armor, equipping the Mythic-grade Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear. The air around them crackled with tension, their weapons gleaming under the battlefield lights.
The countdown had begun.

Broken could feel it—the surge of energy, the anticipation, the sheer intensity of the moment. His mind was sharp, his focus unwavering, his body fully prepared. He tightened his grip on the spear, his heart pounding, ready to meet his opponent head-on.
For some reason, there was a silent understanding between them—unspoken, yet undeniable.
And then—
ZERO!
The battle began!
In an instant, Broken and Frostedge launched forward, closing the distance in a blur of motion. Both wielded their weapons with deadly precision, their footwork flawless as they prepared to clash.
This was it—a rematch of spear versus sword, a battle that had once been interrupted in the past, now set to unfold with no interruptions, no limits, and no holding back.
Broken spun his spear above his head, channeling the full force of his momentum before swinging down for a devastating headstrike.
But Frostedge was as sharp as ever. His mastery of footwork and technique allowed him to evade with stunning precision, barely shifting his stance while avoiding the impact entirely.

Broken grinned, undeterred. He immediately pressed forward, relentlessly attacking with the extended range of his spear—thrust, swipe, thrust, swipe! Every movement was calculated, a steady pressure meant to deny Frostedge any opening to counterattack.
He was faster, sharper, and stronger than ever.

He had forged a deeper connection with his weapon—not just inside the game, but outside of it too. Training both in and out of the battlefield, honing his skills through countless battles—from casual skirmishes to fights that pushed him to his absolute limits.
Broken was no longer just a player relying on his equipment's magic skills.
He was a warrior—trained, experienced, and ready to take on one of the greatest legends of Immortal Legacy.
They clashed fiercely, their weapons colliding in rapid succession, neither giving an inch.

Frostedge wasn't just dodging—he was actively deflecting Broken's spear strikes, redirecting the momentum with precision. And with each successful deflection, he closed the distance, moving in swiftly before delivering a sharp slash with his sword.

Broken reacted instantly, using the momentum of his spear to shift backward, but Frostedge was faster. His blade cut through the air, narrowly missing Broken, who avoided it with an anticipatory grin.
Without missing a beat, Broken yanked his spear back, swiftly spinning his body before lunging forward with another powerful thrust.
Frostedge flipped sideways, evading the attack midair before landing with perfect balance.
But Broken wasn't stopping.

He launched thrust after thrust, forcing Frostedge to continuously dodge, their movements turning into a dizzying dance of speed and precision. They mirrored each other's agility—both leaping to the side, both adjusting their footwork, both testing each other's limits.

Then, in a moment of sheer mastery, Frostedge stomped down on Broken's spear, pinning it to the ground. With the perfectly timed momentum, he propelled himself forward, launching at blinding speed—his sword tip aimed straight at Broken's face!
The crowd gasped.
But Broken twisted his body just in time, sidestepping the attack with stunning finesse. He immediately repositioned himself, maintaining just the right distance to keep Frostedge from pressing in.
This fight—this display of raw skill—was breathtaking.
No one could tear their eyes away.
Everyone already knew that Frostedge was a master swordsman, someone whose combat skills extended far beyond the game, an athlete recognized even outside of Immortal Legacy.
But what shocked everyone the most—what left the entire stadium and the online audience in pure disbelief—was the fact that Broken was matching him.
Not with his overpowered equipment.
Not with his army of summons.
But with his own raw combat ability.
At this moment, if someone claimed that Broken was a professional spear fighter in real life, no one would dare argue.
Brando was practically screaming, his voice bursting with uncontainable excitement as each exchange between the two players sent shockwaves through the stadium.
"OH—MY—GOD! WHAT ARE WE WITNESSING RIGHT NOW?!"
"THIS IS NOT JUST A GAME—THIS IS ART! THIS IS A MASTERPIECE OF COMBAT!"
"Look at the movement! Look at the precision! Frostedge, the legendary swordsman, is displaying his world-class technique, and yet—BROKEN. IS. KEEPING. UP!"
"We all knew Frostedge would put on a show, but NOBODY—AND I MEAN NOBODY—expected Broken to fight like this! No summons, no tricks, just pure technique! HOW IS HE EVEN DOING THIS?!"
"This man—this BLACKSMITH—was supposed to be just a craftsman, a support player, a strategist. And yet here he is, matching Frostedge's footwork, his speed, his precision—BLOW FOR BLOW!"
"This isn't a battle of power anymore. This is a duel between two absolute MASTERS of their craft! And we are witnessing HISTORY IN THE MAKING!"
"I don't care who you're rooting for—whether it's Frostedge or Broken—what we are seeing right now is something that will be TALKED ABOUT FOR YEARS!"
"I need everyone watching to understand—this isn't just an epic final match. This is a MOMENT that will define Immortal Legacy FOREVER!"
"KEEP YOUR EYES ON THIS FIGHT, BECAUSE WE HAVE NO IDEA WHO IS GOING TO COME OUT ON TOP!"
"THIS—IS—INSANE!"
Inside the arena, Broken and Frostedge had now put some distance between each other once again.

They had already tested each other's technique—a battle of pure skill and precision. But now, it was clear to everyone watching that both players were ready to escalate the fight to something even bigger.
The atmosphere in the stadium was electric, anticipation hanging in the air like a storm about to break.
At that moment, Broken muttered softly, his voice almost lost in the tension-filled silence.
"Gaia, Pawpaw... I need you."

chapters.title: Chapter 823 823 - The Ice King Awakens
paragraphs: "Gaia, Pawpaw... I need you."
At those words, Gaia immediately manifested beside Broken—a striking figure with ashen-red hair, her form wrapped in a blend of vines and shadows, creating an ethereal yet ominous presence.
At the same time, Pawpaw, the demon cat, materialized in front of Broken, lazily sitting down before letting out a long, uninterested yawn.

The crowd erupted, cheering wildly the moment Pawpaw was shown on the big screen, his infamous bored expression causing a wave of laughter and excitement across the stadium. Despite his lazy demeanor, everyone knew just how dangerous he truly was.
Broken, however, stayed laser-focused. This fight was about to escalate even further. And he was going to force Frostedge into an even higher-stakes battle.
With a single thought, all twelve of Gaia's Beasts materialized around him, forming a strategic formation, their eyes locked onto Frostedge, ready to strike.
At the same time, Pawpaw's form melted into the shadows, disappearing into the unknown—waiting for the perfect moment to pounce.
The Battle Resumes!
The Elder Tree Dragon twisted through the air, its massive form shifting as it unleashed a sweeping magic attack, engulfing the battlefield around Frostedge in a storm of crushing force.
Frostedge reacted instantly.
He dashed forward, narrowly escaping the blast, but the vines from below shot out, attempting to trap him.

In a flash of ice, his movements became effortlessly fluid—his feet gliding over the ground as a layer of frost formed beneath him, accelerating his momentum. He soared into the air, twisting with precise agility, dodging every grasping vine with inhuman speed.
Then—he struck.
His sword sliced through, cutting down the encroaching roots with razor-sharp efficiency. Every step, every movement—he was untouchable.
But Broken wasn't done.
He dashed forward, closing in from the opposite side, his spear slicing through the air in a perfectly timed strike.

Frostedge reacted in an instant, twisting midair, narrowly avoiding the thrust. An icy trail followed his movement, leaving behind a streak of shimmering frost as he flipped away—graceful, like an artist painting across the battlefield.
And now, he was surrounded.
Twelve beasts. Gaia. Pawpaw lurking in the shadows. And Broken, pressing in with relentless spear attacks.
Yet—
Not a single attack landed.
Frostedge moved like he was gliding on ice—dodging, weaving, countering—each motion was a flawless display of precision and control.
And still—
HE HADN'T USED A SINGLE SKILL.
He was still holding back.
This deadlock continued for a moment—the beasts lunging at Frostedge, attempting to corner him, but he was simply too fast.
He slid across the arena effortlessly, weaving through every attack with near-impossible precision.
And what was even more frustrating?
He still wasn't attacking.
He was only dodging.
Broken narrowed his eyes. Was this a sign that his pressure wasn't enough to force Frostedge into a real fight? Or was he deliberately holding back, putting on a show for the audience?
Not bad!
Fine. If Frostedge wouldn't engage, Broken would force him to.
With a swift motion, Broken activated his spear's skill, channeling a massive surge of water into a single, devastating thrust forward.
A torrent of energy roared through the battlefield, crashing toward Frostedge in an unstoppable wave.
But even in this desperate situation—even with no room left to maneuver—
Frostedge still dodged.
Just barely—but he dodged.
This guy... seriously?!
His control over his body, movement, and spacing was unreal.
"ARE YOU SEEING THIS?! THIS IS INSANE!"

"BROKEN IS THROWING EVERYTHING AT FROSTEDGE! The beasts are attacking! The Elder Tree Dragon is raining destruction! And Broken just unleashed a COLOSSAL water attack—BUT LOOK AT HIM! LOOK AT FROSTEDGE!"
"HE'S DODGING. HE'S WEAVING. HE'S GLIDING ACROSS THE ARENA LIKE IT'S HIS OWN PERSONAL ICE RINK! NOT A SINGLE HIT HAS LANDED! NOT ONE!"
"And here's the CRAZIEST part—HE HASN'T EVEN FOUGHT BACK YET! HE'S JUST DODGING! LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, IS HE TOYING WITH BROKEN?! IS HE PUTTING ON A SHOW FOR THE FANS? OR IS HE JUST THAT CONFIDENT?!"
"BROKEN IS FORCING THE PRESSURE, BUT FROSTEDGE IS JUST... UNTOUCHABLE!"
"This isn't just a fight—this is ART! This is HISTORY IN THE MAKING! I'M LOSING MY MIND RIGHT NOW!"
The relentless attacks from Gaia and her beasts were enough to keep Frostedge occupied—for now.
Broken seized the opportunity.
He leaped back, switching his armor mid-air, instantly equipping his Archer Armor. In one smooth motion, he pulled out his Golden Bow of Artemis, but instead of arrows—
He loaded his spear into it.
He charged the attack.
The moment the charge began, the sky split open—a massive ethereal spear forming above, crackling with sheer destructive force.
The audience gasped.
This was one of Broken's most devastating attacks.
And Frostedge knew it.
For the first time, Frostedge's expression shifted. His movements became sharper, more aggressive—he wasn't just dodging anymore.
He started cutting down the beasts.
He wasn't running away.
He was looking for footing.
Because he knew—if he kept evading like before, there was no way he could escape this attack.
And everyone in the stadium knew it too.
The tension was unbearable.
The crowd held their breath, perched at the edge of their seats.
Broken didn't care what Frostedge had planned.
He knew Frostedge had a way to survive this. But not by dodging.
No. This time—Frostedge would have to take the hit.
He would have to go all out.
Because if he didn't—
He would lose. Right here. Right now.
And Broken wasn't about to hold back.
The spear was released.
A colossal mass of ocean water came crashing down from the heavens—
A titanic water spear, surging toward Frostedge like a falling tidal wave, ready to consume everything in its path.
The sky itself seemed to warp under the sheer pressure, the roar of water drowning out all other sound as the attack descended at blinding speed.
But Broken wasn't done.
He switched weapons again—this time, equipping the Bedrock Breaker Pickaxe.
Follow-up attack—immediate.
The ground trembled violently, cracks splintering outward in every direction—an earthquake of raw power surging beneath the battlefield.
And then—
Boulders rained down from above.
Massive. Monstrous. Unrelenting.
Dozens of gigantic stone slabs crashed through the air, descending like the wrath of an ancient god, each one powerful enough to shatter steel upon impact.
And beneath all of this, the earth split open further, revealing a gaping abyss—a chasm that seemed alive, like the open maw of a colossal beast, threatening to swallow everything whole.
The entire arena was collapsing.
The combined force of magic and physical destruction overwhelmed the battlefield, turning the space around Frostedge into a maelstrom of pure annihilation.
And yet—
He had only a single moment to react.
The audience was frozen in suspense—no one moved, no one blinked.
Then—impact.
The massive water spear hit first, detonating with an explosion so fierce that it sent shockwaves rippling outward, blasting wind and mist across the entire stadium.
The boulders followed immediately after, colliding into the arena like meteors, crushing everything in their wake.

And then, as the final catastrophe, the ground caved in, dragging everything into the abyss, a deafening roar echoing through the arena as the very foundation of the battlefield was consumed by destruction.
For a moment—
Nothing.
Just silence.
The arena was in ruins.
And the question on everyone's mind—
Did Frostedge survive?

As the dust and mist began to settle, the once devastated arena was now covered in layers of shattered rock, cracked ice, and mist from the ocean spear's impact. The sheer force of the attack had ripped apart the battlefield, leaving nothing but ruins in its wake.
For a moment, everyone thought it was over.
And then—
A chill spread through the air.
A surge of frost and ice erupted from the center of the destruction, freezing over the broken ground in an instant.
And as the mist cleared—
He stood there.
Frostedge. Unharmed.
But he was different now.
Behind him, an enormous Ice Avatar had manifested—a towering warrior of pure frozen energy, its form radiating power as an icy aura swirled around its colossal body. It was protecting its summoner!
And on Frostedge himself, a new armor of shimmering ice had formed, wrapping around his body like a second skin, its crystalline surface reflecting the lights of the arena.
The crowd erupted in shock.
Frostedge had activated his skills.
At that moment, Maylon, seated among the spectators, suddenly straightened up, his eyes locked onto the battlefield.
A quiet murmur escaped his lips.
"He is..."
Euna, noticing his reaction, turned to him with curiosity. "Maylon?"
Maylon's gaze remained fixed on a massive screen, his expression a mix of realization and awe.
"...I finally understand the secret behind his Pride Champion blessing."

But not by dodging.
No.
This time—Frostedge would have to take the hit.
He would have to go all out.
Because if he didn't—
He would lose.
Right here.
Right now.
And Broken wasn't about to hold back.
The spear was released.
A colossal mass of ocean water came crashing down from the heavens—
A titanic water spear, surging toward Frostedge like a falling tidal wave, ready to consume everything in its path.
The sky itself seemed to warp under the sheer pressure, the roar of water drowning out all other sound as the attack descended at blinding speed.
But Broken wasn't done.
He switched weapons again—this time, equipping the Bedrock Breaker Pickaxe.
Follow-up attack—immediate.
The ground trembled violently, cracks splintering outward in every direction—an earthquake of raw power surging beneath the battlefield.
And then—
Boulders rained down from above.
Massive.
Monstrous.
Unrelenting.
Dozens of gigantic stone slabs crashed through the air, descending like the wrath of an ancient god, each one powerful enough to shatter steel upon impact.
And beneath all of this, the earth split open further, revealing a gaping abyss—a chasm that seemed alive, like the open maw of a colossal beast, threatening to swallow everything whole.
The entire arena was collapsing.
The combined force of magic and physical destruction overwhelmed the battlefield, turning the space around Frostedge into a maelstrom of pure annihilation.
And yet—
He had only a single moment to react.
The audience was frozen in suspense—no one moved, no one blinked.
Then—impact.
The massive water spear hit first, detonating with an explosion so fierce that it sent shockwaves rippling outward, blasting wind and mist across the entire stadium.
The boulders followed immediately after, colliding into the arena like meteors, crushing everything in their wake.

And then, as the final catastrophe, the ground caved in, dragging everything into the abyss, a deafening roar echoing through the arena as the very foundation of the battlefield was consumed by destruction.
For a moment—
Nothing.
Just silence.
The arena was in ruins.
And the question on everyone's mind—
Did Frostedge survive?
As the dust and mist began to settle, the once devastated arena was now covered in layers of shattered rock, cracked ice, and mist from the ocean spear's impact.
The sheer force of the attack had ripped apart the battlefield, leaving nothing but ruins in its wake.
For a moment, everyone thought it was over.
And then—
A chill spread through the air.
A surge of frost and ice erupted from the center of the destruction, freezing over the broken ground in an instant.
And as the mist cleared—
He stood there.
Frostedge.
Unharmed.
But he was different now.
Behind him, an enormous Ice Avatar had manifested—a towering warrior of pure frozen energy, its form radiating power as an icy aura swirled around its colossal body.
It was protecting its summoner!
And on Frostedge himself, a new armor of shimmering ice had formed, wrapping around his body like a second skin, its crystalline surface reflecting the lights of the arena.
The crowd erupted in shock.
Frostedge had activated his skills.
At that moment, Maylon, seated among the spectators, suddenly straightened up, his eyes locked onto the battlefield.
A quiet murmur escaped his lips.
"He is..."
Euna, noticing his reaction, turned to him with curiosity.
"Maylon?"
Maylon's gaze remained fixed on a massive screen, his expression a mix of realization and awe.
"...I finally understand the secret behind his Pride Champion blessing."

chapters.title: Chapter 824: Frost Titan
paragraphs: A massive ice golem emerged behind Frostedge, its towering form crackling with frozen energy. The colossal guardian had taken the brunt of Broken's devastating attacks, shielding its master from the overwhelming force that had just obliterated the battlefield.
But that wasn't all.
Frostedge himself had changed.
Now, he was clad in even heavier armor, layered with thick, crystalline ice—a fortress of frost wrapped around his body, making him appear like a walking war machine forged from the cold itself.
It was breathtaking.
Not just for Broken, but for everyone watching.
The stadium was in absolute chaos. The moment the spectators realized what had just happened, many of them shot up from their seats, screaming in shock and hysteria.
What kind of skill was this?!
For the first time ever, Frostedge had revealed these abilities—and he had chosen to do so here, in the grand final, against Broken.
And yet, while the entire stadium was reeling in excitement—
Broken frowned.
Because after all the research he had done on Frostedge, after studying every known skill in his public ability list—
This wasn't on it.
He had never seen this before.
But then—a realization began to take shape in his mind.
The Pride Champion Blessing. The ancestral wielders of this power—the ones he had just encountered in the game—
They didn't just fight stronger. They bent reality itself.
Stormbreaker had an ability that granted him a 100% critical hit rate—an impossible mechanic in any normal system.
Vallrick's ability let him sacrifice his own levels to forcibly drain the level of his opponent—rewriting progression mechanics entirely.
And now—Frostedge.
What if his ability allowed him to...
At that exact moment, from the spectator seats, Maylon finally answered Euna's lingering question.
"...he can change the rules of his own skills."
"What?!" Euna gasped, her eyes widening in shock.
"Wait..." Euna muttered, her mind racing with questions. "Change the rules of his own skills? How is that even possible?

Maylon leaned forward slightly, his gaze still locked on the battlefield as he explained. "If you look at Frostedge's known skill list—the ones that have been analyzed and documented by the community—there's actually a pattern."
Euna tilted her head, intrigued. "A pattern?"

Maylon nodded. "Many of his skills share similar mechanics or animation effects. The differences are usually in their damage output, range, or cooldown duration. Some seem nearly identical, except for subtle variations in how they're executed."
Euna frowned, trying to process this. "Wait, are you saying he can change the details of his own skills? That's ridiculously broken! He could just tweak a skill to deal absurd amounts of damage!"

"It's not that simple." Maylon shook his head. "There has to be a price. From what I've observed, increasing the damage percentage means increasing the mana cost or cooldown duration. He can also convert a single-target skill into an AoE attack, but only by sacrificing some other aspect of the skill."
Euna's curiosity deepened. "So... is that why he wasn't using any skills earlier in the fight?"

"Most likely." Maylon nodded. "He could've imposed specific conditions on his skills—higher cooldowns, specific activation triggers—in exchange for enhanced effects. If that's true, then we'll see even more proof of it soon. And if that's really how it works..." He exhaled slowly. "...then this is going to be very difficult for Broken."

Euna's eyes widened as the realization hit her. "That's... insane. Seriously insane! If Frostedge really couldn't use most of his skills before this battle, then it means it would have all been for nothing if he didn't make it to the grand final, right?"
Maylon smirked slightly. "Exactly. He was confident he'd make it here. And he was saving everything for this moment—for Broken."
Euna blinked, still trying to wrap her head around it. "Wait... he knew Broken would make it to the final?"
Maylon finally turned to face her, a knowing look in his eyes. "You didn't?"
Euna let out a small laugh. "Now that I think about it... I don't think I ever had a reason to doubt Broken would get this far."
The entire stadium was still in shock. Even Brando, the ever-enthusiastic caster, was left completely speechless for a moment before bursting into excited commentary.
Meanwhile, Euna's voice cut through the tension. "Was Broken prepared for this?"
Maylon didn't hesitate. "Broken is not that simple, Euna..."
She turned to him as he continued, his tone steady.
"On the surface, he might seem like someone who just charges ahead, taking on massive challenges recklessly... but there's one thing most people fail to notice about him."
Maylon's gaze sharpened. "He has an unshakable drive to progress. When he sets a goal, he almost never fails."
He paused for a brief moment, then added, "And when he set his goal to defeat Frostedge..."
Another pause.
"I have no doubt that he has already done his homework for this moment. Yes... I'm sure Broken has realized this truth as well."
Euna let out a small, knowing smile, shifting her focus back to the giant screen displaying the battlefield.
"This guy... most people think he's just insanely lucky because of his OP blessings..." She exhaled, almost amused. "...but I think his real broken ability is his focus and dedication to his target."
Maylon smirked. "Couldn't agree more."
Broken remained completely still, watching as Frostedge stood tall once again.
Now, even his sword had changed—its blade radiated with a brilliant icy aura, pulsating with pure magic energy. But more than that—
Everything around him had come to life.

The thin layer of ice beneath his feet began to spread outward, slowly but surely consuming the battlefield. Snowflakes started to drift down from above, signaling a rapid transformation of the terrain.
Soon—this entire arena would be a frozen battlefield.
Frostedge looked different now.
Not just in appearance—but in presence.
This was the Frostedge Broken had been waiting for.
This was the legendary warrior he had set his sights on—the ultimate target to surpass.
Broken's lips curled into a small grin. "That's a cool golem."
Frostedge gave a slight bow, then brought his hands together in a calm motion. "It's not exactly a golem like yours... but yeah, I suppose it functions similarly."
"Should we give it a name?" Broken asked.
Frostedge tilted his head for a second before casually replying, "Frost Titan. How's that? Just made it up on the spot."
"That's cool," Broken nodded approvingly. Then, his grin widened. "And I think... Blackthorn would love to be its opponent."
At that moment, a massive magic circle appeared behind Broken.
From the swirling void of dark energy, a towering figure emerged.

A hulking entity, its body mostly composed of twisting black vines, its form shadowy and monstrous, yet unmistakably powerful. Its gorilla-like head loomed over the battlefield, while in its massive hands, it wielded a tremendous greatsword—a blade designed for pure destruction.
The crowd gasped.
Another monstrous clash was about to begin.
Frostedge smirked. "I hope my made-up golem doesn't disappoint your legendary one."
Broken let out a small smile. "I hope so too. Because if it does, my golem is going to make things very difficult for you."
For a brief second—the two warriors locked eyes.
Then—they both grinned.
Excitement surged between them—undeniable, unstoppable.
And at that exact moment—
The Frost Titan and Blackthorn launched forward—rushing straight for each other—ready to collide in an earth-shattering clash!

chapters.title: Chapter 825: Abyssal Reckoning
paragraphs: The Frost Titan and Blackthorn clashed in the center of the arena, the impact of their collision shaking the battlefield.

Blackthorn's massive greatsword came crashing down with monstrous force, only to be caught mid-air by the Frost Titan's colossal arms. The ground beneath them shuddered from the sheer weight of their strength—a true battle between titans.
At the same time, Broken and Frostedge began moving, circling the arena, both maintaining a careful distance while preparing for their next attack.
Meanwhile, the Gaia Beasts continued their relentless assault on Frostedge, attempting to corner him from all directions.
But now—his attacks were stronger.
With just one swing, Abyss Thorn Ox, a massive beast taller than Frostedge himself, was instantly encased in ice, completely frozen in place. One hit. That was all it took.
Broken narrowed his eyes, his focus shifting between Frostedge and the Frost Titan.
Something wasn't adding up.
The way the Frost Titan moved... It had fully functioning limbs—it was acting like a true golem with independent movement.
But wait...
Didn't golem creation require a specialized Class?
Or was this just another modified skill—a natural extension of Frostedge's ice constructs, similar to the massive ice sword he once used against Galactron's skeleton warriors in the past?
If that was the case...
Then the Frost Titan wasn't autonomous. Frostedge was controlling it. Simultaneously. While fighting off multiple beasts and evading Broken's attacks.
That's insane.
The level of control, precision, and awareness needed to pull this off was beyond anything Broken had expected.
Realizing this, Broken tightened his grip on his spear.
This fight... had just become even more difficult.
Frostedge was moving faster than ever, his attacks more relentless, more brutal.
Every time his ice sword slashed, the impact didn't just deal damage—it imprisoned whatever it touched in an ice cage, instantly restricting movement.
A terrifying ability.
And now—he was charging straight for Broken.
Reacting instantly, Broken activated his Water Domain.
The moment Frostedge stepped into the domain, their weapons clashed—spear against sword, water against ice.
But—something was wrong.
As soon as Broken made contact, his body encased in ice, freezing over in an instant. His movements slowed, his strikes became heavier, and his momentum was completely disrupted.
Damn!
He fought back, engaging in rapid weapon exchanges, but he could only remain in close combat for short bursts—any longer, and the ice would fully restrict him.
Then—a sudden, massive threat.
Five colossal ice swords materialized above him, shimmering with deadly precision, before plummeting downward at blinding speed.
Damn!
BOOM!
A violent collision.

The swords crashed into the battlefield with earth-shattering force, sending shockwaves of ice and debris exploding outward. A surge of freezing energy spread through the ground, covering everything in layers of frost.
But when the mist cleared—Broken was still standing.
His Invincible Paragon layer had absorbed the impact.
That was close. Too close.
And then—
More.
Dozens of massive ice swords manifested in the sky, their jagged edges glowing with an ominous blue light, their sheer size dwarfing the battlefield.
And they all descended at once.
This wasn't like the ice shards from Akiko's fight before.
These weren't just large projectiles—these had monstrous damage and a dangerous secondary effect.
If even one of them hit critically and activated its imprisonment effect, Broken would be completely trapped.
He had to destroy them before they hit.
Or else—
He was in serious trouble.

Broken dashed swiftly across the battlefield, narrowly avoiding the relentless onslaught of massive ice swords crashing down from above. Some, he managed to shatter mid-air with well-timed strikes from his spear, the force of his attacks breaking through the ice just before impact.
But even as he focused on surviving the barrage, something changed.
The temperature dropped sharply.
The air grew still.
Then—
A massive, transparent ice dome materialized around the arena.
It expanded in an instant, enclosing the entire battlefield in a frozen, translucent barrier.
What the hell is this?
Broken's eyes darted around, analyzing the sudden shift in his surroundings. Before he could even attempt an escape—
It began.
A storm of razor-sharp ice shards rained down from above, cascading like a deadly blizzard, leaving no room to breathe, no space to run.
Damn it!
This wasn't just a high-damage skill.
This was an environment designed specifically to trap him.
A domain where escape was impossible—where every attack was funneled directly onto him.
Frostedge had planned this. Every move, every ability—all meticulously designed to wear Broken down, forcing him into a battlefield where Frostedge had complete control.
And this time—
He wasn't holding back.
"UNBELIEVABLE! FROSTEDGE JUST SEALED THE BATTLEFIELD WITH A MASSIVE ICE DOME!"
"LOOK AT THIS! The ice shards are falling like a merciless STORM, cutting off every possible escape! No openings, no blind spots—this is a domain designed for ABSOLUTE DOMINATION!"
Brando paused, his voice lowering slightly as the tension in the stadium thickens.
"The question now is... can Broken SURVIVE this?"
"Does he have a way out? Does he have a counter?"
"Or... is THIS the moment? Is THIS where Frostedge claims the final victory?"
The stadium was dead silent, everyone holding their breath as the ice storm continued to crash down.
"BROKEN... this is it! If you have anything left—NOW IS THE TIME TO SHOW IT!"
From every angle—whether on the giant screens or directly inside the arena—it was painfully clear.
Broken was cornered.
The continuous barrage of ice attacks rained down on him, each strike relentless, unyielding, chipping away at his health at an alarming rate.
The only reason he was still standing was his massive regeneration—his body healing just fast enough to keep him alive.
If Gaia's duration had ended already, he would have fallen by now.
And Frostedge knew it.
The crowd watched in tense silence, barely anyone believing there was a way out.
Broken was getting bombarded.
There was no pause, no breathing room, no obvious escape.
Euna shook her head, her voice barely above a whisper. "Will he survive?"
Beside her, Maylon let out a small chuckle, amused by the question. "You of all people should know better, Euna."
She turned to him. "Yes, he hasn't used everything he has yet. What is he doing?"

Maylon leaned forward slightly, his eyes gleaming with understanding. "They're testing each other's limits. Neither one wants to overcommit first—because whoever throws out their ultimate attack and gets countered... is going to lose massively."
"So, they're forcing each other to move first?"
"Exactly. They're trying to maintain their resources, waiting for the right moment."
Euna's expression remained tense as she kept her eyes glued to the battlefield. "But... Gaia's duration. If Broken keeps stalling, Frostedge will just outlast him."
Maylon's lips curled into a small, knowing smile. "You're forgetting something, Euna."
She turned to him sharply.
"Frostedge has limits too. He's not a mage—his mana is finite."
He leaned back, confidence in his voice. "In the end, this fight is about one thing: who runs out of resources first."
Euna exhaled, gripping the edge of her seat. "Damn... I didn't expect this fight to become this strategic."
Just when everyone thought the battle was turning hopeless for Broken—
He suddenly closed the distance. In the blink of an eye, he was right in front of Frostedge—their weapons poised for a direct clash.
But then—
Something changed. A brilliant, blinding light erupted from Broken's body.
Cracks—glowing like molten energy—began spreading across his entire form, splitting through his armor, his skin, his very essence.
Then—
[Self-Destruction: Abyssal Reckoning (Conditional Active Skill) activated]
And then—detonation.
BOOOOOOOOM!!!
A violent explosion erupted from Broken's body, a cataclysmic blast of abyssal energy consuming the entire battlefield.
The first wave of destruction shattered the ice dome from the inside, sending massive crystal shards flying in all directions.
[Ring of Relentless Casting passive skill triggered. Skill cooldown reset.]
He grinned. Wide. Unrestrained.
[Self-Destruction: Abyssal Reckoning (Conditional Active Skill) activated]
Then came the second wave—
A surge of dark energy ripped through the ground, creating earth-shattering fissures, the sheer force sending shockwaves powerful enough to distort the air itself.
A chain reaction.
One explosion after another detonated in rapid succession, spiraling outward like a collapsing star—a vortex of destruction that swallowed everything within its radius.
The arena itself trembled, the crowd screaming in shock as the entire battlefield was now engulfed in chaotic devastation.
Everything—the frost, the Frost Titan, the battlefield itself—was being torn apart.
And at the very center of it all—
Broken and Frostedge.
