A domain where escape was impossible—where every attack was funneled directly onto him.
Frostedge had planned this.
Every move, every ability—all meticulously designed to wear Broken down, forcing him into a battlefield where Frostedge had complete control.
And this time—
He wasn't holding back.
"UNBELIEVABLE!
FROSTEDGE JUST SEALED THE BATTLEFIELD WITH A MASSIVE ICE DOME!"
"LOOK AT THIS!
The ice shards are falling like a merciless STORM, cutting off every possible escape!
No openings, no blind spots—this is a domain designed for ABSOLUTE DOMINATION!"
Brando paused, his voice lowering slightly as the tension in the stadium thickens.
"The question now is... can Broken SURVIVE this?"
"Does he have a way out?
Does he have a counter?"
"Or... is THIS the moment?
Is THIS where Frostedge claims the final victory?"
The stadium was dead silent, everyone holding their breath as the ice storm continued to crash down.
"BROKEN... this is it!
If you have anything left—NOW IS THE TIME TO SHOW IT!"
From every angle—whether on the giant screens or directly inside the arena—it was painfully clear.
Broken was cornered.
The continuous barrage of ice attacks rained down on him, each strike relentless, unyielding, chipping away at his health at an alarming rate.
The only reason he was still standing was his massive regeneration—his body healing just fast enough to keep him alive.
If Gaia's duration had ended already, he would have fallen by now.
And Frostedge knew it.
The crowd watched in tense silence, barely anyone believing there was a way out.
Broken was getting bombarded.
There was no pause, no breathing room, no obvious escape.
Euna shook her head, her voice barely above a whisper.
"Will he survive?"
Beside her, Maylon let out a small chuckle, amused by the question.
"You of all people should know better, Euna."
She turned to him.
"Yes, he hasn't used everything he has yet.
What is he doing?"
Maylon leaned forward slightly, his eyes gleaming with understanding.
"They're testing each other's limits.
Neither one wants to overcommit first—because whoever throws out their ultimate attack and gets countered... is going to lose massively."
"So, they're forcing each other to move first?"
"Exactly.
They're trying to maintain their resources, waiting for the right moment."
Euna's expression remained tense as she kept her eyes glued to the battlefield.
"But...
Gaia's duration.
If Broken keeps stalling, Frostedge will just outlast him."
Maylon's lips curled into a small, knowing smile.
"You're forgetting something, Euna."
She turned to him sharply.
"Frostedge has limits too.
He's not a mage—his mana is finite."
He leaned back, confidence in his voice.
"In the end, this fight is about one thing: who runs out of resources first."
Euna exhaled, gripping the edge of her seat.
"Damn...
I didn't expect this fight to become this strategic."
Just when everyone thought the battle was turning hopeless for Broken—
He suddenly closed the distance.
In the blink of an eye, he was right in front of Frostedge—their weapons poised for a direct clash.
But then—
Something changed.
A brilliant, blinding light erupted from Broken's body.
Cracks—glowing like molten energy—began spreading across his entire form, splitting through his armor, his skin, his very essence.
Then—
[Self-Destruction: Abyssal Reckoning (Conditional Active Skill) activated]
And then—detonation.
BOOOOOOOOM!!!
A violent explosion erupted from Broken's body, a cataclysmic blast of abyssal energy consuming the entire battlefield.
The first wave of destruction shattered the ice dome from the inside, sending massive crystal shards flying in all directions.
[Ring of Relentless Casting passive skill triggered.
Skill cooldown reset.]
He grinned.
Wide.
Unrestrained.
[Self-Destruction: Abyssal Reckoning (Conditional Active Skill) activated]
Then came the second wave—
A surge of dark energy ripped through the ground, creating earth-shattering fissures, the sheer force sending shockwaves powerful enough to distort the air itself.
A chain reaction.
One explosion after another detonated in rapid succession, spiraling outward like a collapsing star—a vortex of destruction that swallowed everything within its radius.
The arena itself trembled, the crowd screaming in shock as the entire battlefield was now engulfed in chaotic devastation.
Everything—the frost, the Frost Titan, the battlefield itself—was being torn apart.
And at the very center of it all—
Broken and Frostedge.

chapters.title: Chapter 826 826 - An Arena Split in Two
paragraphs: Explosion after explosion erupted with brutal intensity, making it feel as if the entire stadium itself was detonating. The sheer power of the blasts, amplified by the massive sound system, sent vibrations through the seats, making the audience feel the impact as if they were part of the battle.

Experiencing a battle of this scale and grandeur in person was on a whole different level compared to watching it online. Nearly everyone in attendance felt completely drawn into the breathtaking clash unfolding in this grand final.

But... after that massive explosion... Everyone was dying to know what had happened to the two contenders, Broken and Frostedge. When their profiles flashed on the screen, the entire crowd was left in shock—both players still had full health.
This was insane!

As the smoke and aftermath of the colossal blast began to settle, two figures gradually came back into view. But then, something else made the entire audience gasp in disbelief—because what they saw was eerily familiar.

Standing in the arena where Frostedge had been, a massive ice golem now loomed behind him, shielding him from the devastating explosion unleashed by Broken. The Frost Titan's left side was shattered, with chunks of ice scattered across the battlefield.
Yet, that wasn't even the most shocking part. This Frost Titan was different from the one before!
There were now two Frost Titans on the field!
How!? What!? Frostedge hadn't even revealed his full arsenal yet.
Just how far did the limits of these two players' power go?

Broken observed the battlefield closely, analyzing the situation and coming to a conclusion—this Frost Titan might be something Frostedge summoned whenever he took a massive hit. And this was already the second time. Who knew how many more times he could do this?
Still, Broken doubted that Frostedge could keep this up more than three times.

If he could land another devastating attack, then at the very least, he was confident that no more Frost Titans would appear. That would force Frostedge to find another way to withstand his onslaught.
This guy was really hiding a lot, wasn't he? And this was probably just the tip of the iceberg. Broken needed to push Frostedge to his absolute limit again—before Gaia's duration ran out.
Even though in an intense one-on-one battle like this, time felt like it was moving slower, the ten-minute duration of Gaia's effect still felt incredibly long.
"FROSTEDGE! FROSTEDGE! FROSTEDGE!"

Broken's attention shifted to the massive transparent screens surrounding the battlefield, where he heard the deafening chants of the crowd, all cheering for his opponent. The sheer volume of their voices was overwhelming—and strangely moving. Even though all that support was directed at the man he was fighting against.

In some sections of the arena, Frostedge's fans were even tossing red roses toward the stage... It was exactly like what happened when Hand Feng retired from the world of ice skating years ago. These people had come here not just to watch a battle but to show their unwavering support for their hero once again.
Frostedge had already recovered, and the fight was about to resume. But the roaring cheers for him were unreal. Was it possible that the majority of the audience here were Frostedge's fans?
Where were Broken's supporters? He didn't hear a single voice calling out his name.
Was he jealous? No. He shouldn't be.

The man he was fighting wasn't some rising star who had exploded onto the scene overnight. Frostedge had already carved his name into legend long before Immortal Legacy even existed. He had earned this moment, this devotion, through years of struggle. He deserved this level of support.
Brando, the caster, let out an amused chuckle as he watched the scene unfold.

"Man, listen to that crowd! If you didn't know better, you'd think this was a Frostedge tribute event instead of a grand final! But let's not forget—Broken isn't just some underdog here. He's proven time and time again that he belongs on this stage. The question is... can he shake off the pressure of this overwhelming crowd support and stay locked in?"
"One thing's for sure—this match is far from over."
Until—
Broken heard it. Faintly at first.
"BROKEN! BROKEN! BROKEN!"
What was that? Were people... chanting his name?
He glanced at the massive transparent screens surrounding the battlefield and saw them—people rising from their seats, calling out for him!
Was this real? They were supporting Broken?! But why?
On the screens, he spotted familiar faces—his guildmates, players he had fought against in previous matches, and even an entire row of people shouting his name with their fists raised high.
He wasn't alone. He had his own supporters now.
It might not have been as overwhelming as the wave of cheers Frostedge received, but... was that even true?
Maylon, Euna, Freya, London, and the others were all there, their voices joining together as they roared his name with unshaken determination.
And wait—why did it suddenly sound just as loud?
No way. This wasn't possible, was it?
Brando's voice came through the broadcast, filled with excitement.

"Oh-ho-ho, would you listen to that!? First, it was Frostedge's name shaking the stadium, and now—Broken's getting just as much love! This place is split right down the middle! Two legends, two warriors, and one grand final—
"This is proof that both of them belong on this stage!"

The camera refocused on the two players, both poised to continue their battle. Their eyes locked with unwavering intensity, revealing their absolute focus. They were fully immersed in this fight, pushing themselves to the limit, showing immense respect for one another, yet doing everything in their power to claim victory. This was an all-out war.
The battle resumed!

Once again, Frostedge unleashed a devastating sequence of skills, starting with a massive ice meteor crashing into the arena, shaking the stadium down to its core. Then, as if that wasn't enough, the entire battlefield became encased in ice, transforming into his domain—a frozen throne under his complete control.
Broken was under relentless pressure.
The onslaught came from all directions—environmental hazards, the massive ice dome above raining shards upon him, and, of course, Frostedge himself, attacking with a brutal yet flawless precision.

They continued to exchange spectacular skill clashes, their attacks colliding in explosions so massive they left the audience in awe. Every time another burst of power shook the battlefield, countless players watching could only comment in disbelief—
"What have I even been doing in this game? How are these two even real?"
And then...
Something no one saw coming happened.
A towering ethereal figure suddenly materialized behind Broken—a warrior clad in heavy black and gold armor, wielding a massive greatsword that radiated overwhelming power.
"GOLDEN PARAGON!"
Brando screamed into the mic, his voice filled with shock and excitement.
Euna sat up straight, eyes wide. "Broken's already using it? Is this really the right moment for Golden Paragon!?"
Because those who truly understood what this meant knew one undeniable fact—
Golden Paragon could only be activated in the most desperate situations, when there was no other way out.
Because once the duration ended...
Broken would lose everything.
And he wouldn't be able to fight again.

chapters.title: Chapter 827: Shadows and Ice
paragraphs: Divine Favor Gauge.

This was the core mechanic behind activating Golden Paragon. The gauge would steadily deplete over time, and if it ever reached 0%, Golden Paragon would expire—immediately rendering Broken unable to use any skills and imposing several severe penalties for 48 hours.
However, the gauge could be sustained.

As long as Broken continued dealing damage, healing, or eliminating his enemies, the duration of Golden Paragon would persist. That was why, with the immense regeneration provided by Gaia and the sustained damage Broken was constantly receiving, he could prolong his Golden Paragon state for much longer.
Unless...
Frostedge stopped attacking him entirely.
If that happened, Broken would slowly lose his Golden Paragon—a dangerous gamble that could shift the entire fight.
But did Frostedge fully understand the conditions of Golden Paragon?

Meanwhile, in this state, Broken wasn't just powerful—he was on an entirely different level. His stats skyrocketed. Strength, Constitution, and Agility increased by 150%. Intelligence increased by 75%. Attack power boosted by 20%. Movement speed enhanced by 15%.
And that wasn't all.
Golden Paragon wasn't just a stat boost—it came with its own set of unique and terrifying skills.
This wasn't some ordinary buff.
This was a game-changing transformation.

The moment Broken activated Golden Paragon, everything changed. He could finally keep up with Frostedge, who had been relentlessly dodging and avoiding direct clashes. Now, they were fully engaged in a head-to-head battle, exchanging devastating blows with incredible skill.

Massive ice swords rained down toward Broken, followed by an endless barrage of ice shards. Frostedge's speed, combined with his frozen abilities, made the entire battlefield feel like it was under his absolute control.
The fight had escalated to an entirely new level of intensity.

Watching Frostedge attack without hesitation, it became clear—he didn't fully understand the hidden mechanics behind Golden Paragon. This ability was unique, possessed only by Broken and Alora, and its details were largely unknown to most players.
After all, Golden Paragon had previously belonged only to the ruler of Dissidia Kingdom and was only ever used in the most desperate of circumstances.
Brando, sitting beside Paul, was practically buzzing with excitement as he analyzed the ongoing battle.
"Is this the move that will bring Broken to victory? What do you think, Paul?"
Paul gave a small, knowing smile before responding.

"Broken is fighting against a ticking time bomb. Once the duration of his spirit skills and Golden Paragon runs out, it's over for him. So we can safely say that within the next two minutes, this fight will be decided. Either Broken defeats Frostedge before time runs out, or the duration expires, and he's completely out of the match."
"On the other hand, I'm sure Frostedge has prepared for this. With his incredible skill set, I have no doubt he has the means to survive just long enough to turn the tables!"
Brando's voice exploded with excitement, fueling the energy of the crowd.
"OHHH, YOU HEARD THAT, EVERYONE! TWO MINUTES! THAT'S ALL WE HAVE LEFT TO SEE HOW THIS LEGENDARY SHOWDOWN ENDS! WILL BROKEN BREAK THROUGH, OR WILL FROSTEDGE OUTLAST HIM!?"
"NO MORE HOLDING BACK! NO MORE SECOND CHANCES! THIS. IS. IT!"
Euna, sitting beside Maylon, couldn't hide the concern on her face as she turned to him.
"What do you think, Maylon?" she asked, her voice tinged with worry.
Maylon gave a small, knowing smile before answering.
"Not yet... Broken hasn't used everything he has.
Euna frowned. "But... would he really reveal something he was never meant to show in front of this many people? Isn't that too risky?"
Maylon shook his head.
"I'm sure Broken has already thought this through. He must have a plan to handle it. And the key lies in—"
Their eyes flicked back to the screen, where one particular figure had yet to make a move in this fight.
Euna's breath hitched as she muttered under her breath.
"Pawpaw...?"
Maylon's smile widened slightly.
"Yes."
[Crimson Eclipse (Ultimate Skill) activated!]
Just as Frostedge and Broken clashed beneath the brutal snowstorm, the entire arena was suddenly engulfed in darkness. Gasps filled the stadium—what was happening!?

It was as if night had descended in an instant. Thick shadow tendrils stretched across the battlefield, consuming everything in their path. At the center of it all, Broken's body was completely wrapped in dense, shifting shadows, making his true form nearly invisible. Only the vague outline of his figure remained, shrouded in pure darkness.
This was Pawpaw's ultimate skill—Crimson Eclipse.

For the next sixty seconds, this ability would wreak havoc on the battlefield, drastically reducing the opponent's vision and movement speed by 30%. An overwhelming skill that could change the tide of battle in an instant.

The moment Crimson Eclipse was cast, every spectator leaned forward, eyes locked onto the screen. The only thing truly visible in that darkness was the golden glow of Broken's Golden Paragon, trailing behind him like a ghostly beacon as he launched attack after attack.
The battle had reached a point where no one could look away. The tension was unbearable.

The effects of the skill became immediately apparent. Frostedge, now struggling to keep up, was being hit repeatedly from unseen angles. His health dropped dangerously low multiple times, only to recover at a rapid pace.
Because of course—Frostedge wasn't one to go down so easily.
He had his own ways of ensuring he wouldn't be taken out without a fight.

The moment Infernal Mirage Weapon Cosmetic was equipped, Broken's entire presence became even more menacing. His spear, now wreathed in flickering black flames, clashed violently against the ice-infused attacks of Frostedge. The sheer contrast between fire and ice illuminated the battlefield in a breathtaking display of power.
He fought with pure brutality, exchanging relentless spear and sword strikes with his opponent. Every movement was precise, every attack devastating—yet despite this, Frostedge still refused to fall.
Until...
In the midst of their high-intensity clash, something changed.
Suddenly, Broken's movements became impossibly fast—faster than anything he had shown before. His dashes, his strikes, his very presence became an overwhelming storm of darkness.
Frostedge's expression shifted, his confidence shaken.
[Eternal Flame - Grim Reaper (Conditional Active Skill) activated!]
Gasps rippled through the audience as the realization sank in.
Broken had entered his Eternal Form.

The surrounding darkness and shadows now fully concealed his true form, making it nearly impossible to track his movements. The only thing visible was the relentless barrage of burning spear strikes cutting through the void.
"What the hell is this!?"
"His speed just TRIPLED! How is Frostedge supposed to counter that!?"
"This isn't just an ultimate move anymore—this is straight-up terrifying!"
"I thought Broken was already going all-out—but he's still pushing beyond that! How many trump cards does he have!?"

Suddenly, the shadows surrounding Broken thickened, swirling and expanding until they consumed the battlefield entirely. Even Frostedge, who had been visible just moments ago, was swallowed by the abyss.
[Soul Blast (Conditional Active Skill) activated!]
A deep, pulsing energy filled the air as Broken switched his weapon—his spear vanished, replaced by the ominous form of The Soul Drainer scythe.
The darkness trembled.
Then—BOOM!

A massive explosion of pure shadow erupted from Broken's form, tendrils of darkness surging outward like a violent tidal wave. The force of the blast sent shockwaves across the arena, warping the air itself as if reality had momentarily cracked under its weight. The entire stage trembled, and for a brief moment, the battlefield became a void of absolute chaos.
Realizing the danger, Frostedge reacted in an instant.

Layer upon layer of thick ice walls materialized around him, encasing his body in a protective fortress of frost. The towering frozen barriers stacked rapidly, one after another, forming an impenetrable cocoon meant to withstand whatever devastating force was coming next.
But then—BOOM!
Another eruption!

A deafening shockwave tore through the darkness, shattering the ground beneath them. The sheer impact of Soul Blast collided with Frostedge's ice defenses, sending cracks splintering through the massive walls.
The entire battlefield became an unreadable chaos of black and blue—shadows against ice, destruction clashing against resilience.
And in the middle of it all, no one could see what was happening.
The audience held their breath.
Then—
Brando's voice erupted in sheer hysteria.
"WHAT IN THE ACTUAL HELL JUST HAPPENED!? I CAN'T SEE A DAMN THING—DID BROKEN JUST OBLITERATE FROSTEDGE!?"
All eyes were locked onto the screen, anticipation at its peak. The battlefield was still engulfed in swirling darkness, but then—finally—something changed.
A single moment of clarity.
And there it was.
For the first time in this entire battle, Frostedge's health bar plummeted.
From near-full... to dangerously low!

For the next sixty seconds, this ability would wreak havoc on the battlefield, drastically reducing the opponent's vision and movement speed by 30%.
An overwhelming skill that could change the tide of battle in an instant.
The moment Crimson Eclipse was cast, every spectator leaned forward, eyes locked onto the screen.
The only thing truly visible in that darkness was the golden glow of Broken's Golden Paragon, trailing behind him like a ghostly beacon as he launched attack after attack.
The battle had reached a point where no one could look away.
The tension was unbearable.
The effects of the skill became immediately apparent.
Frostedge, now struggling to keep up, was being hit repeatedly from unseen angles.
His health dropped dangerously low multiple times, only to recover at a rapid pace.
Because of course—Frostedge wasn't one to go down so easily.
He had his own ways of ensuring he wouldn't be taken out without a fight.
The moment Infernal Mirage Weapon Cosmetic was equipped, Broken's entire presence became even more menacing.
His spear, now wreathed in flickering black flames, clashed violently against the ice-infused attacks of Frostedge.
The sheer contrast between fire and ice illuminated the battlefield in a breathtaking display of power.
He fought with pure brutality, exchanging relentless spear and sword strikes with his opponent.
Every movement was precise, every attack devastating—yet despite this, Frostedge still refused to fall.
Until...
In the midst of their high-intensity clash, something changed.
Suddenly, Broken's movements became impossibly fast—faster than anything he had shown before.
His dashes, his strikes, his very presence became an overwhelming storm of darkness.
Frostedge's expression shifted, his confidence shaken.
[Eternal Flame - Grim Reaper (Conditional Active Skill) activated!]
Gasps rippled through the audience as the realization sank in.
Broken had entered his Eternal Form.
The surrounding darkness and shadows now fully concealed his true form, making it nearly impossible to track his movements.
The only thing visible was the relentless barrage of burning spear strikes cutting through the void.
"What the hell is this!?"
"His speed just TRIPLED!
How is Frostedge supposed to counter that!?"
"This isn't just an ultimate move anymore—this is straight-up terrifying!"
"I thought Broken was already going all-out—but he's still pushing beyond that!
How many trump cards does he have!?"
Suddenly, the shadows surrounding Broken thickened, swirling and expanding until they consumed the battlefield entirely.
Even Frostedge, who had been visible just moments ago, was swallowed by the abyss.
[Soul Blast (Conditional Active Skill) activated!]
A deep, pulsing energy filled the air as Broken switched his weapon—his spear vanished, replaced by the ominous form of The Soul Drainer scythe.
The darkness trembled.
Then—BOOM!
A massive explosion of pure shadow erupted from Broken's form, tendrils of darkness surging outward like a violent tidal wave.
The force of the blast sent shockwaves across the arena, warping the air itself as if reality had momentarily cracked under its weight.
The entire stage trembled, and for a brief moment, the battlefield became a void of absolute chaos.
Realizing the danger, Frostedge reacted in an instant.
Layer upon layer of thick ice walls materialized around him, encasing his body in a protective fortress of frost.
The towering frozen barriers stacked rapidly, one after another, forming an impenetrable cocoon meant to withstand whatever devastating force was coming next.
But then—BOOM!
Another eruption!
A deafening shockwave tore through the darkness, shattering the ground beneath them.
The sheer impact of Soul Blast collided with Frostedge's ice defenses, sending cracks splintering through the massive walls.
The entire battlefield became an unreadable chaos of black and blue—shadows against ice, destruction clashing against resilience.
And in the middle of it all, no one could see what was happening.
The audience held their breath.
Then—
Brando's voice erupted in sheer hysteria.
"WHAT IN THE ACTUAL HELL JUST HAPPENED!?
I CAN'T SEE A DAMN THING—DID BROKEN JUST OBLITERATE FROSTEDGE!?"
All eyes were locked onto the screen, anticipation at its peak.
The battlefield was still engulfed in swirling darkness, but then—finally—something changed.
A single moment of clarity.
And there it was.
For the first time in this entire battle, Frostedge's health bar plummeted.
From near-full... to dangerously low!

chapters.title: Chapter 828: Who Will Stand Last?
paragraphs: Golden Paragon had a maximum activation time of five minutes.
No matter how well Broken had managed to sustain the gauge during the fight, the moment the timer reached its limit, he would inevitably lose the Avatar.
And so, as the battlefield slowly settled, the suffocating darkness faded, replaced by light once more. The towering presence of Golden Paragon behind Broken flickered—then vanished completely.
One by one, the Gaia Beasts dissipated. Even Gaia herself, who had stood beside Broken, disappeared into nothingness.
The battle had taken everything from him.
Now, Golden Paragon entered its 48-hour cooldown, a brutal penalty that rendered Broken completely unable to use any of his skills. At this moment, he was incapable of continuing the fight.
But he wasn't the only one.

As the effects of the battle unraveled, another shift became clear—the layers of ice coating the battlefield were fading at a rapid pace. The heavy snowfall had stopped. The arena, once dominated by an icy fortress, was now melting away.
It wasn't just Broken who had reached his limit.
Across from him, Frostedge had collapsed to one knee, his sword dug into the ground, struggling to hold himself upright.
He had taken massive damage.
His health, which had previously recovered at terrifying speed, wasn't regenerating anymore. His Frost Titan—completely gone. His once-dominant ice domain had crumbled into nothingness.
The fight had drained both of them.
But...
If Frostedge could still stand... if he could launch just one more attack...
Then Broken wouldn't be able to stop it.
The entire stadium fell into an eerie silence, every single person holding their breath.
This was it.
The final moment.
The battle's outcome rested on what happened next.
Brando's voice trembled with excitement, barely able to contain the sheer weight of the moment.
"This... this is beyond anything we could've imagined!"
"Broken's Golden Paragon is gone!"
"But look at Frostedge! The Frost King himself is down on one knee! His health isn't recovering! His legendary endurance—failing!"
"Both players have thrown everything into this fight. They've pushed beyond their limits, beyond what should've been possible!"
"And now—it all comes down to one final moment!"
"WHO—IS—GOING TO FALL FIRST!?"
Frostedge let his sword drop to the ground. Slowly, he lifted his head, and for the first time since the battle began, a faint smile crossed his face.
He stood up.
His eyes met Broken's.
They took slow steps toward each other, closing the distance. No words were exchanged, yet somehow, they understood each other completely.

The price of Frostedge's defeat was clear now. His incredible skill set—designed to control Broken's movements while dealing devastating damage over time—had come at a cost. No one could endure a fight against Frostedge without an immense recovery rate like the one Broken had with Gaia's support.
But at the same time, Frostedge's defense had made him nearly untouchable. Very few could have simultaneously withstood his onslaught and still forced him this close to his limit.
They stood face to face for a moment, neither speaking.
Then, Frostedge broke the silence.
"That last move..." he murmured, his voice just loud enough for Broken to hear. He didn't elaborate.
He should be understood why Broken had concealed his Eternal Flame Form from the cameras.
"Next time, I'll have a counter for that too." His smile widened.
Broken chuckled. "That was a battle I'll never forget."
They exchanged a small nod of respect—then bowed to each other.
And just like that, Frostedge raised both hands in the air.
He had surrendered.
BROKEN HAD WON!
The stadium erupted.
A deafening roar of cheers and shouts filled the air as Brando screamed into his mic, his voice barely audible over the madness.
"BROKEN TAKES IT! HE TAKES IT! AFTER ONE OF THE GREATEST BATTLES IN IMMORTAL LEGACY HISTORY—BROKEN IS THE CHAMPION!"
The crowd was on its feet, roaring his name.
"WHAT A FIGHT! WHAT A FINAL! THIS—WILL BE TALKED ABOUT FOR YEARS TO COME!"

Some time later, both players emerged from their capsule devices, greeted by an explosion of cheers. The stadium was still buzzing with excitement, the energy refusing to fade even after the battle had ended.
Leon barely had time to take a breath before he saw Han Feng being assisted out of his capsule. Without hesitation, he moved toward him.
Han Feng, despite everything, there was no sign of disappointment on his face. Instead, as they were side by side, he looked at Leon with an expression of pure respect.
Meanwhile, the host was practically screaming into the mic, hyping up the historic victory.
Then, as the crowd's chanting grew louder, Leon was handed the championship trophy.
The moment he lifted it high into the air—
The stadium erupted.
Deafening roars filled the air, echoing in waves of pure celebration. The cheers, the flashing lights, the sea of people chanting his name—it all crashed over him at once.
Leon let out a deep breath, his chest rising and falling as if the weight of it all had finally settled in.
He had won.
Who would have thought?
That was a battle beyond anything he had ever experienced.

To secure this victory, he had no choice but to activate Eternal Flame, a skill with severe conditions. The ability demanded him to absorb the souls of his fallen enemies before it could even be triggered—something that could only occur under exceptionally rare circumstances.
It was a one-time-only move.
And he had used it.
But now, as he stood there holding the championship trophy, every ounce of effort, every risk, every desperate moment—it had all been worth it.
And for this achievement, Leon was officially crowned MVP of the Eternal Challenge, the very first official tournament hosted by the game's creators.
Leon stood in front of Han Feng, who was seated in his wheelchair, preparing to enter the waiting car where his assistant stood by.
For a moment, they simply looked at each other.
Then, Han Feng spoke first.
"There are still a lot of things I want to pursue in this game."
Leon remained silent, listening.
"And... I have no intention of joining any guild."
Guild? Why was Han Feng bringing this up?
Han Feng said with a small smile. "It's just out of respect. Before anyone tries to recruit me, I'd rather explain my position first."
Leon raised an eyebrow. "You know I was about to invite you to join Vensalor's Guild?"
Han Feng chuckled and shook his head. "That would definitely be an amazing offer."
It was exactly what Leon's guildmates had been discussing earlier. Recruiting Frostedge would be a massive victory for them. A player of his caliber would be a game-changer for any guild.
But Leon also understood something else.
Han Feng had his own path, his own ambitions, and forcing him into a guild would only take away that freedom.

So, when Han Feng made his stance clear, it wasn't just a refusal—it was a sign of respect. He had spoken first, acknowledging what was coming, so that Leon wouldn't have to extend an offer just to hear a rejection.
"I hope we meet again in the game," Han Feng continued. "And surely, at next year's Duel of Champions."
Leon nodded slowly. "I'll be waiting to defeat you again."
Han Feng smirked. "I won't make it easy for you next time."
They shook hands, the rivalry between them solidified.
They didn't need to be guildmates to be competitors.
And maybe... they didn't need to be in the same guild to be friends, either.

chapters.title: Chapter 829: The Champion’s Feast
paragraphs: Another grand party.
Vensalor Guild, along with their allied guilds, had arranged an extravagant celebration—one last night of revelry before the end of their gathering on the Eternal Challenge.

As always, they had rented out an entire luxury restaurant, making it an exclusive gathering just for them. Live music played in the background, the finest food was served without restraint, and the atmosphere was electric with victory.
Glasses were raised.
"TO BROKEN!"

The guild erupted into cheers, chanting his name. Leon—Broken—had not only won the tournament but had also been crowned MVP of the entire competition. It was a massive win for him and for the Vensalor Guild as a whole.

Even beyond the party, his victory was still being discussed everywhere. Online forums buzzed with speculation about what had truly happened in the final moments of his battle against Frostedge. Theories ranged wildly, with many suspecting it had something to do with his Demon Beast, but no one knew for certain.
Regardless, this win had changed things for him.
Not only had he secured prize money, but thanks to Ronal and the Destroyer team, multiple sponsorship deals had come his way.
The total amount when he saw it?
Unbelievable.
With just a little more, he would be able to fully realize something he had been discussing with Freya for some time now—his own place.
In fact, Freya had already been scouting potential properties for him. She had found several promising options and had taken charge of the negotiations entirely.
And now? The finishing touches were already being worked on. In three to four months, he would be moving into his new home.
Though... calling it a home felt a bit strange. Because the building he had chosen wasn't just an apartment or a house—it was a 20-story building at the edge of the city.
It was slightly away from the bustling center, but still close enough to everything important. The interior design and room layouts were still a work in progress, but he already had a vision for it.
A gaming floor, equipped with multiple capsule devices so more people could play alongside him.
A training room, built specifically for physical workouts and reflex training.
And on the ground floor—a café. Not really for business, but a personal space where he could sit, relax, and unwind whenever he needed a break.
It was all coming together.
And then, London—with his usual over-the-top confidence—dropped another surprise.
"I'm buying a building near yours," he declared casually. "Gotta have a place to crash when I visit the city."
Leon barely had time to react before Euna and Booyoung jumped in as well.
"Actually, we're thinking of getting a place nearby too," Euna added.
And then, one by one, more of their friends started chiming in.
Apparently, several of them were now considering moving close to Leon as well.
Leon stared at them, baffled.
This bunch of rich people...
Was buying an entire building really such an easy decision for them?
They were literally discussing multi-million-dollar purchases in between bites of expensive steak and rounds of laughter.
Leon could only shake his head.
This... was absolutely insane.
As soon as the dinner party ended, Leon made his way to a nearby café, where someone was already waiting for him.
It was Olivia.
He hadn't had the chance to talk to her much lately, having spent most of his time at the tournament venue or logged into the game. Now, finally, they had a moment.
"Congrats! You're famous now," Olivia said casually, her straight black hair falling neatly over her shoulders as she smirked at him.
Leon leaned back in his chair. "Have you considered joining my alliance yet?" he asked just as smoothly.
Olivia raised an eyebrow. "When did I ever say I'd do that, huh? Just because you're a big shot now, you think you can convince me?"
"I don't think I've changed at all, you know that."
Olivia let out a small laugh, tilting her head down slightly as her laughter blended into the café's background music.
"So... why did you ask me to meet you tonight?" she asked, eyes flicking back up to him. "Have you started missing me that much?"
Leon smiled and nodded. "I miss exploring Hell with you."
"That was fun..." Olivia mused, then leaned forward slightly. "Interested in going back?"
"Will you tell me how to get there on my own?"
She paused, considering his words.

"What are you looking for in Hell?" Olivia's tone shifted slightly, becoming more serious. "You do realize you're famous down there too now, right? Ever since the King of Hell revealed himself in the Dissidia Kingdom, you think the demons won't come after you if you step into their domain?"
Leon dodged the question.
"So, are you going to tell me how to get there or not?"
Olivia tapped her finger against the table, thinking.

"That's a tough one... That information is exclusive to my guild, so I can't give you an answer right now. But—" she paused before smirking, "—if you want to visit, we can always schedule a trip together."
Then, her gaze sharpened slightly. "What exactly are you planning to do there?"
Leon had his reasons.
First, he needed to expand his search for Ivana. The sudden appearance of the Demon Hand near the dragonkin had happened right after Ivana regained her Dragon Form. Something about it felt... off.
He had a hunch.
A feeling that High Elves and Demons were connected in some way.
And second—
He wanted to hunt more Named Demons.
Every Named Demon he killed unlocked new abilities in his Demon Shift. Who knew what kind of skills he could gain if he took down even more of them?
"Kill more Named Demons," he answered simply.
Olivia's lips curled into a smirk.
"Interesting," she murmured.
Olivia fell silent for a moment, as if carefully choosing her words. There was something on her mind—something she was debating whether or not to share.
"I have a quest... just like I mentioned before."
Leon immediately recalled what she had told him in the past.
Olivia had a major quest, one that promised something incredibly valuable—most likely a Legendary-grade class. But she had never shared the full details with him.
"And that quest..." She hesitated again before continuing. "Requires me to visit Hell more frequently."
Leon raised an eyebrow. "You need to kill something?"
"Yes..." Olivia admitted. "But I can't tell you what."
Leon nodded, not pushing for more.
Some things were better left undisclosed—at least for now.
That night, their conversation ended there.

As the night deepened, Leon drove back to his place. Sitting in the passenger seat beside him was Freya, who was staying at the same hotel for the night. It was the perfect chance to discuss something that had been on his mind—Ivana.
He had already gone over this with Maylon, and now, it was time to hear Freya's thoughts.
And, as expected, her intuition led her to the same conclusion.
"For some reason, I feel like Vallrick has the answers."
Leon's grip on the wheel tightened slightly.
Vallrick.
That mysterious man... the one who turned out to be the Pride Champion.
Could his quest actually be connected to all of this?
After all, why had he been given the mission to hunt down The Demon Hand?

Olivia fell silent for a moment, as if carefully choosing her words.
There was something on her mind—something she was debating whether or not to share.
"I have a quest... just like I mentioned before."
Leon immediately recalled what she had told him in the past.
Olivia had a major quest, one that promised something incredibly valuable—most likely a Legendary-grade class.
But she had never shared the full details with him.
"And that quest..." She hesitated again before continuing.
"Requires me to visit Hell more frequently."
Leon raised an eyebrow.
"You need to kill something?"
"Yes..." Olivia admitted.
"But I can't tell you what."
Leon nodded, not pushing for more.
Some things were better left undisclosed—at least for now.
That night, their conversation ended there.
As the night deepened, Leon drove back to his place.
Sitting in the passenger seat beside him was Freya, who was staying at the same hotel for the night.
It was the perfect chance to discuss something that had been on his mind—Ivana.
He had already gone over this with Maylon, and now, it was time to hear Freya's thoughts.
And, as expected, her intuition led her to the same conclusion.
"For some reason, I feel like Vallrick has the answers."
Leon's grip on the wheel tightened slightly.
Vallrick.
That mysterious man... the one who turned out to be the Pride Champion.
Could his quest actually be connected to all of this?
After all, why had he been given the mission to hunt down The Demon Hand?

chapters.title: Chapter 830: Another Death Mission?
paragraphs: Broken was back in Immortal Legacy.
He had left the Dragonkin territory, taking a brief detour to a nearby town where he rented an inn to stay for a day or two.
Now, with some quiet time, he focused on analyzing the two Legendary-grade items he had obtained from his battle against The Demon Hand.
One was a bracelet, and the other a ring.

Reading through their descriptions again, he realized the bracelet had an incredible effect—it increased the amount of experience gained based on the level difference between the wearer and their target. The greater the gap, the higher the bonus.
A fantastic item.
Unfortunately... it was useless to him, experience points meant nothing. So, without hesitation, he handed the bracelet over to SexyGrill, knowing it would be far more valuable for her.
As for the ring, its effect was a 10% boost to party-wide buffs.
Not bad, but again... not ideal for him.
Buff-based effects weren't something he actively relied on, so he figured it would be better suited for SexyBloom. Because she was a dedicated support player.

Not bad. At the very least, he had managed to strengthen two people who had contributed a lot to him—especially when SexyGrill and SexyBloom combined their skills when the Lust Divine Blessing activated.
As for himself, he had acquired two Monster Cores.
One had already been consumed by Pawpaw, while the other remained unused.
For now, he was holding onto it.
Unless Pawpaw was about to unlock a transformation, he wasn't in a rush to use it just yet.
Broken sat in a tavern, quietly enjoying his lunch.
Seated across from him was SexyGrill.
And next to her...
Broken sighed.
It was none other than Vallrick—the mysterious Pride Champion who had suddenly barged into his life, bringing nothing but weird and unexpected developments along with him.
Right now, both Broken and SexyGrill were staring at him, their expressions laced with interrogation-level intensity.
Meanwhile, Vallrick, grinning awkwardly, scratched the back of his head.
"Why do I feel like I'm being interrogated?" he muttered.
Silence. With no response from either of them, he quickly tried to shift the subject.
"A-And yes! Broken—congrats on becoming MVP of the first-ever Eternal Challenge! That was truly incredible—"
He kept talking, clearly hoping to defuse the tension.
But when neither Broken nor SexyGrill reacted, he finally stopped.
Awkward silence.
Vallrick hesitated before asking, "Did I... do something wrong?"
"Not exactly," Broken replied. "It's more like... are you finally going to tell me more about your 'incredible, high-ranking' quest? Have you gotten the reward yet?"
At that, Vallrick's awkward smile returned.
"Actually... I need your help again, Broken."
Both Broken and SexyGrill immediately narrowed their eyes.
Vallrick coughed.
"Because there is another Legendary-grade monster."
Broken blinked.
"Another Legendary-grade monster?" he repeated.
So this wasn't just a one-time thing. His quest wasn't about hunting one monster.
There were more.
And who knew how many were still waiting ahead?
"Is this still part of the same quest?" Broken asked, his tone flat.
Vallrick let out a nervous laugh. "Ah... hehe, yes. It's the same quest. And from the looks of it, this one won't be easy.
Before Broken could respond, SexyGrill chimed in with a smirk.
"Oh, right, because the last one was sooo easy. You only had to use your skill once."
Her sarcasm was razor-sharp.
Vallrick immediately put on a dramatic, devastated expression, his lips quivering as if he were on the verge of tears.
"I lost so many levels because of that move... That one hit cost me months of grinding."
Broken ignored the whining.
"Alright. What kind of monster are we dealing with this time? And where is it?"
The sudden shift in focus made Vallrick pause. Then, his entire face lit up. Like a wish had just been granted.

Without wasting a second, he quickly shared a map from his system, showing it to both Broken and SexyGrill. As they studied it, Vallrick eagerly zoomed in and out the maps a few times, before finally pointing at a very specific location.
Both Broken and SexyGrill squinted at the spot.
Because that place...
It was—
"Here." Vallrick tapped the screen, still smiling awkwardly.
"Uhm... heh... Well, the monster is in the middle of nowhere."
Then, with the same shameless grin, he added—
"So, I figured we could take a little vacation to the ocean while we handle this mission!"
The location Vallrick pointed to...
It was the same spot Ronan—the leader of Vensalor Outriders Guild—had shown Broken before.
The exact location where Ronan claimed to have spotted a Legendary-grade monster.
And that wasn't all.
This was also near the area SexyGrill had previously mentioned—the potential location of the floating island of the Forest Elves of Vensalor Kingdom.
Broken paused, processing the coincidence.
Across from him, SexyGrill's expression shifted—she should be thinking the same thing.
Was this really just a coincidence?
Or could this somehow be connected to the High Elf Queen?
Surely not... right?
And yet—
Right now, Broken was completely out of leads on where to search for Ivana.
But this—this was a new lead.
Because this very location was where he and SexyGrill had already planned to begin their expedition in search of the floating island.
And now... Vallrick's quest just happened to lead them there as well.
The timing. The place. The target.
It was too connected.
Somehow, Broken couldn't shake the feeling that this Legendary monster was tied to the Forest Elves of Vensalor Kingdom in some way.
And if that was the case—
He could merge both objectives into one expedition.
A perfect opportunity.
Not only would they be searching for the floating island, but Vallrick's abilities would also make fighting a high-level monster significantly easier.
But first—one question lingered in Broken's mind.
His gaze sharpened as he turned back to Vallrick.
"Can you do it again?" he asked. "Lower this monster's level by 20, just like last time?"
Vallrick responded with yet another awkward smile.
"Hehe... Broken... Yes, I can. But before that, I need to recover my lost 20 levels. Only then can I fulfill the condition again."
He fell silent after that, as if bracing himself for their reactions.
Broken nodded slightly, already expecting the answer. Without wasting time, he contacted Ronan and Mizuki, informing them about the situation.
SexyGrill, after considering the plan, agreed to help power-level Vallrick. With the right team and enough support, regaining those levels shouldn't be too difficult.
With that decided, Broken concluded the discussion.
"Ronan is waiting in the port city. I'm sure he has an efficient grinding spot prepared. Grill, you'll go with him."
Then, he glanced at Vallrick.
"You, SexyGrill, and SexyBloom will head there using my Golem Carriage. Once you're ready, we'll regroup."
Vallrick frowned, looking confused.
"Wait... you're not coming with us?"
He sounded genuinely puzzled. The only route to Dissidia Kingdom was through the port city, which meant traveling together, boarding the same ship, and crossing the strait between continents.
So why was Broken taking a different route?
Broken simply smiled.
Then, he turned to SexyGrill.
She caught his glance, then grinned mischievously before clapping a hand on Vallrick's shoulder.
"Alright, just leave this useless guy to me," SexyGrill teased, giggling.
"No..." Vallrick quickly protested. "I'm not completely useless. I mean... I actually have a mechanic that lets me gain experience faster than normal players."
SexyGrill abruptly turned to him, eyes narrowing.
"What?"
"Now I'm actually jealous of your blessing."
"But you're a Divine Champion too, aren't you?"
"Yes, but my blessing is pretty useless for myself." Vallrick sighed dramatically.
Then, as if trying to smooth things over, he added, "I can share my experience buff with you if you want."
SexyGrill froze. "Wait... seriously?"
And just like that, their conversation shifted entirely.
The two of them immediately dived into planning how to power-level Vallrick, strategizing ways to make the most of his unique mechanic.
If everything went smoothly, it would take around one to two months in Yunatea Time—a considerable effort, but one that could be well worth it.
Broken left first.
There was something urgent he needed to take care of. Alora had sent word—she had important news to share, something she insisted on telling him in person.
What could possibly be so critical that she wanted to meet him immediately?
With that thought in mind, Broken activated Moonlight Dimension, stepping through the portal and emerging inside their royal chambers in Dissidia Kingdom.
The room was empty.
But only for a moment.
Just as he took a step forward, the doors swung open. And there—standing in the doorway—was Alora. The person he had missed far more than he would ever admit.
The moment her eyes locked onto his, a bright smile spread across her face.
Without hesitation, she ran straight toward him.
But—
Something was different. And as Broken watched her approach...
He couldn't shake the feeling that something about Alora had changed.

chapters.title: Chapter 831: Alora’s Gift to Broken
paragraphs: Broken caught Alora in his arms as she ran into him, wrapping her arms tightly around him.
He held her close, sinking into the warmth he had missed so much.
For a few moments, they just stayed like that—silent, unmoving—simply savoring the quiet comfort of each other's presence.
Then, softly, she spoke.
"I miss you so much..."
Broken ran his fingers through her long, crimson hair before she finally pulled away.
Leaning down, he gently kissed her forehead.
"I miss you too... so much."
He smiled—but something felt different.
Something about Alora. And then... he noticed it.
The realization hit him the moment she had pressed against him in that embrace.
Stepping back slightly, his eyes lowered—
To her stomach.
Alora followed his gaze, resting a hand over her belly as she smiled.
Even through the elegant gown she wore, it was unmistakable. Her stomach was rounder, larger than normal.
Broken's breath hitched.
"Alora?" he whispered, looking back up at her.
She smiled tenderly and nodded. "Yes... this is our baby."
Broken froze. His mind blanked for a moment, his breath catching in his throat.
His hands moved almost on their own, reaching forward to gently touch her belly.
A baby...?
He could barely process it.
Their baby.
How long had he been away from the capital? How much had changed while he was gone?
He turned to Alora, his voice hoarse.
"How long...?"
She smiled warmly, eyes filled with nothing but love.
"Five months. In another four... we'll meet our child."
Broken exhaled sharply, his emotions colliding all at once—shock, joy, disbelief, overwhelming happiness.
Then—
He laughed.
A bright, full, unrestrained laugh.
He grabbed Alora and pulled her back into his arms, holding her even tighter than before.
"Alora, hahaha—!"
She laughed along with him, their happiness spilling over like treasure newly discovered.
For the first time in a long time, nothing else mattered.
Broken was going to be a father.
And it was Alora—Queen of Dissidia Kingdom—who carried his child.
They continued their conversation while seated on the lavish sofa in the center of the room, positioned near the grand glass window overlooking the kingdom beyond.
Alora leaned against Broken's right arm, resting her head on his shoulder, while he wrapped an arm around her, holding her close.
It had been months since they had last seen each other.
Months since he had left on his expedition, one that had yet to yield the answers he sought.
As they sat together, Broken recounted everything—the challenges, the battles, and the frustrating twists along the way.
Alora listened attentively, occasionally responding with soft laughter, especially when Broken grumbled about Vallrick, the ever-persistent Pride Champion, and the headaches he had caused.
In return, Alora shared the kingdom's progress with him.
The rebuilding efforts were back on track, and things had finally begun to stabilize.
More knights had risen through the ranks.
The economy had recovered.
And to her pleasant surprise, Slumdon—once an abandoned town—had undergone an incredible transformation.

"More people have moved into the city," she said, her voice carrying a note of admiration. "And there are a lot of high-level players settling there now. Even the knights you brought from the capital have grown tremendously. I think Maylock's influence on their progress has been truly remarkable."
She paused for a moment before adding with a small chuckle,
"With so many new residents—forest elves, faeries, beastkin—Slumdon barely even feels like part of Dissidia Kingdom anymore."
After talking for some time, Broken finally decided to bring up one of the reasons he had come to see Alora. He hesitated at first. But once he mentioned it—
Alora immediately straightened, her expression shifting into one of excitement.
"The Dormant Fae Seed?" she repeated, her eyes lighting up. "Hurry, take it out—I want to see what happens!"
She reached forward slightly, eager.
"Broken, it's okay. We don't need to worry about anything... After all, it's something that came from Elaine, isn't it?"
Broken hesitated. Alora was pregnant—would supplying Mana to the seed affect her in any way? After all, it had only reacted in the first place after his marriage to her.
Still uncertain, he pulled out the Dormant Fae Seed and handed it over.
Alora gently took it in her hands, bringing it onto her lap.
Then, she channeled Mana into it. A faint glow pulsed from the seed.
"It's reacting?" Broken asked.
Alora turned to him and nodded.
Curious, Broken took the seed back and tried the same thing.
Nothing.
No response at all.
"Why?" he muttered under his breath.
Alora studied the seed for a moment before speaking.
"Do you think it only reacts to Mana from me?" she mused. "If that's the case... you can leave it here. I'll handle it. Just leave it to me."
Broken hesitated. He wasn't entirely comfortable with the idea, but...
At this moment, there wasn't anything else he could do.
After a brief pause, he finally handed the Dormant Fae Seed over to Alora.
At the very least, he could monitor its progress over the next few weeks while he stayed in the capital, traveling back and forth between there and Slumdon Town.
For the next two days, Broken spent every moment with Alora—something he rarely had the chance to do.
They wandered through the capital, exploring the city and witnessing firsthand how much it had changed under her leadership.
The once-ruined kingdom had thrived. The bustling energy of the capital had fully returned.

It had been five months since the demon invasion, and now, there were barely any visible traces of destruction left. The damage—both structural and in the number of civilian casualties—had been severe, but the recovery had been nothing short of remarkable.
Under Alora's rule, the atmosphere of Dissidia Kingdom had transformed.

She wasn't just supported by the forest elves, who had settled in the capital and contributed to security and stability—she also had the players on her side, particularly the Vensalor Kingdom members, who had taken on key roles in rebuilding the kingdom.
If this progress continued, Dissidia Kingdom could become the first kingdom in history to develop a true balance of power between NPCs and players.
And that was unprecedented.
But of course, not everyone welcomed this change.
There were still nobles and high-ranking officials who did not fully support Alora as Queen.
Thanks to Broken's influence, Maylock's control, and Alora's firm leadership, resistance from the old royal faction had been reduced to a minimum.
For now, these dissenters were monitored closely rather than confronted.
Spies that Broken and Maylock had strategically placed across various major cities ensured that any suspicious movements were immediately reported.

As long as these figures remained under surveillance, it was better than forcing a civil war, which would only weaken Dissidia Kingdom further—especially when its military strength had not yet fully recovered from the deaths of the Imperial Knights, who had once served under the previous king, Elorik.
Then, on the second day, It was time for him to visit Slumdon Town. A place he hadn't set foot in since before the great war in Dissidia Kingdom.
It had been far too long.
He stepped through the Moonlight Gate, emerging into his private office.
The familiar scent of polished wood filled his lungs the moment he entered, a nostalgic reminder of the space he hadn't occupied in a long time.
Just as he took a breath, there was a knock at the door.
Then, a voice he hadn't heard for a while.
"My Lord, have you arrived...?"
Yara.
Broken exhaled slightly before responding.
"Yes, Yara. Come in."

We don't need to worry about anything...
After all, it's something that came from Elaine, isn't it?"
Broken hesitated.
Alora was pregnant—would supplying Mana to the seed affect her in any way?
After all, it had only reacted in the first place after his marriage to her.
Still uncertain, he pulled out the Dormant Fae Seed and handed it over.
Alora gently took it in her hands, bringing it onto her lap.
Then, she channeled Mana into it.
A faint glow pulsed from the seed.
"It's reacting?" Broken asked.
Alora turned to him and nodded.
Curious, Broken took the seed back and tried the same thing.
Nothing.
No response at all.
"Why?" he muttered under his breath.
Alora studied the seed for a moment before speaking.
"Do you think it only reacts to Mana from me?" she mused.
"If that's the case... you can leave it here.
I'll handle it.
Just leave it to me."
Broken hesitated.
He wasn't entirely comfortable with the idea, but...
At this moment, there wasn't anything else he could do.
After a brief pause, he finally handed the Dormant Fae Seed over to Alora.
At the very least, he could monitor its progress over the next few weeks while he stayed in the capital, traveling back and forth between there and Slumdon Town.
For the next two days, Broken spent every moment with Alora—something he rarely had the chance to do.
They wandered through the capital, exploring the city and witnessing firsthand how much it had changed under her leadership.
The once-ruined kingdom had thrived.
The bustling energy of the capital had fully returned.
It had been five months since the demon invasion, and now, there were barely any visible traces of destruction left.
The damage—both structural and in the number of civilian casualties—had been severe, but the recovery had been nothing short of remarkable.
Under Alora's rule, the atmosphere of Dissidia Kingdom had transformed.

She wasn't just supported by the forest elves, who had settled in the capital and contributed to security and stability—she also had the players on her side, particularly the Vensalor Kingdom members, who had taken on key roles in rebuilding the kingdom.
If this progress continued, Dissidia Kingdom could become the first kingdom in history to develop a true balance of power between NPCs and players.
And that was unprecedented.
But of course, not everyone welcomed this change.
There were still nobles and high-ranking officials who did not fully support Alora as Queen.
Thanks to Broken's influence, Maylock's control, and Alora's firm leadership, resistance from the old royal faction had been reduced to a minimum.
For now, these dissenters were monitored closely rather than confronted.
Spies that Broken and Maylock had strategically placed across various major cities ensured that any suspicious movements were immediately reported.

As long as these figures remained under surveillance, it was better than forcing a civil war, which would only weaken Dissidia Kingdom further—especially when its military strength had not yet fully recovered from the deaths of the Imperial Knights, who had once served under the previous king, Elorik.
Then, on the second day, It was time for him to visit Slumdon Town.
A place he hadn't set foot in since before the great war in Dissidia Kingdom.
It had been far too long.
He stepped through the Moonlight Gate, emerging into his private office.
The familiar scent of polished wood filled his lungs the moment he entered, a nostalgic reminder of the space he hadn't occupied in a long time.
Just as he took a breath, there was a knock at the door.
Then, a voice he hadn't heard for a while.
"My Lord, have you arrived...?"
Yara.
Broken exhaled slightly before responding.
"Yes, Yara.
Come in."

chapters.title: Chapter 832: A Ruler’s Silent Return
paragraphs: The door to his office swung open, and in stepped a familiar face—one he hadn't seen in months.
Yara.
The cheerful maid with short, orange hair entered with her usual bright expression.
"My Lord..." she hurried forward, standing before him.
Right behind her, another figure followed—a young elf girl with long blonde hair.
Nimue.
She was Elowen's younger sister.
"Your Majesty, King Broken," Nimue greeted formally, bowing deeply. "Welcome back to Slumdon Town."
Hearing that, Yara suddenly froze, her eyes widening. It seemed she had just realized her mistake.
"My Lord— I mean— Your Majesty! I-I'm so sorry!" Yara panicked, immediately dropping to her knees before Broken.
"Forgive me, I—uh—King—ah—Your Majesty—I forgot—please forgive me! I'm not used to it yet!" she stammered.
Broken chuckled, watching her flustered reaction.
Yara had always been like this—awkward, clumsy, and completely unsure how to act around him.
"Yara, stand up. You don't need to do that. I'm still the same person you've always known."
Yara hesitated, looking up at him before slowly rising to her feet.
Then, as if trying to correct herself, she bowed again.
"Your Majesty, King Broken... welcome back to Slumdon Town. We've all missed you here."
Then, she suddenly froze again.
Her eyes widened as she realized what she had just said.
"Ah! No—wait—I mean—King—uhm—" she stammered, completely panicking.
Broken laughed and placed a hand on her shoulder.
"It's fine. Now, come on—show me around the city. I've missed this place too."
Yara immediately perked up, nodding eagerly.
With that, he stepped out of the room, Yara and Nimue following closely behind.
Broken stepped out of the room, switching his outfit to his standard armor.
To further conceal his identity, he donned his helmet, ensuring that no one in the city would recognize him.
If word got out that Broken was here, it would cause a stir—especially among players and residents.
Most people believed he was still in Dissidia Kingdom's capital, and the fact that he could move between cities so easily was not something he wanted to reveal to anyone outside his trusted circle.
As he walked, he spoke quietly.
"Maylock is in town, isn't he?"
Yara, following closely behind, nodded.
"Yes, King... Lord Maylock is currently training the knights."
Broken, accompanied by Yara and Nimue, made his way downstairs and stepped out of the House of Slumdon, his boots pressing against the stone streets.
The moment he set foot outside, his gaze swept across the revitalized town.
This place—Slumdon Town, once a forgotten settlement in the middle of the desert—had undergone a drastic transformation.
What he saw now was unrecognizable compared to the city he had last visited.
The buildings along the streets were no longer worn-down ruins—they were well-maintained, vibrant, and filled with life.
The town itself, once bleak and dry, now had potted plants and flowers decorating storefronts and walkways, adding a lush green contrast to what had once been a barren landscape.
And then—
The players.
This was the most noticeable change.
Before, players in this town had been few and far between. Now?
They filled the streets, moving with purpose.
And what stood out the most? Their levels. These were not low-level adventurers.
Most of them were at least level 150—a clear sign that Slumdon's surrounding hunting grounds had become valuable leveling hotspots.
With more players and hunters drawn to the area, the local economy had likely seen an enormous boost.
Slumdon had evolved far beyond what it once was.
It was no longer a dying town in the middle of nowhere. It had become a growing hub of power and opportunity.
And yet—
Broken knew the truth. He had done little to make this happen.
The real driving forces behind this transformation were his companions—Freya, Livelywood, Maylock, and the others. Without them, none of this would have happened so quickly.
Broken walked along the edge of the city streets, his presence largely unnoticed.
The residents glanced toward him occasionally—mainly because he was walking alongside Yara and Nimue, both well-known figures in Slumdon Town.
Some people might have wondered about the identity of the armored man accompanying them.
But none of them suspected it was Broken.
Why would they?
The King Consort of Dissidia Kingdom wouldn't just show up unannounced in a town like this—without a grand welcome, without an escort, without any formal notice.
With that disguise, his presence remained a mystery to them all.
Continuing forward, Broken made his way toward the training grounds.
A large open space, surrounded by a wire-mesh fence, allowed onlookers to see inside while keeping the training area enclosed.
Inside, knights were hard at work.
Some practiced their sword techniques under strict instruction, while others engaged in sparring matches, their blades clashing in intense duels.
And overseeing them all—
Maylock. The archer, wearing his signature sunglasses, stood watching the knights with his arms crossed.
Broken stepped through the entrance, making his way directly toward him.
Noticing the approach, Maylock turned slightly, glancing over his shoulder.
Then, he smirked.
"Well, well... the big man arrives."
Broken didn't respond.
Instead, he simply stood beside Maylock, his helmet still concealing his identity, his gamer name hidden.
For now, he remained just another observer.
But—
To Broken's surprise, some of the knights began to notice him.
Their eyes lingered, their movements hesitating.
Then—one of them reacted instantly. A young female knight with short blonde hair—Anna.
She immediately ran toward Maylock and Broken, her expression lighting up with recognition.
And she wasn't alone.
The moment she moved, the others followed. Igor. Karl. Elowen. Even Mira, the bunny beastkin.
They all rushed over, their training forgotten in an instant.
Anna reached them first.
Her expression filled with excitement, she stood firmly, then brought her right fist over her heart, bowing slightly.
"Your Majesty, King Broken!"
The others quickly followed suit, standing tall as they performed the formal Dissidia Knight's salute.
Maylock chuckled. "Looks like you couldn't hide your identity from them, Broken."
The surrounding knights who had been training a moment ago now looked on in confusion.
Why had Anna, of all people, suddenly addressed this armored stranger as Your Majesty?
But as they watched the higher-ranking knights—Anna, Igor, Karl, Elowen, and Mira—all showing formal respect, realization spread like wildfire.
One by one, the knights stopped their training, turning their full attention toward him.
Then, without hesitation, they gathered and formed proper ranks, standing in an orderly line.
Broken smiled.
Slowly, he reached up and removed his helmet, revealing his face.
A moment of silence—
Then, the confirmation hit them all at once.
King Broken was here.
And in perfect unison, the entire squad of knights stepped forward and struck their official salute—
A fist over the heart, backs straight, heads bowed slightly in unwavering respect.
"WELCOME BACK, YOUR MAJESTY!" they called out in one voice.
One thing immediately stood out to Broken.
The number of knights.
What had once been a small, struggling force had now grown into the hundreds.
Based on Maylock's reports, their numbers had already surpassed 400.
That kind of growth—in such a short time—was incredible.
His gaze swept over the gathered knights, noting their discipline and presence.
But there was one thing he was especially curious about.
The progress of his strongest knights—
His commanders.

chapters.title: Chapter 833: Valantar City’s Power Play
paragraphs: Standing before Broken were his Knight Commanders—Igor, Orion, Elowen, and Mira.
One name, however, was missing.
Cedric.
According to Maylock, the fae knight was currently away on a hunting expedition outside the city.
Beyond the commanders, a staggering force of 400 knights stood in formation.
Seeing their numbers in person was far beyond what Broken had expected.
And, as Maylock had told him before, this was only the beginning.
Recruitment was limited by the available population and the number of individuals with true knight potential.
But with Slumdon's rapid expansion, more people would eventually arrive, meaning more knights could be trained and enlisted into the army.
Before, the highest rank among Broken's knights had been Knight Commander.
But now—
That had changed.
He now had two Knight Grand Cross—
Orion and Elowen had both ascended to this elite rank.
A remarkable achievement.
"If things continue at this pace," Maylock added, "Igor, Mira, and Cedric should be able to reach Knight Grand Cross soon. We just need to push them a little further."
"On top of that—Karl and Inggrid are also close to achieving Knight Commander. Soon, they'll have their own troops to lead."
Broken gave a small nod, taking it all in.
"What do we need to accelerate their progress?"
Maylock crossed his arms.
"Exceptional skill scrolls, class upgrades, and most importantly—real battlefield experience in large-scale warfare."
Broken's expression sharpened.
"Understood."
Broken realized it had been a long time since he last checked the Reputation Shop in his Land Management system.
With the massive reputation points he had accumulated, it was time to spend them.
Immediately, he opened the shop menu and purchased every available item related to unit upgrades.
[You have used 50 Reputation Points to purchase a Skill Scroll (Basic)]
[You have used 200 Reputation Points to purchase a Skill Scroll (Advanced)]
[You have used 75 Reputation Points to purchase a Talent Scroll (Common)]
[You have used 250 Reputation Points to purchase a Talent Scroll (Rare)]
[You have ...]
After spending a significant amount of points, he had acquired several skill and talent scrolls—items that had the potential to greatly enhance his knights.
With a deep breath, he began opening them one by one.
Some were useful.
Some were... completely useless.
"Tch." Broken sighed.
It was frustrating. The system clearly had a random element, making it feel like a gamble rather than a strategic purchase.
Still, he set aside the useless talents for later and handed the valuable skills over to Maylock, who would distribute them to the knights accordingly.
Then, out of curiosity, he browsed the other available items in the shop.
And that's when he saw it.
A... rubber duck?
[Rubber Duck - A fun companion for your bath. Price: 50 Reputation Points]
Why?
WHY?
Broken stared at the screen.
Of all the advanced tools, weapons, and strategic items in this high-tech land management system—
There was a BATH TOY!?
"System... what the hell is this?" he muttered, pinching the bridge of his nose.
For all its complexity and advancement, this shop still found ways to annoy him.
[You have used 110 Reputation Points to purchase an Ancient Map Fragment.]
Out of curiosity, Broken decided to purchase an item that seemed at least somewhat promising.
He didn't expect much—
But when the map fragment materialized in his hands, he couldn't help but study it.
It was old, the paper worn and brown, marked with lines and symbols that appeared to depict a town and the surrounding forest areas.
A partial map.
Apparently, he needed all five fragments to form a complete version.
[You have used 110 Reputation Points to purchase an Ancient Map Fragment.]
[You have used ...]
Maylock, noticing what he was looking at, leaned over slightly, glancing at the opened map.
But before either of them could analyze it further, Broken simply stored it away in his inventory.
He could figure this out later.
Broken and Maylock moved to the side of the training grounds, giving the knights space to continue their training.
As a precaution, Broken put his helmet back on, ensuring that no passing civilians would recognize him if they happened to wander near.
Once they were settled, he spoke.
"So, any interesting updates?"
"Oh, this one's definitely interesting," Maylock replied, opening his map interface and sharing the display with Broken.
A specific point was highlighted—
Near the border between Dissidia Kingdom and Keseon Kingdom, right by the forest region.
Broken studied the marked location.
"What's happening there?"
Maylock's expression shifted, a faint smirk forming.
"Over the past month, forces from Valantar City have started gathering there. They've set up camp and begun military training in that area."
Broken narrowed his eyes.
"Knights from Valantar City? What are they doing so close to the border?"
Maylock let out a low chuckle.

"You already know why. Valantar Guild Alliance, led by Lucy, moved their entire guild base to Slumdon. More and more players are choosing this city as their hunting ground instead of stopping by Valantar City like before."
Broken gave a slow nod.
"So they're... annoyed by our growth?"

"Oh, very annoyed," Maylock confirmed. "Especially Constantine—the Wrath Champion—who, if you remember, was the one who orchestrated the previous attack on Slumdon using Lucy and her guild alliance as pawns."
Broken's expression darkened slightly.
"Okay?"
Maylock continued.
"I think they're intentionally setting up camp this close to provoke us—to see if we'll take the first step in confronting them."
Broken fell silent for a moment, processing the situation.
"But if they don't cross into our territory, there's no issue, right?"
Maylock shook his head.

"That's the problem—they aren't crossing into the Dissidia Kingdom. Instead, they've blocked players from moving freely between regions by establishing an unofficial settlement at the border. They're forcing adventurers to stay in their outpost, then directing them back to Valantar City instead of letting them pass through."
Broken exhaled slowly.
A power play.
They weren't directly attacking, but they were manipulating the situation, trying to cut off growth for Slumdon and Dissidia Kingdom's player base.
And now—it was a problem he had to deal with.
This situation, in theory, wasn't a major issue—yet.
If Valantar City escalated their actions beyond just setting up a border camp, it would become a direct political conflict between the two kingdoms.
This time, they weren't just using independent player forces like before.
Now, they were deploying their official knights—a move that carried real consequences.
And in a way...
What Valantar City was doing made sense from a strategic perspective.
With Slumdon Town's rapid expansion, its economic growth would inevitably weaken Valantar City's influence.
They were reacting out of self-preservation.
But there was one more critical detail—
The City Lord of Valantar City was none other than the younger brother of the current King of Keseon Kingdom.
This wasn't just a territorial dispute. It had layers of political weight behind it.
Broken thought for a moment, then turned his gaze toward Maylock.
"I have one guess as to why you're telling me all this..."
A small smirk formed on his lips.
"I know that this is something you could easily handle your way, isn't it? Assuming, of course... that you want to handle it the way... Broken would."
Maylock let out a quiet chuckle, his own smirk matching Broken's.
"Exactly. So, why don't you solve this problem... in a way that's uniquely Broken?"
